    A construct relation in which the construct agrees with the core construct on everything the core covers, and covers more.
    CONSTRAINED_FIELD
    The field-meaning concept of the pattern field this constraint governs.
    CONSTRAINED_PATTERN
    The referenced-component role a field constraint semantic's attachment target plays: the pattern that has one of its own fields constrained — one attachment role, shared by the Taxonomy Field Constraint Pattern and the Value-set Field Constraint Pattern, and distinct from the constraint mechanisms themselves.
    CONSTRAINT_ANCHOR_CONCEPT
    The concept a kind-of, descendant, leaf-descendant, or immediate-child constraint is relative to.
    CONSTRAINT_KIND
    Which Taxonomy field constraint kind this constraint semantic expresses.
    CONSTRAINT_RULE
    Why the Constraint kind value is recorded: to say which taxonomy-relative rule — kind-of, descendant, leaf-descendant, or immediate-child — applies.
    CONSTRAINT_SCOPE
    Why the Constrained field value is recorded: to say which field of the constrained pattern this rule applies to.
    CONSTRUCT_ADMISSION
    Why a keyword binding exists: to admit what it names to the logic's allowed set.
    CONSTRUCT_DENOTATION
    What a Construct Denotation Pattern semantic is: what one operator takes and what it yields, recorded as operand kind, result kind, and arity.
    CONSTRUCT_RELATION
    A relation between a construct and a core construct whose truth a check can settle, recorded so that the build runs the check.
    CONSTRUCT_RELATION_ASSERTION
    What a Construct Relation Pattern semantic is: a checked claim that the referenced construct bears the named relation to the core construct.
    CONTEXT_BIRTH_DATE_ELEMENT
    The element that carries the context's birth date, as written.
    CONTEXT_CLASS
    That class as a concept, resolved by IKE.
    CONTEXT_KEY_ELEMENT
    The element that keys the context, as written.
    CONTEXT_NAME
    The context's name as written: Patient, Encounter, Practitioner.
    CONTEXT_TYPE
    The class that is the context, as written.
    CONVERSATION_JOURNAL
    A conversation held as a structured document: each conversation is anchored by an instance of this concept, its turns' lines are prose elements in manifest order, and its turns and their blocks are document elements.
    CONVERSATION_JOURNAL_MODULE
    The module every conversation journal's lines, elements and manifest stamp in, so conversations can be carried or omitted as a unit.
    CONVERSATION_TURN
    One turn of a conversation, by a person or by the Komet assistant; its members are its blocks.
    CONVERSION_FROM_TYPE
    The type a conversion converts from, as written.
    CONVERSION_FUNCTION
    The function the file names for the conversion, as written.
    CONVERSION_POSSIBLE
    Whether a conversion has a value: of a value to a kind, or of a measure to a unit.
    CONVERSION_TARGET_CLASS
    The type converted to, as a concept, resolved by IKE.
    CONVERSION_TO_TYPE
    The type a conversion converts to, as written.
    CORE_CONSTRUCT
    The construct a relation assertion relates the extending construct to: a construct of the EL++ core.
    CORRELATION_CONSTRAINT
    A criterion that tests a statement against a set of other statements of the same subject: does any statement in that set relate to this one in a given way, for example a condition whose onset was within the period of this encounter.
    CORRELATION_EXPRESSION
    Correlation expression (SOLOR)
    CORRELATION_PROPERTIES
    Correlation properties (SOLOR)
    CORRELATION_REFERENCE_EXPRESSION
    Correlation reference expression (SOLOR)
    CQL_DIALECT
    The dialect of English in which a construct CQL names reads as CQL's keyword, spelled as CQL spells it.
    CREATIVE_COMMONS_BY_LICENSE
    Creative Commons BY license (SOLOR)
    CRITERION
    A test applied to one statement.
    CZECH_DIALECT
    Czech dialect (SOLOR)
    CZECH_LANGUAGE
    Czech language (SOLOR)
    DANISH_LANGUAGE
    Danish language (SOLOR)
    DATA_CONCEPT
    Groups concepts that represent data values and defaults — the data-carrying side of the model, as distinct from IKE base model concept's structural, self-descriptive side.
    DATA_MODEL
    A data model as the CQL translator describes it in model information: the classes a library can retrieve and walk, each with its elements and their types, the contexts a library can run in, and the conversions to other models.
    DATA_PROPERTY_SET
    Data property set
    DATA_PROPERTY_SET_AXIOMS
    Data Property Set Axioms
    DATA_TYPE_DEFAULT_EXEMPLAR
    Why every Data Type Defaults Pattern field value is recorded: to carry its data type's loud default — a value that works as an initial value but reads as obviously needing revision, never Java's silent zero-value.
    DATA_TYPE_DEFAULT_PROVISION
    Why a Data Type Defaults Pattern semantic exists: to provide, in one semantic, a loud default value for every data type a pattern field can declare — and, replayed, to exercise every field serialization path the store supports end to end.
    DAY
    A unit of the Gregorian calendar, midnight to midnight in a time zone, twenty-four hours except where a clock change makes it twenty-three or twenty-five.
    DECIMAL
    Decimal (SOLOR)
    DECIMAL_DATA_TYPE
    Decimal data type
    DECIMAL_DEFAULT
    The Decimal field's loud default: the stretched-sevens sentinel 777777777.777 — nine sevens, a decimal point, three more sevens.
    DECLARATION_KEYWORD
    A lexical role: in a CQL library a value set, a code, or a concept is declared once by name and used many times, and the keyword that declares it introduces a thing rather than an operation.
    DEEP_PART_LISTING
    The parts of a value and the parts of its parts, all the way down, as one list.
    DEFAULT_DATA_CONCEPT
    Default Data Concept
    DEFAULT_MODULE_FOR_EDIT_COORDINATE
    Default module for edit coordinate (SOLOR)
    DEFAULT_VALUE_CONCEPT
    The attachment point for default values: a default value semantic of a pattern is a complete semantic of that pattern whose referenced component is this concept and whose fields carry the default values an editor offers for that pattern's fields.
    DEFAULTED_DATA_TYPES
    What a Data Type Defaults Pattern semantic means: the sixteen data types ConceptToDataType recognizes for pattern fields, each exemplified by one field carrying that type's loud default.
    DEFAULTS_AND_TEMPLATES_MODEL
    The model family for the defaults, templates, and constraints capabilities: the attachment points a pattern's default and template semantics reference, the per-data-type default field concepts, and the field-constraint apparatus (taxonomy and value-set constraints, value restrictions, match rules).
    DEFAULTS_AND_TEMPLATES_MODULE
    The module scoping every default value and template semantic.
    DEFINITION_DESCRIPTION_TYPE
    Definition description type
    DEFINITION_REFERENCE
    The use of a definition's value by its name; evaluating it is evaluating the definition, once, for the subject at hand.
    DEFINITION_ROOT
    Definition root (SOLOR)
    DEFINITIONAL_EXTENSION
    A construct relation in which the construct can be defined using only what the core construct already says: new names, no new logic.
    DESCENDANT_FIELD_CONSTRAINT
    Legal values are every descendant of the anchor concept, not including the anchor concept itself.
    DESCENDANT_OF
    A taxonomy operator that yields, for an anchor concept, every concept below it in the is-a hierarchy under the view, not including itself.
    DESCENDANT_OR_SELF_OF
    A taxonomy operator that yields, for an anchor concept, every concept below it in the is-a hierarchy under the view, itself included.
    DESCRIPTION
    Description
    DESCRIPTION_ACCEPTABILITY
    Description acceptability
    DESCRIPTION_ATTACHMENT
    Why a Description Pattern semantic exists: to attach a human-readable name or definition to a concept.
    DESCRIPTION_CASE_SENSITIVE
    Description case sensitive
    DESCRIPTION_CASE_SIGNIFICANCE
    Description case significance
    DESCRIPTION_CORE_TYPE
    Description core type (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_DIALECT_PAIR
    Description dialect pair (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_FOCUS
    Description focus (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_FOR_DIALECT_DESCRIPTION_PAIR
    Description for dialect/description pair (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_INITIAL_CHARACTER_CASE_SENSITIVE
    Description initial character case sensitive (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_LIST_FOR_CONCEPT
    Description list for concept (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_LOGIC_PROFILE
    Description-logic profile (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_LOGIC_PROFILE_FOR_LOGIC_COORDINATE
    Description logic profile for logic coordinate (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_NOT_CASE_SENSITIVE
    Description not case sensitive
    DESCRIPTION_ROLE
    Why a description's type value is recorded: to say which of the three description roles — fully qualified name, regular name, or definition — this description plays.
    DESCRIPTION_SEMANTIC
    Description semantic
    DESCRIPTION_TYPE
    Description type
    DESCRIPTION_TYPE_FOR_DESCRIPTION
    Description type for description (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_TYPE_PREFERENCE_LIST_FOR_LANGUAGE_COORDINATE
    Description type preference list for language coordinate (SOLOR)
    DESCRIPTION_VERSION_PROPERTIES
    Description version properties (SOLOR)
    DESTINATION_MODULE_FOR_EDIT_COORDINATE
    Destination module for edit coordinate (SOLOR)
    DEVELOPMENT_MODULE
    Development module (SOLOR)
    DEVELOPMENT_PATH
    Development path
    DIALECT
    Dialect
    DIALECT_FOR_DIALECT_DESCRIPTION_PAIR
    Dialect for dialect/description pair (SOLOR)
    DIALECT_PATTERN_PREFERENCE_LIST_FOR_LANGUAGE_COORDINATE
    Dialect pattern preference list for language coordinate
    DIGRAPH_DATA_TYPE
    DiGraph data type
    DIGRAPH_DEFAULT
    The DiGraph field's loud default: a simple cycle — two vertices, both Uninitialized Component, with edges in both directions.
    DIGRAPH_FOR_LOGIC_COORDINATE
    Digraph for logic coordinate (SOLOR)
    DIMENSIONLESS_NUMBER
    A measure semantic for a number that carries no unit: a count of encounters, the 2 in twice, a plain figure.
    DIRECTED_GRAPH
    Directed graph
    DIRECTED_TREE
    A rooted tree whose every edge is directed away from (or toward) the root: a kind of Directed graph and a kind of Tree at once — the multi-parent placement that makes a classified taxonomy a DAG rather than a tree.
    DISJOINT_WITH
    Disjoint with (SOLOR)
    DISPLAY_FIELDS
    Display Fields
    DISPLAY_SEQUENCE
    Why a roster order value is recorded: to say where this entry falls in the roster's own display order.
    DISPOSITION_READING
    A statement reading: what became of the act or the order, a concept.
    DITREE_DATA_TYPE
    DiTree data type
    DITREE_DEFAULT
    The DiTree field's loud default: a single-vertex tree whose vertex meaning is Uninitialized Component — the smallest well-formed tree, carrying the loud placeholder at its root.
    DOCUMENT_BLOCK
    A block-level element grouping lines: the paragraphs, listings, quotations, lists, tables and images a section or a turn contains.
    DOCUMENT_ELEMENT
    Anything that groups a structured document's lines: a section, a block, a row, a cell, a list item, a conversation turn.
    DOCUMENT_ELEMENT_KIND
    Which element a block semantic is: a concept under Document element.
    DOCUMENT_ELEMENT_LEVEL
    A section's heading level, or a list's nesting depth.
    DOCUMENT_ELEMENT_MEMBERS
    The lines and elements an element contains, in order.
    DOCUMENT_ELEMENT_PARAMETERS
    The element's parameters as written, such as an AsciiDoc attribute line or a Markdown fence's info string, kept verbatim so the document reads back unchanged; a reader parses what it needs.
    DOCUMENT_ELEMENT_TITLE
    A section's heading text, a block's title, a description list item's term.
    DOCUMENT_FIELD
    A field of the document block pattern.
    DOCUMENT_IMAGE
    An image; the target and the alternative text are in its parameters.
    DOCUMENT_LIST
    An unordered, ordered or description list; the kind is in its parameters, its items its members.
    DOCUMENT_LIST_ITEM
    One item of a list, with its continuation blocks as members; a description list item's term is its title.
    DOCUMENT_LISTING
    A delimited block of text kept as written, such as an AsciiDoc ---- listing or a Markdown fenced block; its language or other tag is in its parameters.
    DOCUMENT_OPAQUE_BLOCK
    A block the parse recognises but does not model, kept verbatim so the document reads back unchanged.
    DOCUMENT_PARAGRAPH
    A run of prose lines up to a blank line; under semantic line breaks each line is one claim, so the paragraph groups claims and the line keeps the provenance.
    DOCUMENT_QUOTATION
    A quotation block, with its attribution in its parameters when it has one.
    DOCUMENT_SECTION
    A section: a heading of some level and the elements beneath it until the next heading of that level or shallower.
    DOCUMENT_STRUCTURE
    Carrying a structured document's structure: the purpose of the document block and document attributes patterns and their fields.
    DOCUMENT_STRUCTURE_MODEL
    The structure a document and a conversation journal have in common: lines held as prose elements in the order a manifest gives them, and the elements that group them, so either is held line for line with its provenance and given back unchanged.
    DOCUMENT_TABLE
    A table; its column specification and options are its parameters, its rows its members.
    DOCUMENT_TABLE_CELL
    One cell of a table row; its lines are its members.
    DOCUMENT_TABLE_ROW
    One row of a table; its cells are its members.
    DOUBLE
    Double (SOLOR)
    DOUBLE_DISPLAY_FIELD
    Double display field (SOLOR)
    DUTCH_LANGUAGE
    Dutch language (SOLOR)
    DYNAMIC_COLUMN_DATA_TYPES
    Dynamic column data types (SOLOR)
    DYNAMIC_REFERENCED_COMPONENT_RESTRICTION
    Dynamic referenced component restriction (SOLOR)
    ECL_DIALECT
    The dialect of English in which a construct ECL names reads as ECL's token, spelled as ECL spells it.
    EDIT_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES
    The dimensions of the edit coordinate — where a view writes: the author, the default and destination modules, the module and path options offered, and the promotion path that together govern how new versions are stamped.
    EDIT_DOCUMENT_BLOCK
    Replaces the text of one block of a document materialized from git, a block whose members are lines: an unchanged line keeps its element, a changed line gets a new version of it, a new line gets a provisional element until a commit gives it an identity, and a removed line leaves the block.
    EDITORIAL_CLARIFICATION
    Why a free-text comment is captured: to explain an authoring decision or provide context a formal field cannot, for a future reviewer or maintainer.
    EL
    An expression language: the description-logic profile this set's stated and inferred axioms are written in, with class intersection, existential restriction, necessary and sufficient sets, and disjointness.
    EL_AND
    EL++ AND (SOLOR)
    EL_DIALECT
    The dialect of English in which the EL++ conjunction reads as AND.
    EL_DIGRAPH
    EL++ digraph (SOLOR)
    EL_DITREE
    The directed tree carrying one concept's EL++ axiom expression — the stored form of a single stated or inferred definition, with sets and atoms as vertices under one definition root.
    EL_INFERRED_CONCEPT_DEFINITION
    El++ Inferred Concept Definition (SOLOR)
    EL_INFERRED_TERMINOLOGICAL_AXIOMS
    EL++ Inferred terminological axioms
    EL_LOGIC_PROFILE
    EL++ logic profile (SOLOR)
    EL_PROFILE_SET_OPERATOR
    El profile set operator (SOLOR)
    EL_STATED_CONCEPT_DEFINITION
    EL++ Stated Concept Definition (SOLOR)
    EL_STATED_TERMINOLOGICAL_AXIOMS
    EL++ Stated terminological axioms
    EL_TERMINOLOGICAL_AXIOMS
    EL++ terminological axioms
    ELEMENT_BINDING_NAME
    The name of the value set binding the file gives the element, as written.
    ELEMENT_BINDING_STRENGTH
    The binding's strength, as written: required, extensible, preferred, example.
    ELEMENT_BINDING_VALUE_SET
    The value set the binding names, as written.
    ELEMENT_CLASS
    The class the type names, as a concept, resolved by IKE when the type names exactly one.
    ELEMENT_COMMENT
    The comment the file gives the element, as written.
    ELEMENT_CONTENT
    Carrying an element's content: the purpose shared by the element patterns and their fields.
    ELEMENT_DEFINITION
    The definition the file gives the element, as written.
    ELEMENT_DESCRIPTION
    The short description the file gives the element, as written.
    ELEMENT_LABEL
    The label the file gives the element, as written.
    ELEMENT_MAXIMUM
    The most values the file allows, as written.
    ELEMENT_MINIMUM
    The least number of values the file allows, as written.
    ELEMENT_MUST_SUPPORT
    Whether the file marks the element as one an implementation must support.
    ELEMENT_NAME
    The element's name as written.
    ELEMENT_ONE_BASED
    Whether the file marks a list element as counted from one.
    ELEMENT_ORDER
    Ordering a structured document's lines: the purpose of the journal manifest and its field.
    ELEMENT_POSITION
    The first position of an element in a list, or minus one when absent.
    ELEMENT_PROHIBITED
    Whether the file prohibits the element.
    ELEMENT_READING
    The statement reading a model's element answers.
    ELEMENT_TARGET
    The element of another model this element stands on, as written.
    ELEMENT_TYPE
    The element's type as written, one class, a list, an interval, or a choice.
    ELEMENT_TYPE_SPECIFIER
    The element's type as a tree of the catalog's type specifiers, named, list, interval, and choice, each named type resolved to its class, built by IKE.
    ELM_ABS
    From the ELM specification: The Abs operator returns the absolute value of its argument.
    ELM_ACCESSLEVEL_POSITION
    The argument position named accessLevel, an attribute, on 6 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_ACCESSMODIFIER
    From the ELM specification: The AccessModifier type is used to specify the access level for the various definitions within a library such as parameters, expressions, and functions.
    ELM_ACCESSMODIFIER_PRIVATE
    The AccessModifier value Private of the ELM specification.
    ELM_ACCESSMODIFIER_PUBLIC
    The AccessModifier value Public of the ELM specification.
    ELM_ADD
    From the ELM specification: The Add operator performs numeric addition of its arguments.
    ELM_AFTER
    From the ELM specification: The After operator is defined for Intervals, as well as Date, DateTime, and Time values.
    ELM_AGGREGATE
    From the ELM specification: The Aggregate operator performs custom aggregation by evaluating an expression for each element of the source.
    ELM_AGGREGATE_POSITION
    The argument position named aggregate, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_AGGREGATECLAUSE
    From the ELM specification: The AggregateClause element defines the result of the query in terms of an aggregation expression performed for each item in the query.
    ELM_AGGREGATEEXPRESSION
    From the ELM specification: Aggregate expressions perform operations on lists of data, either directly on a list of scalars, or indirectly on a list of objects, with a reference to a property present on each object in the list.
    ELM_ALIAS_POSITION
    The argument position named alias, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_ALIASEDQUERYSOURCE
    From the ELM specification: The AliasedQuerySource element defines a single source for inclusion in a query scope.
    ELM_ALIASREF
    From the ELM specification: The AliasRef expression allows for the reference of a specific source within the scope of a query.
    ELM_ALLTRUE
    From the ELM specification: The AllTrue operator returns true if all the non-null elements in source are true.
    ELM_AND
    From the ELM specification: The And operator returns the logical conjunction of its arguments.
    ELM_ANNOTATION_POSITION
    The argument position named annotation, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_ANYINCODESYSTEM
    From the ELM specification: The AnyInCodeSystem operator returns true if any of the given codes are in the given code system.
    ELM_ANYINVALUESET
    From the ELM specification: The AnyInValueSet operator returns true if any of the given codes are in the given value set.
    ELM_ANYTRUE
    From the ELM specification: The AnyTrue operator returns true if any non-null element in source is true.
    ELM_AS
    From the ELM specification: The As operator allows the result of an expression to be cast as a given target type.
    ELM_ASTYPE_POSITION
    The argument position named asType, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_ASTYPESPECIFIER_POSITION
    The argument position named asTypeSpecifier, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_AVG
    From the ELM specification: The Avg operator returns the average of the non-null elements in source.
    ELM_BEFORE
    From the ELM specification: The Before operator is defined for Intervals, as well as Date, DateTime, and Time values.
    ELM_BINARYEXPRESSION
    From the ELM specification: The BinaryExpression type defines the abstract base type for expressions that take two arguments.
    ELM_BY_POSITION
    The argument position named by, a child element, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_BYCOLUMN
    From the ELM specification: The ByColumn element specifies that the sort should be performed using the given column and direction.
    ELM_BYDIRECTION
    From the ELM specification: The ByDirection element specifies that the sort should be performed using the given direction.
    ELM_BYEXPRESSION
    From the ELM specification: The ByExpression element specifies that the sort should be performed using the given expression and direction.
    ELM_CALCULATEAGE
    From the ELM specification: Calculates the age in the specified precision of a person born on the given date.
    ELM_CALCULATEAGEAT
    From the ELM specification: Calculates the age in the specified precision of a person born on a given date, as of another given date.
    ELM_CANCONVERT
    From the ELM specification: The CanConvert operator returns true if the given value can be converted to a specific type, and false otherwise.
    ELM_CANCONVERTQUANTITY
    From the ELM specification: The CanConvertQuantity operator returns true if the Quantity can be converted to an equivalent Quantity with the given Unit.
    ELM_CASE
    From the ELM specification: The Case operator allows for multiple conditional expressions to be chained together in a single expression, rather than having to nest multiple If operators.
    ELM_CASEITEM
    A type of the ELM specification; the schema gives no description.
    ELM_CASEITEM_POSITION
    The argument position named caseItem, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CATALOG_STRUCTURE
    Why type positions are recorded: so that a tree can be checked against the catalog and a reader can know what each node may hold.
    ELM_CEILING
    From the ELM specification: The Ceiling operator returns the first integer greater than or equal to the argument.
    ELM_CHILDREN
    From the ELM specification: For structured types, the Children operator returns a list of all the values of the elements of the type.
    ELM_CHOICE_POSITION
    The argument position named choice, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CHOICETYPESPECIFIER
    From the ELM specification: ChoiceTypeSpecifier defines the possible types of a choice type.
    ELM_CLASSTYPE_POSITION
    The argument position named classType, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_COALESCE
    From the ELM specification: The Coalesce operator returns the first non-null result in a list of arguments.
    ELM_CODE
    From the ELM specification: The Code type represents a literal code selector.
    ELM_CODE_POSITION
    The argument position named code, an element on some types and an attribute on others, on 7 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_CODECOMPARATOR_POSITION
    The argument position named codeComparator, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CODEDEF
    From the ELM specification: The CodeDef type defines a code identifier that can then be used to reference single codes anywhere within an expression.
    ELM_CODEFILTER_POSITION
    The argument position named codeFilter, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CODEFILTERELEMENT
    From the ELM specification: The CodeFilterElement type specifies a terminology filter criteria for use within a retrieve, specified as either [property] [comparator] [value] or [search] [comparator] [value].
    ELM_CODEPROPERTY_POSITION
    The argument position named codeProperty, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CODEREF
    From the ELM specification: The CodeRef expression allows a previously defined code to be referenced within an expression.
    ELM_CODES_POSITION
    The argument position named codes, a child element, on 5 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_CODESEARCH_POSITION
    The argument position named codeSearch, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CODESYSTEM_POSITION_LOWER_CASE
    The argument position named codesystem, a child element, on 3 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_CODESYSTEM_POSITION_MIXED_CASE
    The argument position named codeSystem, a child element, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_CODESYSTEMDEF
    From the ELM specification: The CodeSystemDef type defines a code system identifier that can then be used to identify code systems involved in value set definitions.
    ELM_CODESYSTEMEXPRESSION_POSITION
    The argument position named codesystemExpression, a child element, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_CODESYSTEMREF
    From the ELM specification: The CodeSystemRef expression allows a previously defined named code system to be referenced within an expression.
    ELM_CODESYSTEMS_POSITION
    The argument position named codeSystems, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_COLLAPSE
    From the ELM specification: The Collapse operator returns the unique set of intervals that completely covers the ranges present in the given list of intervals.
    ELM_COMBINE
    From the ELM specification: The Combine operator combines a list of strings, optionally separating each string with the given separator.
    ELM_COMPARAND_POSITION
    The argument position named comparand, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_COMPARATOR_POSITION
    The argument position named comparator, an attribute, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_CONCATENATE
    From the ELM specification: The Concatenate operator performs string concatenation of its arguments.
    ELM_CONCEPT
    From the ELM specification: The Concept type represents a literal concept selector.
    ELM_CONCEPTDEF
    From the ELM specification: The ConceptDef type defines a concept identifier that can then be used to reference single concepts anywhere within an expression.
    ELM_CONCEPTREF
    From the ELM specification: The ConceptRef expression allows a previously defined concept to be referenced within an expression.
    ELM_CONCEPTS_POSITION
    The argument position named concepts, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CONDITION_POSITION
    The argument position named condition, a child element, on 3 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_CONTAINS
    From the ELM specification: The Contains operator returns true if the first operand contains the second.
    ELM_CONTEXT_POSITION
    The argument position named context, an element on some types and an attribute on others, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_CONTEXTDEF
    From the ELM specification: The ContextDef type defines a context definition statement.
    ELM_CONTEXTPROPERTY_POSITION
    The argument position named contextProperty, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CONTEXTS_POSITION
    The argument position named contexts, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CONTEXTSEARCH_POSITION
    The argument position named contextSearch, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_CONVERT
    From the ELM specification: The Convert operator converts a value to a specific type.
    ELM_CONVERTQUANTITY
    From the ELM specification: The ConvertQuantity operator converts a Quantity to an equivalent Quantity with the given unit.
    ELM_CONVERTSTOBOOLEAN
    From the ELM specification: The ConvertsToBoolean operator returns true if the value of its argument is or can be converted to a Boolean value.
    ELM_CONVERTSTODATE
    From the ELM specification: The ConvertsToDate operator returns true if the value of its argument is or can be converted to a Date value.
    ELM_CONVERTSTODATETIME
    From the ELM specification: The ConvertsToDateTime operator returns true if the value of its argument is or can be converted to a DateTime value.
    ELM_CONVERTSTODECIMAL
    From the ELM specification: The ConvertsToDecimal operator returns true if the value of its argument is or can be converted to a Decimal value.
    ELM_CONVERTSTOINTEGER
    From the ELM specification: The ConvertsToInteger operator returns true if the value of its argument is or can be converted to an Integer value.
    ELM_CONVERTSTOLONG
    From the ELM specification: The ConvertsToLong operator returns true if the value of its argument is or can be converted to a Long value.
    ELM_CONVERTSTOQUANTITY
    From the ELM specification: The ConvertsToQuantity operator returns true if the value of its argument is or can be converted to a Quantity value.
    ELM_CONVERTSTORATIO
    From the ELM specification: The ConvertsToRatio operator returns true if the value of its argument is or can be converted to a Ratio value.

    From the ELM specification: The ProperContains operator returns true if the first operand properly contains the second.
    ELM_PROPERIN
    From the ELM specification: The ProperIn operator tests for proper membership in an interval or list.
    ELM_PROPERINCLUDEDIN
    From the ELM specification: The ProperIncludedIn operator returns true if the first operand is included in the second, and is strictly smaller.
    ELM_PROPERINCLUDES
    From the ELM specification: The ProperIncludes operator returns true if the first operand includes the second, and is strictly larger.
    ELM_PROPERTY
    From the ELM specification: The Property operator returns the value of the property on the source (or named scope) specified by the path attribute.
    ELM_PROPERTY_FORM
    The form of a position that holds a plain value, an attribute in the schema: our vertex holds it as a property keyed by the position.
    ELM_PROPERTY_POSITION
    The argument position named property, an attribute, on 3 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_QUANTITY
    From the ELM specification: The Quantity type defines a clinical quantity.
    ELM_QUERY
    From the ELM specification: The Query operator represents a clause-based query.
    ELM_QUERYLETREF
    From the ELM specification: The QueryLetRef expression allows for the reference of a specific let definition within the scope of a query.
    ELM_RATIO
    From the ELM specification: The Ratio type defines a ratio between two quantities.
    ELM_REFERENCE
    A thing a definition names: another define, a value set, a code, a code system, a concept, a parameter, a function, or an included library.
    ELM_REFERENCE_KIND
    The kind of thing a definition names, as one of the catalog's reference node kinds, such as ELM ValueSetRef or ELM ExpressionRef.
    ELM_REFERENCED_DEFINITION
    The definition a name means, as a direct link to that definition's semantic.
    ELM_RELATEDDATATYPE_POSITION
    The argument position named relatedDataType, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_RELATEDPROPERTY_POSITION
    The argument position named relatedProperty, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_RELATEDSEARCH_POSITION

    ELM_RELATIONSHIP_POSITION

    ELM_RELATIONSHIPCLAUSE

    ELM_REPEAT
    From the ELM specification: The Repeat expression performs successive ForEach until no new elements are returned.
    ELM_REPLACEMATCHES

    ELM_RESULTTYPESPECIFIER_POSITION

    ELM_RETURNCLAUSE

    From the ELM specification: The Round operator returns the nearest integer to its argument.

    ELM_SAMEORAFTER
    From the ELM specification: The SameOrAfter operator is defined for Date, DateTime, and Time values, as well as intervals.
    ELM_SAMEORBEFORE

    ELM_SIGNATURE_POSITION

    ELM_SLICE

    ELM_SORTDIRECTION_DESC
    The SortDirection value desc of the ELM specification.
    ELM_SORTDIRECTION_DESCENDING
    The SortDirection value descending of the ELM specification.

    ELM_STARTING_POSITION

    From the ELM specification: The Starts operator returns true if the first interval starts the second.
    ELM_STARTSWITH
    From the ELM specification: The StartsWith operator returns true if the given string starts with the given prefix.

    The argument position named statements, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_STDDEV

    ELM_STRICT_POSITION
    The argument position named strict, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_STRING_POSITION

    ELM_SUBSUMEDBY
    From the ELM specification: The SubsumedBy operator returns true if the given codes are equivalent, or if the first code is subsumed by the second code (i.e. the first code is a descendent of the second code in a subsumption hierarchy), and false otherwise.
    ELM_SUBSUMES
    From the ELM specification: The Subsumes operator returns true if the given codes are equivalent, or if the first code subsumes the second (i.e. the first code is an ancestor of the second in a subsumption hierarchy), and false otherwise.

    From the ELM specification: The Subtract operator performs numeric subtraction of its arguments.
    ELM_SUCCESSOR
    From the ELM specification: The Successor operator returns the successor of the argument.
    ELM_SUCHTHAT_POSITION

    A tree whose vertices are ELM nodes: the one field of the ELM tree pattern.

    From the ELM specification: The Truncate operator returns the integer component of its argument.
    ELM_TRUNCATEDDIVIDE
    From the ELM specification: The TruncatedDivide operator performs integer division of its arguments.
    ELM_TUPLE
    From the ELM specification: The Tuple expression allows tuples of any type to be built up as an expression.
    ELM_TUPLEELEMENT
    From the ELM specification: The TupleElement is used within a Tuple expression to provide the value of a specific element within a tuple literal expression.
    ELM_TUPLEELEMENTDEFINITION
    From the ELM specification: TupleElementDefinition defines the name and type of a single element within a TupleTypeSpecifier.
    ELM_TUPLETYPESPECIFIER
    From the ELM specification: TupleTypeSpecifier defines the possible elements of a tuple.
    ELM_TYPE_POSITION
    What a type position semantic is: one position of one node kind, with the type of value it holds, the fewest and the most values the schema allows, the schema's own note on that position for that kind, and its form: whether our vertex holds it as a property or as an edge.
    ELM_TYPESPECIFIER
    From the ELM specification: TypeSpecifier is the abstract base type for all type specifiers.
    ELM_TYPESPECIFIER_POSITION
    The argument position named typeSpecifier, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.

    ELM_UNION
    From the ELM specification: The Union operator returns the union of its arguments.
    ELM_UNIT_POSITION
    The argument position named unit, an element on some types and an attribute on others, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_UPPER
    From the ELM specification: The Upper operator returns the given string with all characters converted to their upper case equivalents.
    ELM_URI_POSITION
    The argument position named uri, an attribute, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_USINGDEF
    From the ELM specification: Defines a data model that is available within the artifact.
    ELM_USINGS_POSITION
    The argument position named usings, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_VALUE_POSITION
    The argument position named value, an element on some types and an attribute on others, on 16 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_VALUE_TYPE_FIELD
    The type of value that position holds on that type: a node kind of the catalog, a schema primitive, or a type of another schema.
    ELM_VALUESET_POSITION
    The argument position named valueset, a child element, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.

    From the ELM specification: The ValueSetDef type defines a value set identifier that can be referenced by name anywhere within an expression.
    ELM_VALUESETEXPRESSION_POSITION
    The argument position named valuesetExpression, a child element, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_VALUESETPROPERTY_POSITION
    The argument position named valueSetProperty, an attribute, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_VALUESETREF
    From the ELM specification: The ValueSetRef expression allows a previously defined named value set to be referenced within an expression.
    ELM_VALUESETS_POSITION
    The argument position named valueSets, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_VALUETYPE_POSITION
    The argument position named valueType, an attribute, on 4 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_VARIANCE
    From the ELM specification: The Variance operator returns the statistical variance of the elements in source.
    ELM_VERSION_POSITION
    The argument position named version, an element on some types and an attribute on others, on 7 node kinds of the catalog.
    ELM_VERSIONEDIDENTIFIER
    From the ELM specification: VersionedIdentifier is composed of three parts: (1) an optional system, or namespace, which provides a globally unique, stable scope for the identifier, (2) an identifier which identifies the set of all versions of a given resource, and (3) the actual version of the instance of interest in this set.
    ELM_WHEN_POSITION
    The argument position named when, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_WHERE_POSITION
    The argument position named where, a child element, on 1 node kind of the catalog.
    ELM_WIDTH
    From the ELM specification: The Width operator returns the width of an interval.
    ELM_WITH
    From the ELM specification: The With clause restricts the elements of a given source to only those elements that have elements in the related source that satisfy the suchThat condition.
    ELM_WITHOUT
    From the ELM specification: The Without clause restricts the elements of a given source to only those elements that do not have elements in the related source that satisfy the suchThat condition.
    ELM_XOR
    From the ELM specification: The Xor operator returns the exclusive or of its arguments.
    ELM_YEAR_POSITION
    The argument position named year, a child element, on 2 node kinds of the catalog.
    ENGLISH_DIALECT
    English Dialect
    ENGLISH_LANGUAGE
    English Language
    EQUAL_MATCH_RELATION
    A value matches a member when they are equal by the member datatype's natural equality: entity references by identity, scalars by value, byte arrays by content, and Decimal by numeric equality (compareTo == 0 — an identical-representation rule would be its own relation).
    EQUAL_TO
    Equal to (SOLOR)
    EVALUATION_MESSAGE
    A note attached to a value's evaluation, the value passed through; a message of error severity whose condition holds refuses the evaluation with its text.
    EVALUATION_MOMENT
    The moment an evaluation runs at, fixed once per run: read as a date, as an instant, or as a time of day.
    EVENT_DURATION_MEASURE
    A repetition measure: how long each individual action should last, on a time-unit measure semantic, such as fifteen to twenty minutes.
    EVENT_FREQUENCY_MEASURE
    A repetition measure: how often the action should occur, on a frequency measure semantic, such as three times a day.
    EVENT_SEPARATION_MEASURE
    A repetition measure: the interval between one action and the next, on a time-unit measure semantic, such as every six hours.
    EXACT
    Exact (SOLOR)
    EXAMPLE_UCUM_UNITS
    Example UCUM Units (SOLOR)
    EXISTENCE
    An operator that takes a set of statements and a criterion and returns one presence value for the set as a whole: Present if the criterion's result is Present for any statement in the set, Absent if it is Absent for every statement, and Indeterminate otherwise.
    EXISTENTIAL_RESTRICTION
    Existential restriction
    EXPRESS_AXIOM_SYNTAX
    Express axiom syntax (SOLOR)
    EXPRESSION_LANGUAGE
    A logic whose expressions are evaluated over this set's content or over ANF statements.
    EXPRESSION_LANGUAGE_MODEL
    The concepts and patterns that represent the operators a query language over ANF needs, and relate each one explicitly to the logics it overlaps: the logics and their dialects; the keyword bindings that admit a construct to a logic; the denotations that say what a construct takes and what it yields; and the checked relations between a construct and a core construct, which are logical equivalence, definitional extension, and conservative extension.
    EXTENDED_DESCRIPTION_TYPE
    Extended description type (SOLOR)
    EXTENDED_RELATIONSHIP_TYPE
    Extended relationship type (SOLOR)
    EXTENT_MERGING
    The fewest extents that cover the same points as a list of extents, those that overlap or meet merged, ordered by their starts.
    EXTENT_PARTITION
    The unit extents of a step that cover an extent, or their starts as points; nothing for an extent written coarser than the step.
    EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_MAPPING
    Why an Identifier Pattern semantic exists: to record an alternate identifier a component carries in an external terminology's own identifier scheme.
    FEATURE
    Feature (SOLOR)
    FEATURE_ROLE_TYPE
    Feature Role Type
    FEATURE_TYPE
    Feature Type (SOLOR)
    FHIR_DIALECT
    The dialect in which a class's name and label are read as the FHIR model information writes them, so that a class is found by either, the way a unit is found by its name and its symbol.
    FIELD_CATEGORIES
    Groups the field-level meta-schema concepts: the terminology describing what kind of value — a component, a field definition, a semantic field, or a set of these — a semantic's field can hold.
    FIELD_DEFINITION_DATA_TYPE_FIELD
    Field definition data type field
    FIELD_DEFINITION_FIELD
    The field kind naming a pattern version's field-definition slot: each value is one field definition — the meaning, purpose, and data type the pattern declares for one of its fields.
    FIELD_DEFINITION_MEANING_FIELD
    Field definition meaning field
    FIELD_DEFINITION_PURPOSE_FIELD
    Field definition purpose field
    FIELD_DEFINITIONS_SET
    Why a pattern version's field-definition field is recorded: to hold the pattern's complete, ordered field definitions — the declared shape every semantic of the pattern must fit.
    FIELD_SUBSTITUTION
    Field substitution (SOLOR)
    FIELD_VALUE_FIELD
    Field value field
    FIELD_VALUE_RESTRICTION
    Why a field constraint semantic exists: to restrict which values are legal for one of the constrained pattern's own fields.
    FIRST_PRESENT
    The first of its operands that is not a missing value, or a missing value when every operand is.
    FIXED_VALUE
    Why a literal denotation exists: a literal is a value, not an operator, so what is recorded is its bounds rather than what it takes and yields.
    FLOAT
    Float (SOLOR)
    FLOAT_DATA_TYPE
    Float data type
    FLOAT_DEFAULT
    The Float field's loud default: NaN, the type's native non-value — chosen over a stretched-sevens sentinel because a true non-value is louder still: it cannot be mistaken for data at all, and it propagates through arithmetic, so any computation over an unrevised default stays loudly not-a-number.
    FLOAT_LITERAL
    Float literal (SOLOR)
    FLOAT_SUBSTITUTION
    Float substitution (SOLOR)
    FRENCH_DIALECT
    French dialect (SOLOR)
    FRENCH_LANGUAGE
    French Language (SOLOR)

    Fully qualified name description type

    A lexical role: the name of a function a logic calls with its arguments in parentheses, as CQL calls Count, Sum, Min, Max, Avg, and Median, rather than a keyword written before or between its operands.
    GENERIC_AND
    A connective operator that joins two or more operands of one kind into a result of that same kind.
    GENERIC_OR
    Generic OR (SOLOR)
    GERMAN_LANGUAGE
    German Language (SOLOR)
    GIT_AUTHOR
    The home of author concepts derived from git identities: one per person, keyed by canonical email after mailmap consolidation.
    GIT_MODULE
    The home of module concepts derived from repositories or Kompendium components: content materialized from a repository stamps in its module.
    GIT_PATH
    The home of path concepts derived from branches: content materialized from a branch stamps on its path.
    GIT_PROVENANCE
    Carrying git provenance: the purpose of the git source pattern and its fields.
    GIT_PROVENANCE_MODEL
    The apparatus that stamps content materialized from a git repository with the repository's own provenance: the homes of the author, module and path concepts an identity adapter derives per repository, and the git source that names the commit a version came from.
    GIT_SOURCE
    Where a document version came from: the repository-relative path and the commit, one version per commit that changed the file — the bridge from a graph back to git.
    GRAMMATICAL_PLACEMENT
    Why the Lexical role field is recorded: where in the logic's grammar the keyword stands, and so what kind of thing the binding names.
    GRAPH
    A structure of vertices connected by edges — the root of the structure family this model stores knowledge in.
    GREAT_BRITAIN_ENGLISH_DIALECT
    Great Britain English dialect
    GREATER_THAN
    Greater than (SOLOR)
    GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO
    Greater than or equal to (SOLOR)
    GREATEST_SELECTION
    A statement operator that takes a set of statements and the name of one statement measure and returns the statements that could hold the greatest value of it: those whose high end is not below the highest of the low ends.
    GREGORIAN_CALENDAR
    The calendar in civil use, which defines day, week, month, and year as stretches of the time scale: a day runs from midnight to midnight in a time zone, a week is seven days, a month has 28 to 31 days, and a year has 365 or 366.
    GREGORIAN_CALENDAR_DATE
    A time scale: civil dates counted in days from 1970-01-01, with no time zone, what Java's LocalDate records.
    GRETEL
    Gretel (User)
    GROUPING
    Grouping (SOLOR)
    HAS_ACTIVE_INGREDIENT
    Has Active Ingredient (SOLOR)
    HAS_DOSE_FORM
    Has Dose Form (SOLOR)
    HEALTH_CONCEPT
    Health concept (SOLOR)
    HOUR
    A unit of time of fixed length, sixty minutes.
    IDENTIFIED_COMPONENT
    What an Identifier Pattern semantic's referenced component is: the component an external identifier names — the carrier of an alternate identity in another identifier scheme, distinct from Identifier source, which names the field value saying where that identifier came from (IKE-Network/ike-issues#891).
    IDENTIFIER_AUTHORITY
    Why an identifier source value is recorded: to say which identifier-issuing authority the identifier came from.
    IDENTIFIER_SOURCE
    Identifier Source
    IDENTIFIER_TEXT
    Why an identifier value is recorded: to hold the identifier's own literal text, once a source has been chosen.
    IDENTIFIER_VALUE
    Identifier Value (SOLOR)
    IDENTITY
    A construct relation in which the two are one idea admitted twice, so that every claim true of one is true of the other and nothing is lost either way.
    IKE_BASE_MODEL_CONCEPT
    IKE base model concept
    IKE_COMMUNITY
    Community authorship: the IKE Network itself, attributed as author for content synthesized by tooling on the Network's behalf (e.g. the identity-exact starter-set ingest, IKE-Network/ike-issues#872) rather than by an individual editor or an ingested upstream source.

    IMPORTER
    The importer that read the release, with its version: the implementation version of its jar, otherwise the jar's file name.
    INACTIVATE_COMPONENT
    Retires a component: writes a new version of the subject with state inactive and every field as the latest version has it.
    INACTIVE_STATE
    Inactive state

    An indeterminate result on the presence frame of reference, and one of the three presence values: the determination could not tell whether the topic was present or absent.
    INDETERMINATE_RESULT
    An indeterminate result means a determination was performed but could not arrive at a value within its frame of reference.

    INSTANT
    A time reading: a position in time with no extent, an onset or a blood draw, whose bounds are where the moment could be.
    INSTANT_DEFAULT
    The Instant field's loud default: the premundane instant, the time type's native non-value — the platform's own before-all-recorded-time marker, chosen over a sentinel date because a true non-value cannot be mistaken for a real timestamp.
    INSTANT_FIELD
    Instant field

    INSTANT_SUBSTITUTION

    INTEGER_DEFAULT
    The Integer field's loud default: the stretched-sevens sentinel 777777777 (nine sevens) — a repdigit signature that reads as deliberately planted and cannot plausibly occur as natural data, where Integer.MIN_VALUE would read as an overflow bug.
    INTEGER_FIELD
    Integer field

    Is-a inferred navigation (SOLOR)
    IS_A_STATED_NAVIGATION
    Is-a stated navigation (SOLOR)
    ITALIAN_LANGUAGE
    Italian Language (SOLOR)
    JOURNAL_ELEMENTS
    The ordered lines of one structured document, as prose elements: the manifest pattern's single field.
    JOURNAL_MANIFEST
    What a manifest semantic means: the ordered lines of one structured document, a document or a conversation journal.
    JUDGMENT
    A stance on the referenced version.
    KEYWORD_BINDING
    What an Expression Language Keyword Pattern semantic is: one spelling, in one logic, of one construct, kind, or literal.
    KEYWORD_TEXT
    The spelling in the binding logic, exactly as written, with the case the logic's grammar uses.
    KIND_ASSERTION
    A value taken as being of a kind: the value itself when it is of that kind, the missing value of that kind when it is missing, and otherwise the missing value of that kind, or a refusal where the assertion is strict.
    KIND_CONVERSION
    A value re-expressed in another kind where its content carries over: a whole number as a decimal at one place, a date as an instant, a code as a one-code concept, a value as a one-element list, text read into the value it writes, a value written out as text.
    KIND_LIMIT
    The greatest or least value a language writes for a kind: a limit of the language's machine words and calendars, not of the measure, which has no width.
    KIND_OF_FIELD_CONSTRAINT
    Legal values are the anchor concept itself plus every one of its descendants (self included) — the kind-of relation.
    KIND_TEST
    Whether a value is of a kind or of one under it: Present or Absent, and Absent for a missing value, which is of no kind.
    KNOWLEDGE_BASE_COMPOSITION
    How a knowledge base was assembled: its inputs in load order with their checksums, the source releases it holds in the order they arrived, and the classifier that reasoned over them.
    KNOWLEDGE_BASE_PROVENANCE
    Recording what a knowledge base is made of, inside the knowledge base, so a store can say which releases it holds and how it was assembled: the purpose of the source release and composition patterns and their fields.
    KNOWLEDGE_BASE_PROVENANCE_MODEL
    The apparatus a knowledge base uses to record what it is made of: the source releases imported into it and the assembly that composed them.
    KOMET_ACTION
    Something a person or the assistant does to the knowledge base through Komet, with a defined input and result: offered in a menu by the rules that decide when it makes sense, and offered to the assistant as a tool under the same rules.
    KOMET_ASSISTANT
    The author of the Komet assistant's turns in a conversation journal, and of what the assistant proposes; a person settles what it proposes.
    KOMET_ISSUE
    Komet issue (SOLOR)
    KOMET_MODULE
    KOMET module (SOLOR)
    KOMET_USER
    KOMET user (SOLOR)
    KOREAN_DIALECT
    Korean dialect (SOLOR)
    KOREAN_LANGUAGE
    Korean Language (SOLOR)
    LANGUAGE
    Language
    LANGUAGE_CONCEPT_NID_FOR_DESCRIPTION
    Language concept nid for description (SOLOR)
    LANGUAGE_COORDINATE_NAME
    Language coordinate name (SOLOR)
    LANGUAGE_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES
    Language coordinate properties (SOLOR)
    LANGUAGE_MEMBERSHIP
    Why the Binding language field is recorded: the logic's allowed constructs are exactly the constructs its bindings name.
    LANGUAGE_NID_FOR_LANGUAGE_COORDINATE
    Language nid for language coordinate (SOLOR)
    LANGUAGE_SPECIFICATION_FOR_LANGUAGE_COORDINATE
    Language specification for language coordinate (SOLOR)
    LATERALITY
    Laterality (SOLOR)
    LEAF_DESCENDANT_FIELD_CONSTRAINT
    Legal values are the anchor concept's leaf descendants only — descendants with no children of their own — excluding grouping concepts that exist only to organize other concepts.
    LEAST_SELECTION
    A statement operator that takes a set of statements and the name of one statement measure and returns the statements that could hold the least value of it: those whose low end is not above the lowest of the high ends.
    LEGACY
    A visible deprecation signal, not a functional restriction: content reparented here is dormant or superseded and a candidate for removal in a near-future revision.
    LEGAL_VALUE_SOURCE
    Why the Value-set pattern value is recorded: to name the pattern whose active semantics enumerate the legal values for a value-set constraint.
    LESS_THAN
    Less than (SOLOR)
    LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL_TO
    Less than or equal to (SOLOR)
    LEXICAL_ROLE
    The place a keyword occupies in its logic's grammar, which decides what kind of thing the keyword's binding names.
    LICENSE
    The model family for content licenses — the terms a knowledge artifact is published and consumed under.
    LIST_FLATTENING
    A list of lists lifted one level into one list.
    LIST_KIND
    An operand kind: an ordered collection of values of one kind, kept in the order given and allowing a value to repeat; what a query yields before it is reduced.
    LITERAL_DENOTATION
    What a Literal Denotation Pattern semantic is: the kind and the bounds of one literal, a fixed value of the query language.
    LITERAL_KEYWORD
    A lexical role: the keyword is itself a fixed value of the logic, so the binding names the literal that carries that value's bounds.
    LITERAL_LOWER_BOUND
    Why the literal's lower bound is recorded: the low end of the value it stands for.
    LITERAL_UPPER_BOUND
    Why the literal's upper bound is recorded: the high end of the value it stands for.
    LITERAL_VALUE
    Literal value (SOLOR)
    LITHUANIAN_LANGUAGE
    Lithuanian language (SOLOR)
    LOGIC_COORDINATE_NAME
    Logic coordinate name (SOLOR)
    LOGIC_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES
    Logic coordinate properties (SOLOR)
    LOGIC_GRAPH_FOR_SEMANTIC
    Logic graph for semantic (SOLOR)
    LOGICAL_DEFINITION
    Logical Definition
    LOGICAL_EQUIVALENCE
    A construct relation in which the two constructs give the same result on every input and agree on operand kind, result kind, and arity.
    LOGICAL_EXPRESSION_DISPLAY_FIELD
    Logical expression display field (SOLOR)
    LOGICAL_EXPRESSION_SEMANTIC
    Logical expression semantic (SOLOR)
    LOGICAL_EXPRESSION_VERTEX
    The kinds of node in an EL++ expression tree that are not operators: the definition root that anchors an expression, and the concept reference that names a class.
    LOGICALLY_EQUIVALENT_TO
    Logically equivalent to (Solor)
    LONG
    Long (SOLOR)
    LONG_DEFAULT
    The Long field's loud default: the stretched-sevens sentinel 777777777777777777 (eighteen sevens) — a repdigit signature that reads as deliberately planted and cannot plausibly occur as natural data, where Long.MIN_VALUE would read as an overflow bug (and sits one away from the platform's premundane time sentinel).
    LOWER_BOUND_OPEN
    Lower Bound Open
    LOWER_BOUND_VALUE
    The lower bound of a literal's measure, as a whole number on the result kind's scale: 0 or 1 on the Presence semantic.
    MARK_CODE_FIELD
    The field of the pattern that carries the class's code.
    MARK_MODEL_NAME
    The name of the model of IKE's own that a pattern is written into.
    MARK_RETRIEVABLE
    Whether a library may retrieve the pattern's semantics as a class.
    MASTER_PATH
    Master path
    MATCH_RULE
    Why the Member match relation value is recorded: to say how a constrained field's value must match an enumerated member — which member match relation the constraint holds under.
    MAXIMUM_VALUE_OPERATOR
    Maximum Value Operator (SOLOR)
    MEANING
    Meaning
    MEANING_DECLARATION
    Why a Pattern Version Pattern's Pattern meaning field is recorded: to hold this pattern-version's own declared meaning concept.
    MEASURE_ADDITION
    A measure operator that adds two or more measures, in any order.
    MEASURE_ADJACENCY
    Whether one extent's end is the neighbour of the other's start at the kind's step, on either side or on a named one; an unknown end leaves it open.
    MEASURE_AFTER
    An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the first is entirely later, or higher, than the second.
    MEASURE_AGGREGATE
    A measure operator that produces one measure from a list of measures.
    MEASURE_ALIGNMENT
    Whether two extents share a start, the first ending no later, or share an end, the first starting no earlier.
    MEASURE_ALL_PRESENT
    A measure aggregate over presence values, Presence AND across a list: Present when every member that counts is Present, Absent when any member is Absent, and Indeterminate otherwise; with no member it comes out with nothing, as Existence does on an empty set.
    MEASURE_ANY_PRESENT
    A measure aggregate over presence values, Presence OR across a list: Present when any member that counts is Present, Absent when every member is Absent, and Indeterminate otherwise; with no member it comes out with nothing.
    MEASURE_BEFORE
    An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the first is entirely earlier, or lower, than the second.
    MEASURE_COMPARISON
    A criterion that compares a measure with an interval on a measure semantic: one of the statement's measures, the result, the timing, the normal range, or a request's, with a threshold in millimoles per liter or a date on the calendar; or a presence value, stored or produced by another comparison, with the presence values that count.
    MEASURE_CONTAINS
    An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the first encloses the second.
    MEASURE_CONVERSION
    A measure operator that converts a measure from one unit to another: a weight recorded in grams given in kilograms, a glucose in milligrams per decilitre given in millimoles per litre.
    MEASURE_COUNT
    A measure aggregate that gives how many members count, as a single value whose measure semantic is a count of statements.
    MEASURE_DIVISION
    A measure operator that divides the first of two measures by the second.
    MEASURE_EXPONENTIATION
    A base raised to an exponent: exact for a whole exponent, a decimal at eight places otherwise; e is a base like any other.
    MEASURE_GREATEST
    A measure aggregate that gives the greatest value among the members that count: from the highest of the low ends to the highest of the high ends.
    MEASURE_INNER_SPAN
    A measure operator that takes two measures on one scale and gives the period from the latest value the first allows to the earliest value the second allows: what was certainly covered, and nothing at all when those two cross.
    MEASURE_KIND
    An operand kind: an ANF measure, a lower and an upper bound, the inclusivity of each, a resolution, and the measure semantic that is its frame of reference.
    MEASURE_LEAST
    A measure aggregate that gives the least value among the members that count: from the lowest of the low ends to the lowest of the high ends.
    MEASURE_LIST_KIND
    An operand kind: a list of measures on one measure semantic, one entry per statement, in which the same value appears as many times as statements recorded it.
    MEASURE_LIST_MERGE
    A measure list operator that takes a list of periods and returns the fewest periods that cover the same time.
    MEASURE_LIST_OPERATOR
    An operator that produces a list of measures from a list of measures, the measures of a set of statements gathered by a Measure projection.
    MEASURE_LIST_SPLIT
    A measure list operator that takes a list of periods and a unit of time and returns one measure for each whole unit that any period touches, in order, each a whole unit of that size.
    MEASURE_LOGARITHM
    The exponent that raises a base to a value, at eight places; missing of a non-positive value or at base one.
    MEASURE_LOWER_BOUND
    A measure operator that gives the lowest value inside a measure as a single value on the same measure semantic: the lower bound when it is included, and otherwise the first value above it at the measure's resolution.
    MEASURE_MAGNITUDE
    A measure with its sign dropped: the distance from zero on its semantic.
    MEASURE_MEAN
    A measure aggregate that gives the mean of the members that count: from the mean of the low ends to the mean of the high ends.
    MEASURE_MEDIAN
    A measure aggregate that gives the median of the members that count: from the median of the low ends to the median of the high ends.
    MEASURE_MODE
    The most frequent present value of a list, the least of them when several tie; missing of none.
    MEASURE_MULTIPLICATION
    A measure operator that multiplies two or more measures, in any order.
    MEASURE_OPERATOR
    An operator that produces a measure from one or more measures.
    MEASURE_OUTER_SPAN
    A measure operator that takes two measures on one scale and gives the period from the earliest value the first allows to the latest value the second allows.
    MEASURE_OVERLAPS
    An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the two share any of the scale.
    MEASURE_PRODUCT
    The product of a list's present values; missing of none.
    MEASURE_PROJECTION
    A statement operator that takes a set of statements and the name of one statement measure, the result, the timing, the normal range, or a request's, and returns the list of that measure from each statement that carries it, one entry per statement.
    MEASURE_RATIO
    A numerator measure and a denominator measure, each on its own measure semantic, kept as written: 1:128 stays 1:128 and 5 mg:1 mL stays a strength rather than becoming a concentration, because the two parts mean something apart.
    MEASURE_ROUNDING
    A number taken to a whole number or to a number of places: up, down, toward zero, or to the nearest with a half taken away from zero.
    MEASURE_SINGLE_POINT
    The one value of an extent whose ends coincide; missing when the ends are unknown, refused when the extent is wider.
    MEASURE_SPREAD
    How far a list's present values lie from their mean: the variance or its root, of the sample or of the population, at eight places; missing of none.
    MEASURE_SUBTRACTION
    A measure operator that takes the second of two measures away from the first.
    MEASURE_SUM
    A measure aggregate that adds every member that counts, Measure addition across the list: the low ends added together to the high ends added together, on the members' measure semantic.
    MEASURE_UPPER_BOUND
    A measure operator that gives the highest value inside a measure as a single value on the same measure semantic: the upper bound when it is included, and otherwise the first value below it at the measure's resolution.
    MEASURE_WHOLE_UNIT
    A measure operator that gives the whole unit of a named size that a measure occupies: the day of a timestamp is the whole day, from midnight to midnight, the month of a date is the whole month, and a range that touches two days becomes those two whole days.
    MEASURE_WIDTH
    A measure operator that gives how wide a measure's range is, the upper bound less the lower bound, as a single value on the measure semantic the knowledge layer defines for a difference on that scale: for a range of dates, a length of time.
    MEASURE_WITHIN
    An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the first is inside the second.
    MEMBER_FIELD_CONSTRAINT
    A taxonomy operator that takes a reference set and yields the concepts of the members whose named field holds a value in a given concept set; the field may be the member itself.
    MEMBER_FIELD_PROJECTION
    A taxonomy operator that takes a reference set and a field of its membership pattern and yields the values of that field across the active members, as a concept set: the ICD-10 codes of a cohort's SNOMED concepts, once a Member field constraint has kept the members that name them.
    MEMBER_MATCH_RELATION
    The closed taxonomy of relations a Value-set Field Constraint Pattern semantic can require between a constrained field's value and an enumerated member.
    MEMBER_OF_REFERENCE_SET
    A taxonomy operator that yields, for a reference-set concept, the concepts its active membership semantics list: a fixed concept set, which is what a CQL value set is too.
    MEMBERSHIP_SEMANTIC
    Membership semantic (SOLOR)
    MILLISECOND
    A unit of time of fixed length, one thousandth of a second, and the finest precision CQL records.
    MINIMUM_VALUE_OPERATOR
    Minimum Value Operator (SOLOR)
    MINUTE
    A unit of time of fixed length, sixty seconds.
    MISSING_VALUE
    A value of a kind with no content: an Indeterminate presence, a measure with its measure semantic and no bounds, a reference to no concept, a list that is missing rather than empty.
    MODEL_BRIDGE
    Why a field is recorded: it says what a model's class or element stands for in IKE's own terms, authored by IKE and checked at admission, so that a library written against the model evaluates over statements.
    MODEL_CASE_SENSITIVE
    Whether the file marks the model's names case sensitive.
    MODEL_CLASS_KIND
    What kind of type the file declares, as written: a class, a profile, or a simple type.
    MODEL_CONCEPT
    Model concept
    MODEL_DEFAULT_CONTEXT
    The context a library runs in when it names none, as written.
    MODEL_GENERATION
    Why a field is recorded: it says how a pattern of IKE's own is written into model information, so that a library can be written against IKE's own knowledge.
    MODEL_INFORMATION_RECORD
    Why a field is recorded: it is what the model information file says, kept verbatim.
    MODEL_INSTRUCTIONS
    What a model must know when it performs the action, beyond the action's definition: what to check first, what never to do, how to report.
    MODEL_NAME
    The name the model information gives the model, as written: FHIR, QDM, QUICK.
    MODEL_PATIENT_BIRTH_DATE_PROPERTY
    The element the file names as the patient's birth date, as written.
    MODEL_PATIENT_CLASS
    The class the file names as the patient, as written.
    MODEL_PATIENT_CLASS_IDENTIFIER
    The identifier the file gives the patient class, as written.
    MODEL_RESOLUTION
    Why a field is recorded: it is what IKE resolved the file's text to, a concept, a semantic, or a tree of the catalog's type specifiers, and is IKE's, not the file's.
    MODEL_SCHEMA_LOCATION
    Where the file says the model's schema is, as written.
    MODEL_STRICT_RETRIEVE_TYPING
    Whether the file marks retrieves as strictly typed.
    MODEL_TARGET_QUALIFIER
    The qualifier the file gives the model's types, as written.
    MODEL_TARGET_URL
    The url of the model a profile model stands on, as written, empty when none.
    MODEL_TARGET_VERSION
    The version of the model a profile model stands on, as written.
    MODEL_URL
    The url the model's types are qualified by in a library, as written.
    MODEL_VERSION
    The model's version as written, empty when the file gives none.

    Module
    MODULE_EXCLUSION_SET_FOR_STAMP_COORDINATE
    Module exclusion set for stamp coordinate (SOLOR)
    MODULE_FIELD
    A concept field whose value is the module dimension of a STAMP — the module the version belongs to.
    MODULE_FOR_VERSION

    MODULE_LINEAGE
    Why a module's own origin record is captured: to track which modules a given module originated from.
    MODULE_OPTIONS_FOR_EDIT_COORDINATE

    MODULE_ORIGINS

    MODULE_PREFERENCE_LIST_FOR_LANGUAGE_COORDINATE
    Module preference list for language coordinate (SOLOR)
    MODULE_PREFERENCE_LIST_FOR_STAMP_COORDINATE
    Module preference list for stamp coordinate (SOLOR)
    MODULE_PREFERENCE_ORDER_FOR_STAMP_COORDINATE
    Module preference order for stamp coordinate (SOLOR)
    MODULES_FOR_STAMP_COORDINATE
    Modules for stamp coordinate (SOLOR)
    MODULES_WRITTEN
    The modules of the stamps the import wrote.
    MONTH
    A unit of the Gregorian calendar, twenty-eight to thirty-one days, so a duration in months depends on where in the calendar it starts.
    NARRATIVE_CIRCUMSTANCE
    A circumstance kind: text about the topic that resists being structured, kept as written.
    NAVIGATE_ACTION
    An action that changes what a person sees — focus, window, layout — and nothing in the knowledge base.

    Navigation (SOLOR)
    NAVIGATION_CONCEPT_SET

    The dimensions of the navigation coordinate — how a view traverses parent/child structure: the navigation concept set naming which navigation patterns to read, the vertex state set filtering which states a vertex may be in, and the vertex sort ordering siblings.
    NAVIGATION_VERTEX
    Navigation vertex (SOLOR)
    NECESSARY_BUT_NOT_SUFFICIENT_CONCEPT_DEFINITION
    Necessary but not sufficient concept definition (SOLOR)
    NECESSARY_SET
    Necessary set
    NEIGHBOURING_VALUE
    The next or the previous value at a kind's step: one for a whole number, the eighth place for a decimal, one unit of the written resolution for a date or a time.
    NID
    NID (SOLOR)
    NORMAL_RANGE_MEASURE
    A statement measure, cross-cutting to the result: the reference range that framed this determination, on the result's own measure semantic.
    NOT_APPLICABLE
    Not Applicable (SOLOR)
    NULLARY
    An operator that takes no operand: a literal, a reference, a retrieve.
    NUMERIC_VALUE_RESTRICTION
    Why a Value Constraint Pattern semantic exists: to restrict which literal values are legal for a component — the numeric-domain counterpart to Field Value Restriction.
    OBJECT
    Object (SOLOR)
    OBJECT_PROPERTIES
    Object Properties (SOLOR)
    OPERAND_COUNT
    Why the Arity field is recorded: how many operands the operator takes.
    OPERAND_KIND
    The kind of thing an operator works on or yields, taken from ANF's structural definition.
    OPERAND_TYPING
    Why the Operand kind field is recorded: what the operator takes.
    OPERATOR_KEYWORD
    A lexical role: the keyword names an operation applied to operands, so the binding names a construct.
    ORDERING
    The rows of a query in the order its keys give, missing values first.
    ORDERING_KEY
    One key of an ordering: the rows themselves, a column by its path, or an expression of each row, ascending or descending.
    ORIGIN_CHECKSUM
    The SHA-256 of the artifact as imported, written sha256:; for a directory, of its files in path order, each relative path followed by its content.
    ORIGIN_MODULE_SET
    Why a module's origin set value is recorded: to name the modules this module originated from.
    ORIGINATED_MODULE
    What a Module origins pattern semantic's referenced component is: the module whose origins are declared — the module that originated from the modules the semantic names, distinct from Module origins, which names the origin-set value itself.
    ORIGINATED_PATH
    What a Path origins pattern semantic's referenced component is: the path whose branch point is declared — the path that originated from the path the semantic names, distinct from Path origins, which names the origin-record value itself.
    OUTCOME_MESSAGE
    Text for the person or the model about the outcome: why the run was refused or failed, or what to look at next.
    PARAMETER_REFERENCE
    The use of a value supplied to a library when it is evaluated, or the parameter's default when none is supplied.
    PART_LISTING
    The parts of a value as a list: a tuple's parts, a list's elements.
    PART_OF
    Part of (SOLOR)
    PARTIAL
    Partial (SOLOR)
    PATH
    Path
    PATH_CONCEPT
    Path concept (SOLOR)
    PATH_COORDINATE_NAME
    Path coordinate name (SOLOR)
    PATH_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES
    Path coordinate properties (SOLOR)
    PATH_FIELD
    A concept field whose value is the path dimension of a STAMP — the path the version was committed on.
    PATH_FOR_PATH_COORDINATE
    Path for path coordinate (SOLOR)
    PATH_FOR_VERSION
    Path for version
    PATH_LINEAGE
    Why a path's own origin record is captured: to track which path it branched from, and when.
    PATH_OPTIONS_FOR_EDIT_COORDINATE
    Path options for edit coordinate (SOLOR)
    PATH_ORIGINS
    Path origins (SOLOR)
    PATH_ORIGINS_FOR_STAMP_PATH
    Path origins for stamp path (SOLOR)
    PATTERN_FIELD
    A component field narrowed to patterns: its value references a pattern.
    PATTERN_MEANING_FIELD
    A concept field whose value is a pattern version's declared meaning concept — naming what a semantic of the pattern is about.
    PATTERN_MEMBERSHIP
    Why a Semantic Chronology Pattern's Semantic pattern field is recorded: to identify which pattern this semantic is an instance of.
    PATTERN_PURPOSE_FIELD
    A concept field whose value is a pattern version's declared purpose concept — naming why semantics of the pattern are captured.
    PATTERN_VERSIONS_FIELD
    The component versions field narrowed to pattern chronicles: its value collects a pattern's own versions.
    PATTERN_VERSIONS_SET
    Why a pattern chronicle's versions field is recorded: to hold every version the pattern has ever had — the pattern-chronicle specialization of Component versions set.
    PERFORMANCE_CIRCUMSTANCE
    A circumstance kind: what was determined about the topic, a result as a measure, with what became of the act, when, and by what method.
    PERFORMED_ACTION
    The kind of action a run performed: a concept beneath Komet action.
    PERIOD
    A time reading: a stretch of time with a beginning and an end, a hospital stay, whose bounds are where it began and ended.
    PERIOD_DURATION_MEASURE
    A repetition measure: how long the repeated action should continue, on a time-unit measure semantic, such as seven to ten days.
    PERIOD_START_MEASURE
    A repetition measure: when the repeated action should begin, on a date-time measure semantic.
    PHENOMENON
    Phenomenon

    Polish dialect (SOLOR)
    POLISH_LANGUAGE
    Polish Language (Language)

    PREFERRED_REVIEWER_ASSIGNMENT
    Illustrative pattern whose single field is constrained to membership in the starter set author roster, demonstrating a Value-set Field Constraint Pattern end to end.
    PRESENCE_AND
    A connective operator that joins two or more presence values into one, in any order; every one of them is required.
    PRESENCE_EXCLUSIVE_OR
    A connective operator on two presence values: Present when one is Present and the other Absent, Absent when both are Present or both are Absent, and Indeterminate when either is Indeterminate.
    PRESENCE_IMPLICATION
    A connective operator on two presence values: Present when the first is Absent or the second is Present, Absent when the first is Present and the second is Absent, and Indeterminate otherwise.
    PRESENCE_MEASURE_KIND
    A measure kind: a measure on the Presence semantic, whose value is one of three.
    PRESENCE_NOT
    A connective operator on one presence value that turns Present into Absent and Absent into Present, and leaves Indeterminate as it is, because the opposite of could not tell is still could not tell.
    PRESENCE_OR
    A connective operator that joins two or more presence values into one, in any order; any one of them is enough.
    PRESENT_LITERAL
    One of the three presence values: the determination found the topic present.
    PRESENTATION_UNIT_DIFFERENT
    Presentation unit different (SOLOR)
    PRIMORDIAL_MODULE
    Primordial module
    PRIMORDIAL_PATH
    Primordial path
    PRIMORDIAL_STATE
    Primordial state
    PRIMORDIAL_UUID_FOR_CHRONICLE
    Primordial UUID for chronicle (SOLOR)
    PROMOTION_PATH_FOR_EDIT_COORDINATE
    Promotion Path for Edit Coordinate (SOLOR)
    PROPERTY_ACCESS
    Reading one part of a value by name: on a statement, the reading the named element stands for; on a tuple, the part of that name.
    PROPERTY_PATTERN_IMPLICATION
    Property pattern implication (SOLOR)
    PROPERTY_SEQUENCE
    Property Sequence (SOLOR)
    PROPERTY_SEQUENCE_IMPLICATION
    Property sequence implication
    PROPERTY_SET
    Property set (SOLOR)
    PROPERTY_SET_AXIOMS
    Property set Axioms
