    A prose block's text: lightweight markup whose inline concept references are id-bearing k: tokens — the interchange form.
    PROSE_ELEMENT
    An embedded prose block: the journal owns the content, carried as text on the prose element pattern.
    PUBLIC_ID_FIELD
    The field kind holding a chronicle's public identity — the universally unique identifiers that name a component across every system it is exchanged with.
    PURPOSE
    Purpose
    PURPOSE_DECLARATION
    Why a Pattern Version Pattern's Pattern purpose field is recorded: to hold this pattern-version's own declared purpose concept.
    QDM_DIALECT
    The dialect in which a class's name and label are read as the QDM model information writes them, so that a class is found by either, the way a unit is found by its name and its symbol.
    QI_CORE_DIALECT
    The dialect in which a class's name and label are read as the QI-Core model information writes them, so that a class is found by either, the way a unit is found by its name and its symbol.
    QUERY
    A pass over the values of one or more sources, alias by alias, keeping those a condition admits, correlating them with other sources where asked, and yielding what a return clause names, in order where sorted.
    QUERY_BINDING
    A name bound to a value per row of a query, for the clauses that follow.
    QUERY_CLAUSES
    Query clauses (SOLOR)
    QUERY_FOLDING
    The rows of a query folded into one value through a named accumulator, from a starting value or missing, over distinct rows when asked.
    QUERY_PROJECTION
    What each kept row of a query yields, distinct unless the clause says all.
    QUERY_SOURCE
    One source of a query, a list or a single value, named by the alias the query reads it through.
    QUICK_DIALECT
    The dialect in which a class's name and label are read as the QUICK model information writes them, so that a class is found by either, the way a unit is found by its name and its symbol.
    READ_ACTION
    An action that reports on the knowledge base and changes nothing in it.
    REFERENCE_RANGE
    Reference Range (SOLOR)
    REFERENCE_RANGE_AUTHORITY
    Why a value constraint's source value is recorded: to name the organization that specifies the constraint.
    REFERENCE_RANGE_MAXIMUM
    Reference Range Maximum (SOLOR)
    REFERENCE_RANGE_MINIMUM
    Reference Range Minimum (SOLOR)
    REFERENCED_COMPONENT_NID_FOR_SEMANTIC
    Referenced component nid for semantic (SOLOR)
    REFERENCED_COMPONENT_SUBTYPE_RESTRICTION
    Referenced component subtype restriction (SOLOR)
    REFERENCED_COMPONENT_TYPE_RESTRICTION
    Referenced component type restriction (SOLOR)

    Reflexive Feature (SOLOR)

    REGULAR_NAME_DESCRIPTION_TYPE
    Regular name description type

    Why the Construct relation field is recorded: which of the three checked relations is claimed, and therefore which check runs.
    RELATION_TARGET
    Why the Core construct field is recorded: which core construct the claim is about.
    RELATIONSHIP_CONTEXT
    That context's record on the model, resolved by IKE.
    RELATIONSHIP_CONTEXT_NAME
    The context a class reaches, as written.
    RELATIONSHIP_DESTINATION
    Relationship destination
    RELATIONSHIP_KEY_ELEMENT
    The element by which the class reaches the context, as written.
    RELATIONSHIP_ORIGIN
    Relationship origin
    RELATIONSHIP_TO_TARGET
    Whether the file declares the relationship on the target model rather than this one.
    RELEASE_ARTIFACT
    The artifact the release was imported from: its Maven coordinate when it was resolved from a repository, otherwise its file name.
    RELEASE_DATE
    When the release took effect in the knowledge base: the latest time among the stamps its import wrote.
    RELEASE_NAME
    The source's own name for the release, as its importer reports it: an edition, a version, a release date.
    REMAINDER
    What remains of a dividend after the whole quotient is taken, with the dividend's sign; missing at a zero divisor.
    REPEAT_REMOVAL
    A list with each value once, a missing element the same as a missing element, in the order first seen.
    REPETITION_MEASURE
    A statement measure on a request that describes an action requested for more than one occurrence: how often, for how long, and from when.
    REPLACEMENT_TEXT
    The text a run puts in place of its subject's: for a document block, the block's new lines, one per line.

    REQUEST_TIMING_MEASURE

    REQUESTED_RESULT_MEASURE
    A statement measure on a request: the result that is sought, on the measure semantic the result will have.

    The required model's concept in the store, resolved by IKE.
    REQUIRED_MODEL_NAME
    The name of a model this model requires, as written.
    REQUIRED_MODEL_VERSION
    The version of a model this model requires, as written.
    RESULT_KIND
    The operand kind of the result a construct or a literal yields.
    RESULT_MEASURE
    A statement measure: the statement's one result, what was determined, on the statement's measure semantic.
    RESULT_PATTERN
    The pattern each run's result takes: what the action produced, and whether it completed.
    RESULT_READING
    A statement reading: the result of a performance, a measure.
    RESULT_TYPING
    Why the Result kind field is recorded: what the operator yields.
    REVIEW_MODULE
    The module annotations made in a knowledge base are written to, so a module coordinate decides whether review metadata travels with a release.
    REVIEW_ROUTING
    Why a Preferred Reviewer Pattern semantic exists: to direct a component's future edits to a specific reviewer.
    REVIEWED_PROVENANCE
    Recording who reviewed which version of what, and their stance: the purpose of the Annotation pattern and its fields.
    REVIEWED_VERSION
    The STAMP of the version the annotator saw; with the referenced component it names one exact, immutable version.

    Role
    ROLE_GROUP
    Role group
    ROLE_OPERATOR
    Role operator

    Role restriction (SOLOR)
    ROLE_TYPE
    Role type
    ROLE_TYPE_TO_ADD
    Role type to add (SOLOR)
    ROOT_FOR_LOGIC_COORDINATE
    Root for logic coordinate (SOLOR)

    The author concept named by one roster entry.
    ROSTER_ENTRY
    Why a roster author value is recorded: to name one member of the roster.
    ROSTER_MEMBERSHIP
    Why a Starter Set Author Roster Pattern semantic exists: to enumerate this starter set's own author roster as a value-set source.
    ROSTER_ORDER
    The roster entry's display order — the "additional characteristic" field a value-set constraint's Value-set field disambiguates against.
    RUSSIAN_DIALECT
    Russian dialect (SOLOR)
    RUSSIAN_LANGUAGE
    Russian language (SOLOR)

    Sandbox component (SOLOR)
    SANDBOX_MODULE
    Sandbox module (SOLOR)
    SANDBOX_PATH
    Sandbox path
    SANDBOX_PATH_MODULE
    Sandbox path module (SOLOR)

    The identifier source of SNOMED CT identifiers (SCTIDs): an identifier semantic whose source is this concept carries the SNOMED CT identifier of the component it identifies.
    SECOND
    A unit of time of fixed length, sixty to the minute.
    SEMANTIC_DATA_TYPE
    Semantic data type
    SEMANTIC_DEFAULT
    The Semantic field's loud default: the fully qualified name description semantic of Uninitialized Component — a real, resolvable semantic whose subject is itself the loud placeholder, so the reference is valid yet plainly unrevised.
    SEMANTIC_FIELD
    A component field narrowed to semantics: its value references a semantic.
    SEMANTIC_FIELD_CONCEPTS
    Semantic field concepts (SOLOR)
    SEMANTIC_FIELD_FIELD
    The field kind naming a semantic version's field-value slot: each value is one field the version actually carries, as distinct from the field definition its pattern declares.
    SEMANTIC_FIELD_FIELDS_SET
    Why a semantic version's field-value field is recorded: to hold, together, every field value that version carries — the value-side counterpart to a pattern's Field definitions set.
    SEMANTIC_FIELD_NAME
    Semantic field name (SOLOR)
    SEMANTIC_LIST_FOR_CHRONICLE
    Semantic list for chronicle (SOLOR)
    SEMANTIC_PATTERN_FIELD
    A pattern field whose value identifies which pattern a semantic is an instance of — the field a semantic chronicle records for pattern membership.
    SEMANTIC_PROPERTIES
    Semantic properties (SOLOR)
    SEMANTIC_REFERENCED_COMPONENT_FIELD

    SEMANTIC_TYPE
    Semantic type (SOLOR)

    The component versions field narrowed to semantic chronicles: its value collects a semantic's own versions.

    Why a semantic chronicle's versions field is recorded: to hold every version the semantic has ever had — the semantic-chronicle specialization of Component versions set.
    SET_AND
    A connective operator that joins two or more sets of one kind into one set of that kind and requires every one of them: the result is the members that are in every operand set.
    SET_DIFFERENCE
    A connective operator that takes two sets of one kind and produces a set of that kind.

    An operand kind: a set of things of one kind, concepts, statements, or subjects.

    A component's role as an element of a pattern's own set of semantics — the modern replacement for the deprecated SOLOR term Membership semantic.
    SET_OR
    A connective operator that joins two or more sets of one kind into one set of that kind and requires at least one of them: the result is the members that are in any operand set.

    The one value of a list that holds one; a missing value for an empty list; a refusal for a list of more than one.
    SNOMED_CT_EXPRESSION_CONSTRAINT_LANGUAGE
    An expression language: the language for selecting sets of concepts from a classified terminology by is-a, refinement, and set operations.

    STARTER_DATA_AUTHORING

    STATEMENT_OPERATOR
    An operator that works on sets of ANF statements.

    What a model's element answers when a library reads it off a statement: one of a closed set, the statement's topic, its circumstance kind, its disposition, its timing whole or by an end, its result, its statement time, or a fact of the subject.
    STATEMENT_SET_KIND
    An operand kind: a set of ANF statements, which is what a retrieve yields and what a filter narrows.

    A statement measure, cross-cutting to the result: when the statement was made, on a date-time measure semantic.
    STATEMENT_TIME_READING
    A statement reading: when the statement was made, an instant.

    A concept field whose value is the status dimension of a STAMP — the version's state (active, inactive, or otherwise) at the time it was committed.
    STATUS_FOR_VERSION
    Status for version (SOLOR)
    STATUS_VALUE
    Status value
    STRICT_INCLUSION
    Inclusion with sameness ruled out: a value within an extent and at neither end, a list holding an element among more than one, a collection within another and not the same.
    STRING_DATA_TYPE
    String data type
    STRING_DEFAULT
    The String field's loud default: the literal "UNINITIALIZED" — a value that works as an initial value but reads as obviously needing revision, never Java's silent empty string.
    STRING_FIELD
    String field
    STRUCTURED_DOCUMENT
    Anything held as lines in manifest order and grouped into elements: a document materialized from a repository, or a conversation journal.
    SUBJECT_BIRTH_DATE_READING
    A statement reading of the subject rather than the statement: the subject's birth date, a measure on the calendar.
    SUBJECT_OF_COMMENTARY
    The referenced-component role a Comment Pattern semantic's attachment target plays: the subject free-text commentary is about — distinct from Comment, which names the commentary's own content type, not the component being commented on.
    SUBJECT_PROJECTION
    An operator that takes a set of statements and returns the subjects those statements are records of, the subject of record and not the subject of information: a family-history statement is about a relative but is a record of the patient.
    SUBJECT_SET_KIND

    Sufficient concept definition (SOLOR)
    SUFFICIENT_CONCEPT_DEFINITION_OPERATOR
    Sufficient concept definition operator (SOLOR)
    SUFFICIENT_SET

    Swedish language (SOLOR)

    The kind of taxonomy-relative rule a Taxonomy Field Constraint Pattern semantic expresses: which concepts are legal values for the constrained pattern field, derived from the taxonomy under the checking view.

    TAXONOMY_OPERATOR
    Taxonomy operator (SOLOR)

    Why the Constraint anchor concept value is recorded: to give a kind-of, descendant, leaf-descendant, or immediate-child rule something concrete to measure against.

    Parent of the per-purpose template attachment concepts: each child is minted for one template purpose, and a template semantic of a pattern for that purpose is a complete semantic of that pattern whose referenced component is that child — starting content offered when authoring new components.

    Temporal Axiom

    Whether a text begins or ends with another.
    TEXT_CASE
    A text in lower or upper case.
    TEXT_COMPARISON_MEASURE_SEMANTIC
    Text comparison measure semantic (SOLOR)
    TEXT_FOR_DESCRIPTION
    Text for description
    TEXT_JOINING
    Texts joined end to end, or a list's texts joined with a separator; missing when a text is, or the list is empty or missing.

    An operand kind: a sequence of characters read as written, compared character by character; what CQL's String is a value of (IKE-Network/ike-issues#1122).

    TEXT_PATTERN_REPLACEMENT
    A text with every match of a regular expression replaced.

    TEXT_SLICE
    The characters of a text from a position for a length; missing off either end.
    TEXT_SPLITTING
    A text divided at a separator into a list of texts, the text whole when none is given or found.

    A point in time, as a general concept — the meaning counterpart to Status value/Author/Module/Path: what kind of value a STAMP's time field holds, distinct from TimeForVersion, which names why it is recorded.
    TIME_FIELD
    An instant field whose value is the time dimension of a STAMP — when the version was committed.
    TIME_FOR_VERSION
    Time for version (SOLOR)
    TIME_OF_DAY

    TIME_READING
    Whether a timing's bounds are where a moment could be or where a stretch of time began and ended.
    TIME_SCALE
    A measure semantic for a position in time, counted from an origin in a unit, so that a timing's bounds are two numbers on it.
    TIME_ZONE
    A region's rule for reading the clock: the offset from UTC at any instant, including the seasonal changes where daylight saving is used, named as in the IANA database, Europe/Paris, what Java's ZoneId records.
    TIMING_END_READING
    A statement reading: the upper bound of the timing, an instant.
    TIMING_MEASURE
    A statement measure, cross-cutting to the result: when the determination occurred, on a date-time measure semantic.
    TIMING_READING
    A statement reading: when the circumstance held, a measure on the calendar.
    TIMING_START_READING
    A statement reading: the lower bound of the timing, an instant.
    TOPIC_CITATION
    The :topic-citation: attribute of an external-source topic.
    TOPIC_CONSTRAINT
    A criterion that tests the statement's topic for membership in a concept set, named as a concept and its kinds, one concept exactly, an ECL expression, or a reference set, and computed under the view before the test runs.
    TOPIC_ID
    The :topic-id: attribute: the topic's registry key and block anchor.
    TOPIC_KEYWORDS
    The :topic-keywords: attribute, comma-separated.
    TOPIC_LICENSE
    The :topic-license: attribute of an external-source topic.
    TOPIC_PROVENANCE
    The :topic-provenance: attribute of an external-source topic.
    TOPIC_READING
    A statement reading: the statement's topic, a concept.
    TOPIC_SCOPE_NOTE
    The :topic-scope-note: attribute, with its continued lines joined.
    TOPIC_STATUS
    The :topic-status: attribute: draft, review, published, or another registry status.
    TOPIC_TYPE
    The :topic-type: attribute: concept, task, reference, or another registry type.

    Transitive Feature (SOLOR)
    TREE
    A connected, acyclic graph: between any two vertices there is exactly one path.
    TREE_AMALGAM_PROPERTIES
    Tree amalgam properties (SOLOR)
    TREE_LIST
    Tree list (SOLOR)
    TUPLE_KIND
    An operand kind: a value of named parts, each a value of a kind of its own, read part by part by name.
    TYPE_KEYWORD
    A lexical role: the keyword names a type of the logic, so the binding names the operand kind that type is represented as.
    UCUM_ARBITRARY
    Whether UCUM marks the unit arbitrary: a procedure-defined unit like an international unit, which never converts.
    UCUM_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CODE
    The code UCUM gives for systems that cannot keep case, as written.

    The class UCUM files a unit under, as written: si, iso1000, clinical, and the rest.

    The code UCUM gives a unit or a prefix, case-sensitive, as written: mg, min, mm[Hg].

    A unit built by UCUM's grammar from prefixes, units, powers, products, and quotients, such as mg/dL or kg.m/s2, made when it is first met and never listed in advance.

    The unit UCUM defines the unit in terms of, as written.
    UCUM_DEFINITION_VALUE
    The number in UCUM's definition of the unit, as written.

    The dialect in which a unit's UCUM name and print symbol are read, so that a unit is found by either, the way a definition is found by its name.

    UCUM_PREFIX_FACTOR
    The multiplier a prefix stands for, as UCUM writes it.
    UCUM_PRINT_SYMBOL
    The symbol UCUM prints for a unit or a prefix, as written.
    UCUM_PROPERTY
    What a unit measures, in UCUM's word for it: length, mass, time, pressure.
    UCUM_RECORD
    Why a field is recorded: it is what UCUM says, kept verbatim.

    An arity: one operand.

    UNIQUELY_IDENTIFY_KNOWLEDGE_GRAPH_COMPONENTS
    Uniquely identify knowledge graph components

    UNIT_OF_TIME

    Why a field is recorded: it is what IKE computes from UCUM's definitions, and is IKE's, not UCUM's.

    US_NURSING_DIALECT
    US Nursing dialect (SOLOR)
    USERS_MODULE
    Users module (SOLOR)

    UUID_DATA_TYPE
    UUID data type (SOLOR)
    UUID_DISPLAY_FIELD
    UUID display field (SOLOR)
    UUID_LIST_FOR_COMPONENT
    UUID list for component (SOLOR)
    VALUE_CONSTRAINT
    Value Constraint (SOLOR)
    VALUE_CONSTRAINT_SOURCE

    Why the Value-set field value is recorded: to say which Model Feature of the value-set pattern actually holds the member value, when that pattern carries other fields too, such as a sort order.
    VALUE_SET_FIELD
    For a value-set constraint, the Model Feature of the value-set pattern that holds the member value, named by its meaning concept: a declared field's meaning, or the value-set pattern's referenced-component meaning when the members are the referenced components themselves (a membership pattern) — disambiguating when that pattern carries other fields, such as a sort order.
    VALUE_SET_PATTERN
    For a value-set constraint, the pattern whose active semantics enumerate the legal values.
    VARIADIC
    An arity: any number of operands, as with the EL++ set formers and the concept-set and statement-set ANDs and ORs.
    VERSION_HISTORY
    Why a Semantic Chronology Pattern's Semantic versions set is recorded: to hold every version of this semantic, in order — the semantic-level counterpart to the versions-field/set pair every other chronicle-shape pattern already names distinctly.
    VERSION_LIST_FOR_CHRONICLE
    Version list for chronicle (SOLOR)
    VERSION_PROPERTIES
    Version Properties (SOLOR)
    VERSION_PROVENANCE
    Why a version-shape pattern's own STAMP field is recorded: to say who committed this version, in what state, module, path, and when.
    VERSION_SNAPSHOT
    Why a version-shape pattern's referenced component carries this semantic: to record one point-in-time state of a chronicle — the STAMP it was committed with, plus whatever field values were true then.
    VERTEX_DISPLAY_FIELD
    Vertex display field (SOLOR)
    VERTEX_SORT
    Vertex sort (SOLOR)
    VERTEX_STATE_SET
    Vertex state set (SOLOR)
    VIEW_COORDINATE_KEY
    View coordinate key (SOLOR)
    VIEW_COORDINATE_MODEL
    The model family for the coordinates composing a view of the knowledge graph: a view coordinate is composed of a stamp coordinate (which versions are visible), language coordinates (which descriptions to prefer), a logic coordinate (how to reason), a navigation coordinate (how to traverse), and an edit coordinate (where changes are written).
    WEEK
    A unit of the Gregorian calendar, seven calendar days.
    WELL_TYPED_RELATION
    Why a denotation exists: a relation between two constructs is a claim only when both sides say what they take and yield; the kinds decide which relations are even possible; and one keyword naming two constructs is legitimate only when their operand kinds differ.
    WHOLE_QUOTIENT
    The quotient of two numbers taken toward zero; missing at a zero divisor.
    WITHDRAWN_STATE
    Withdrawn state
    WRITTEN_BOUNDARY
    An end of the span a value leaves unwritten, out to a precision asked: the first or the last value the written value could be.
    WRITTEN_COMPONENT_READING
    One component of a value as written: the year, the month of the year, the day of the month, the hour, the minute, the second, or the millisecond of an instant or a time of day, read in the offset the value was written with, or the offset itself.
    WRITTEN_PRECISION
    How finely a value was written: the places of a decimal, the digits of a date's, an instant's, or a time's resolution.
    WRITTEN_VALUE
    A value written in the text of a library, a number, a text, a date, a truth value, held under its type and read as its type's relation says: a number as a measure on the dimensionless number, a truth value as a presence, a date as a measure on the calendar.
    WRITTEN_VERSION
    The STAMP of the version a run wrote; with the run's subject it names that version.
    YEAR
    A unit of the Gregorian calendar, twelve months, 365 or 366 days.

      Field definition meaning field

    • INTERVAL_LOWER_BOUND

      public static final IkeConcept INTERVAL_LOWER_BOUND
      Interval Lower Bound

    • INCLUDE_UPPER_BOUND

      public static final IkeConcept INCLUDE_UPPER_BOUND
      Include Upper Bound

    • FIELD_DEFINITION_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept FIELD_DEFINITION_FIELD
      The field kind naming a pattern version's field-definition slot: each value is one field definition — the meaning, purpose, and data type the pattern declares for one of its fields.

    • FIELD_CATEGORIES

      public static final IkeConcept FIELD_CATEGORIES
      Groups the field-level meta-schema concepts: the terminology describing what kind of value — a component, a field definition, a semantic field, or a set of these — a semantic's field can hold.

    • INTERVAL_UPPER_BOUND

      public static final IkeConcept INTERVAL_UPPER_BOUND
      Interval Upper Bound

    • STAMP_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept STAMP_FIELD
      A component field whose value references a STAMP — the five-dimension provenance tuple a version was committed with. The STAMP Chronology Pattern's referenced-component meaning, and the first field of every version-shape pattern, recorded for version provenance.

    • COMPONENT_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept COMPONENT_FIELD
      The field kind whose value references a component of any kind — concept, pattern, semantic, or STAMP. The parent of every reference-valued field kind, and the Component Chronology Pattern's referenced-component meaning: the component whose identity and history the chronicle records.

    • IMPLICATION_SET

      public static final IkeConcept IMPLICATION_SET
      Implication set

    • INTEGRATED_KNOWLEDGE_MANAGEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept INTEGRATED_KNOWLEDGE_MANAGEMENT
      Integrated Knowledge Management (SOLOR)

    • BOOLEAN_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept BOOLEAN_FIELD
      Boolean field

    • STAMP_VERSIONS_SET

      public static final IkeConcept STAMP_VERSIONS_SET
      Why a STAMP chronicle's versions field is recorded: to hold every version the STAMP has ever had — the STAMP-chronicle specialization of Component versions set.

    • DATA_PROPERTY_SET_AXIOMS

      public static final IkeConcept DATA_PROPERTY_SET_AXIOMS
      Data Property Set Axioms

    • STAMP_VERSIONS_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept STAMP_VERSIONS_FIELD
      The component versions field narrowed to STAMP chronicles: its value collects a STAMP's own versions. The STAMP version field pattern's referenced-component meaning.

    • STATUS_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept STATUS_FIELD
      A concept field whose value is the status dimension of a STAMP — the version's state (active, inactive, or otherwise) at the time it was committed.

    • TIME_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept TIME_FIELD
      An instant field whose value is the time dimension of a STAMP — when the version was committed.

    • AUTHOR_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept AUTHOR_FIELD
      A concept field whose value is the author dimension of a STAMP — who committed the version.

    • COMPONENT_VERSIONS_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept COMPONENT_VERSIONS_FIELD
      The field kind holding a chronicle's version collection — one entry per committed version of the component. Every chronicle-shape pattern declares it beside the public id, and the Component Version Pattern carries it as its own referenced-component meaning.

    • MODULE_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept MODULE_FIELD
      A concept field whose value is the module dimension of a STAMP — the module the version belongs to.

    • DEFAULT_DATA_CONCEPT

      public static final IkeConcept DEFAULT_DATA_CONCEPT
      Default Data Concept

    • DATA_CONCEPT

      public static final IkeConcept DATA_CONCEPT
      Groups concepts that represent data values and defaults — the data-carrying side of the model, as distinct from IKE base model concept's structural, self-descriptive side.

    • IKEFOUNDATION_MODULE

      public static final IkeConcept IKEFOUNDATION_MODULE
      The module scoping every stamp of the IkeFoundation content set; the export dimension for this knowledge.

    • IKEFOUNDATION_ROOT

      public static final IkeConcept IKEFOUNDATION_ROOT
      Root concept of the Ike starter set.

    • IKE_COMMUNITY

      public static final IkeConcept IKE_COMMUNITY
      Community authorship: the IKE Network itself, attributed as author for content synthesized by tooling on the Network's behalf (e.g. the identity-exact starter-set ingest, IKE-Network/ike-issues#872) rather than by an individual editor or an ingested upstream source.

    • SCTID

      public static final IkeConcept SCTID
      The identifier source of SNOMED CT identifiers (SCTIDs): an identifier semantic whose source is this concept carries the SNOMED CT identifier of the component it identifies.

    • PROSE_ELEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept PROSE_ELEMENT
      An embedded prose block: the journal owns the content, carried as text on the prose element pattern.

    • PROSE_CONTENT

      public static final IkeConcept PROSE_CONTENT
      A prose block's text: lightweight markup whose inline concept references are id-bearing k: tokens — the interchange form.

    • ELEMENT_CONTENT

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_CONTENT
      Carrying an element's content: the purpose shared by the element patterns and their fields.

    • JOURNAL_MANIFEST

      public static final IkeConcept JOURNAL_MANIFEST
      What a manifest semantic means: the ordered lines of one structured document, a document or a conversation journal. Inserting, removing or reordering a line writes a new manifest version; replay walks manifest versions in time.

    • JOURNAL_ELEMENTS

      public static final IkeConcept JOURNAL_ELEMENTS
      The ordered lines of one structured document, as prose elements: the manifest pattern's single field.

    • ELEMENT_ORDER

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_ORDER
      Ordering a structured document's lines: the purpose of the journal manifest and its field.

    • TAXONOMY_FIELD_CONSTRAINT_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept TAXONOMY_FIELD_CONSTRAINT_KIND
      The kind of taxonomy-relative rule a Taxonomy Field Constraint Pattern semantic expresses: which concepts are legal values for the constrained pattern field, derived from the taxonomy under the checking view.

    • KIND_OF_FIELD_CONSTRAINT

      public static final IkeConcept KIND_OF_FIELD_CONSTRAINT
      Legal values are the anchor concept itself plus every one of its descendants (self included) — the kind-of relation.

    • DESCENDANT_FIELD_CONSTRAINT

      public static final IkeConcept DESCENDANT_FIELD_CONSTRAINT
      Legal values are every descendant of the anchor concept, not including the anchor concept itself.

    • LEAF_DESCENDANT_FIELD_CONSTRAINT

      public static final IkeConcept LEAF_DESCENDANT_FIELD_CONSTRAINT
      Legal values are the anchor concept's leaf descendants only — descendants with no children of their own — excluding grouping concepts that exist only to organize other concepts.

    • IMMEDIATE_CHILD_FIELD_CONSTRAINT

      public static final IkeConcept IMMEDIATE_CHILD_FIELD_CONSTRAINT
      Legal values are the anchor concept's direct children only, not deeper descendants.

    • CONSTRAINED_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRAINED_FIELD
      The field-meaning concept of the pattern field this constraint governs.

    • CONSTRAINT_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRAINT_KIND
      Which Taxonomy field constraint kind this constraint semantic expresses.

    • CONSTRAINT_ANCHOR_CONCEPT

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRAINT_ANCHOR_CONCEPT
      The concept a kind-of, descendant, leaf-descendant, or immediate-child constraint is relative to.

    • VALUE_SET_PATTERN

      public static final IkeConcept VALUE_SET_PATTERN
      For a value-set constraint, the pattern whose active semantics enumerate the legal values.

    • VALUE_SET_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept VALUE_SET_FIELD
      For a value-set constraint, the Model Feature of the value-set pattern that holds the member value, named by its meaning concept: a declared field's meaning, or the value-set pattern's referenced-component meaning when the members are the referenced components themselves (a membership pattern) — disambiguating when that pattern carries other fields, such as a sort order.

    • MEMBER_MATCH_RELATION

      public static final IkeConcept MEMBER_MATCH_RELATION
      The closed taxonomy of relations a Value-set Field Constraint Pattern semantic can require between a constrained field's value and an enumerated member. Relations are directed and named in full, and a relation is admitted only when its evaluator ships in code: relation concepts correspond one-to-one with the service-loaded evaluators — the bijection gate.

    • EQUAL_MATCH_RELATION

      public static final IkeConcept EQUAL_MATCH_RELATION
      A value matches a member when they are equal by the member datatype's natural equality: entity references by identity, scalars by value, byte arrays by content, and Decimal by numeric equality (compareTo == 0 — an identical-representation rule would be its own relation). Float compares by IEEE semantics, so NaN matches nothing — keeping the loud-defaults coherence: an unrevised NaN default fails its constraint until revised. Graph types are outside this relation's operand conformance — graph enumerations await the isomorphic relations.

    • CONSTRAINED_PATTERN

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRAINED_PATTERN
      The referenced-component role a field constraint semantic's attachment target plays: the pattern that has one of its own fields constrained — one attachment role, shared by the Taxonomy Field Constraint Pattern and the Value-set Field Constraint Pattern, and distinct from the constraint mechanisms themselves.

    • FIELD_VALUE_RESTRICTION

      public static final IkeConcept FIELD_VALUE_RESTRICTION
      Why a field constraint semantic exists: to restrict which values are legal for one of the constrained pattern's own fields.

    • CONSTRAINT_SCOPE

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRAINT_SCOPE
      Why the Constrained field value is recorded: to say which field of the constrained pattern this rule applies to.

    • CONSTRAINT_RULE

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRAINT_RULE
      Why the Constraint kind value is recorded: to say which taxonomy-relative rule — kind-of, descendant, leaf-descendant, or immediate-child — applies.

    • TAXONOMY_REFERENCE_POINT

      public static final IkeConcept TAXONOMY_REFERENCE_POINT
      Why the Constraint anchor concept value is recorded: to give a kind-of, descendant, leaf-descendant, or immediate-child rule something concrete to measure against.

    • LEGAL_VALUE_SOURCE

      public static final IkeConcept LEGAL_VALUE_SOURCE
      Why the Value-set pattern value is recorded: to name the pattern whose active semantics enumerate the legal values for a value-set constraint.

    • VALUE_DISAMBIGUATION

      public static final IkeConcept VALUE_DISAMBIGUATION
      Why the Value-set field value is recorded: to say which Model Feature of the value-set pattern actually holds the member value, when that pattern carries other fields too, such as a sort order.

    • MATCH_RULE

      public static final IkeConcept MATCH_RULE
      Why the Member match relation value is recorded: to say how a constrained field's value must match an enumerated member — which member match relation the constraint holds under.

    • STARTER_SET_AUTHOR_ROSTER

      public static final IkeConcept STARTER_SET_AUTHOR_ROSTER
      Illustrative value-set source: an ordered roster of this starter set's own authors, demonstrating a Value-set Field Constraint Pattern's value-set pattern.

    • ROSTER_AUTHOR

      public static final IkeConcept ROSTER_AUTHOR
      The author concept named by one roster entry.

    • ROSTER_ORDER

      public static final IkeConcept ROSTER_ORDER
      The roster entry's display order — the "additional characteristic" field a value-set constraint's Value-set field disambiguates against.

    • ROSTER_MEMBERSHIP

      public static final IkeConcept ROSTER_MEMBERSHIP
      Why a Starter Set Author Roster Pattern semantic exists: to enumerate this starter set's own author roster as a value-set source.

    • ROSTER_ENTRY

      public static final IkeConcept ROSTER_ENTRY
      Why a roster author value is recorded: to name one member of the roster.

    • DISPLAY_SEQUENCE

      public static final IkeConcept DISPLAY_SEQUENCE
      Why a roster order value is recorded: to say where this entry falls in the roster's own display order.

    • PREFERRED_REVIEWER

      public static final IkeConcept PREFERRED_REVIEWER
      Illustrative constrained field: the reviewer a Preferred Reviewer Pattern semantic names.

    • PREFERRED_REVIEWER_ASSIGNMENT

      public static final IkeConcept PREFERRED_REVIEWER_ASSIGNMENT
      Illustrative pattern whose single field is constrained to membership in the starter set author roster, demonstrating a Value-set Field Constraint Pattern end to end.

    • REVIEW_ROUTING

      public static final IkeConcept REVIEW_ROUTING
      Why a Preferred Reviewer Pattern semantic exists: to direct a component's future edits to a specific reviewer.

    • ASSIGNED_REVIEWER

      public static final IkeConcept ASSIGNED_REVIEWER
      Why a preferred reviewer value is recorded: to name which author is the preferred reviewer.

    • EXPRESSION_LANGUAGE_MODEL

      public static final IkeConcept EXPRESSION_LANGUAGE_MODEL
      The concepts and patterns that represent the operators a query language over ANF needs, and relate each one explicitly to the logics it overlaps: the logics and their dialects; the keyword bindings that admit a construct to a logic; the denotations that say what a construct takes and what it yields; and the checked relations between a construct and a core construct, which are logical equivalence, definitional extension, and conservative extension.

    • EXPRESSION_LANGUAGE

      public static final IkeConcept EXPRESSION_LANGUAGE
      A logic whose expressions are evaluated over this set's content or over ANF statements. A member of this family is the value of a keyword binding's Binding language field, and the logic's allowed constructs are exactly the constructs its keyword bindings name. Each has a dialect of English through which its own spellings display.

    • CLINICAL_QUALITY_LANGUAGE

      public static final IkeConcept CLINICAL_QUALITY_LANGUAGE
      An expression language: the language for clinical quality measure and decision-support logic. Every CQL value is represented as an ANF measure with nothing left over: a Boolean as a presence measure, a Quantity or an Interval as a measure with bounds and inclusivity, a date as a measure on a date-time measure semantic. Once "null" is read as Indeterminate, CQL's three-valued "and", "or", and "not" are the presence connectives, and CQL's own tables follow from them row for row.

    • SNOMED_CT_EXPRESSION_CONSTRAINT_LANGUAGE

      public static final IkeConcept SNOMED_CT_EXPRESSION_CONSTRAINT_LANGUAGE
      An expression language: the language for selecting sets of concepts from a classified terminology by is-a, refinement, and set operations. Every ECL construct is definable from the EL++ core and computes a concept set under a view: new names, no new logic. In a query over ANF it is the topic layer.

    • EL

      public static final IkeConcept EL
      An expression language: the description-logic profile this set's stated and inferred axioms are written in, with class intersection, existential restriction, necessary and sufficient sets, and disjointness. It has no surface syntax of its own. The one keyword bound to it, AND, is the set's own rendering of its conjunction, carried by its dialect.

    • CQL_DIALECT

      public static final IkeConcept CQL_DIALECT
      The dialect of English in which a construct CQL names reads as CQL's keyword, spelled as CQL spells it. Everything CQL does not name falls back to the next dialect in the language coordinate's preference list.

    • ECL_DIALECT

      public static final IkeConcept ECL_DIALECT
      The dialect of English in which a construct ECL names reads as ECL's token, spelled as ECL spells it.

    • EL_DIALECT

      public static final IkeConcept EL_DIALECT
      The dialect of English in which the EL++ conjunction reads as AND. That is the set's own rendering, since EL++ has no surface syntax.

    • LEXICAL_ROLE

      public static final IkeConcept LEXICAL_ROLE
      The place a keyword occupies in its logic's grammar, which decides what kind of thing the keyword's binding names. Also the meaning of the Expression Language Keyword Pattern's third field, whose value is one of its members: Operator keyword, Type keyword, Unit keyword, Literal keyword, Function name, and Declaration keyword.

    • OPERATOR_KEYWORD

      public static final IkeConcept OPERATOR_KEYWORD
      A lexical role: the keyword names an operation applied to operands, so the binding names a construct.

    • TYPE_KEYWORD

      public static final IkeConcept TYPE_KEYWORD
      A lexical role: the keyword names a type of the logic, so the binding names the operand kind that type is represented as.

    • UNIT_KEYWORD

      public static final IkeConcept UNIT_KEYWORD
      A lexical role: the keyword names a unit of measure or of time precision. Singular and plural spellings are two bindings on one unit concept.

    • LITERAL_KEYWORD

      public static final IkeConcept LITERAL_KEYWORD
      A lexical role: the keyword is itself a fixed value of the logic, so the binding names the literal that carries that value's bounds.

    • FUNCTION_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept FUNCTION_NAME
      A lexical role: the name of a function a logic calls with its arguments in parentheses, as CQL calls Count, Sum, Min, Max, Avg, and Median, rather than a keyword written before or between its operands. The binding is the same as an operator keyword's; only the spelling on the page differs.

    • DECLARATION_KEYWORD

      public static final IkeConcept DECLARATION_KEYWORD
      A lexical role: in a CQL library a value set, a code, or a concept is declared once by name and used many times, and the keyword that declares it introduces a thing rather than an operation. The binding records what that thing is in this model: a value set is a reference set under the view, a code names a concept, and a concept declared from several equivalent codes is one concept with identifiers in several code systems.

    • CONSTRUCT_RELATION

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRUCT_RELATION
      A relation between a construct and a core construct whose truth a check can settle, recorded so that the build runs the check. Also the meaning of the Construct Relation Pattern's second field, whose value is one of its members: Logical equivalence, Definitional extension, and Conservative extension. There is no member for "unrelated". A construct with no relation semantic is simply distinct, and recording that as a value would put a placeholder in a field. An instance's is-a to its generic parent is a different claim, the same idea at another kind, and is not a construct relation.

    • LOGICAL_EQUIVALENCE

      public static final IkeConcept LOGICAL_EQUIVALENCE
      A construct relation in which the two constructs give the same result on every input and agree on operand kind, result kind, and arity. The check is equality of results over every input: every combination where the inputs are finite, and equality over the conformance corpus for concept sets.

    • DEFINITIONAL_EXTENSION

      public static final IkeConcept DEFINITIONAL_EXTENSION
      A construct relation in which the construct can be defined using only what the core construct already says: new names, no new logic. The kinds need not agree, so a construct that computes concept sets may extend a core construct that builds classes. The check is that the construct's own evaluation equals its definition over a corpus.

    • CONSERVATIVE_EXTENSION

      public static final IkeConcept CONSERVATIVE_EXTENSION
      A construct relation in which the construct agrees with the core construct on everything the core covers, and covers more. Operand kind, result kind, and arity agree, and the added coverage is the extension. The check is agreement on every input the core covers. One construct claims it: Closed-world existence, which agrees with Existence on every set that holds a statement and adds an answer, Absent, for the empty set. The three-valued connectives that would have claimed it turned out to be ordinary measure arithmetic instead.

    • IDENTITY

      public static final IkeConcept IDENTITY
      A construct relation in which the two are one idea admitted twice, so that every claim true of one is true of the other and nothing is lost either way. It relates a type of another language to the IKE concept that is the same type, where an operator of another language would instead be admitted as the construct itself. The check is that the two carry the same values, one to one.

    • OPERAND_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept OPERAND_KIND
      The kind of thing an operator works on or yields, taken from ANF's structural definition. Also the meaning of the Construct Denotation Pattern's first field. A generic operator is typed at this root, meaning any kind. Kinds are what make a relation claim well-formed, and what tell apart two constructs that one keyword names. There is no truth-value kind: what a determination, a criterion, or a derived criterion yields is a presence measure. Its members are Class kind, Axiom kind, Concept kind, Concept set kind, Measure kind with Presence measure kind beneath it, Measure list kind, Statement kind, and Set kind with Concept set kind, Statement set kind, and Subject set kind beneath it.

    • CLASS_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_KIND
      An operand kind: the set of things a concept stands for in a model, which is what the EL++ class constructors take and yield. The EL++ layer.

    • AXIOM_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept AXIOM_KIND
      An operand kind: a terminological axiom, which is what an EL++ axiom former yields: a necessary set, a sufficient set, a disjointness, or an is-a.

    • CONCEPT_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept CONCEPT_KIND
      An operand kind: one concept of the knowledge layer, the topic of a statement, the anchor of a Descendant of or Ancestor of, and the value a CQL Code or Concept is represented as.

    • SET_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept SET_KIND
      An operand kind: a set of things of one kind, concepts, statements, or subjects. The set operations work on any of them the same way; the kind of the members rides on the operands. Its members are Concept set kind, Statement set kind, and Subject set kind.

    • CONCEPT_SET_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept CONCEPT_SET_KIND
      An operand kind: a finite set of concepts computed under a view, which is what the ECL operators and the taxonomy field constraint kinds yield, and what a topic constraint selects statements by. The topic layer.

    • MEASURE_RATIO

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_RATIO
      A numerator measure and a denominator measure, each on its own measure semantic, kept as written: 1:128 stays 1:128 and 5 mg:1 mL stays a strength rather than becoming a concentration, because the two parts mean something apart. It is the same idea as an ELM Ratio, admitted as a concept of the model.

    • MEASURE_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_KIND
      An operand kind: an ANF measure, a lower and an upper bound, the inclusivity of each, a resolution, and the measure semantic that is its frame of reference. Every value in a query over ANF is one: a result, a timing, a normal range, a CQL Quantity, Interval, Decimal, or DateTime. A range means one of two things. A measure whose measure semantic is a period on the calendar, a hospital stay, has bounds where it began and ended. A measure whose measure semantic is an instant on the calendar, an onset, or any quantity, has bounds where the value could be. Every relation on measures is decided the same way: Present when the answer is yes for every value the ranges allow, Absent when it is no for every one, and Indeterminate when it is yes for some and no for others. A relation between two periods is therefore decided outright, and it is Indeterminate only when an end known to a coarse resolution, a discharge known to the day, straddles the other's boundary. Two measures can be compared when both are on one scale, as an instant and a period on the calendar are; Measure conversion puts two on one scale when the knowledge layer has a rule between their measure semantics. The measure semantic of a measure operator's result must be a concept the knowledge layer already defines.

    • PRESENCE_MEASURE_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept PRESENCE_MEASURE_KIND
      A measure kind: a measure on the Presence semantic, whose value is one of three. Present: the determination found the topic present. Absent: it found the topic absent. Indeterminate: it could not tell. It is what a determination records, what a comparison, a criterion, or a derived criterion yields, and what a CQL Boolean is represented as: "true" is Present, "false" is Absent, and "null" is Indeterminate when it stands for a determination that did not resolve. Like every measure it has two bounds, and Indeterminate is the value whose bounds cover the whole presence frame, both points at once, so it is a value with width and not a third truth value. The presence layer.

    • STATEMENT_SET_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept STATEMENT_SET_KIND
      An operand kind: a set of ANF statements, which is what a retrieve yields and what a filter narrows. Each statement carries its topic, its circumstance, one result measure with its cross-cutting measurements, and its subject. Every stored value has definite bounds, and a criterion over them yields a presence value that may be Present, Absent, or Indeterminate. The statement layer.

    • STATEMENT_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept STATEMENT_KIND
      An operand kind: one ANF statement, which is what a criterion tests.

    • SUBJECT_SET_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept SUBJECT_SET_KIND
      An operand kind: a set of subjects of record, which is what a query over ANF ultimately answers with, the subjects for which a statement set is not empty.

    • MEASURE_LIST_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_LIST_KIND
      An operand kind: a list of measures on one measure semantic, one entry per statement, in which the same value appears as many times as statements recorded it. It is what a Measure projection produces and what a measure aggregate takes, and it is a list rather than a set because a sum or a mean must count every statement.

    • ARITY

      public static final IkeConcept ARITY
      How many operands an operator takes. A concept rather than a number, so that "any number" is a value and not a placeholder. A literal takes no operands and has no arity; it carries a literal denotation instead. Its members are Unary, Binary, and Variadic.

    • UNARY

      public static final IkeConcept UNARY
      An arity: one operand. An operator with a fixed parameter, such as the attribute of an existential restriction, the concept set of a topic constraint, or the criterion of a filter, is unary in its operand.

    • BINARY

      public static final IkeConcept BINARY
      An arity: two operands.

    • VARIADIC

      public static final IkeConcept VARIADIC
      An arity: any number of operands, as with the EL++ set formers and the concept-set and statement-set ANDs and ORs.

    • BINDING_LANGUAGE

      public static final IkeConcept BINDING_LANGUAGE
      The logic a keyword binding admits the named construct, kind, or literal to.

    • KEYWORD_TEXT

      public static final IkeConcept KEYWORD_TEXT
      The spelling in the binding logic, exactly as written, with the case the logic's grammar uses. Also the text of the dialect-scoped name the same declaration produces.

    • CORE_CONSTRUCT

      public static final IkeConcept CORE_CONSTRUCT
      The construct a relation assertion relates the extending construct to: a construct of the EL++ core.

    • RESULT_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept RESULT_KIND
      The operand kind of the result a construct or a literal yields.

    • LOWER_BOUND_VALUE

      public static final IkeConcept LOWER_BOUND_VALUE
      The lower bound of a literal's measure, as a whole number on the result kind's scale: 0 or 1 on the Presence semantic.

    • UPPER_BOUND_VALUE

      public static final IkeConcept UPPER_BOUND_VALUE
      The upper bound of a literal's measure, as a whole number on the result kind's scale. Equal to the lower bound for Present and Absent, one greater for Indeterminate.

    • KEYWORD_BINDING

      public static final IkeConcept KEYWORD_BINDING
      What an Expression Language Keyword Pattern semantic is: one spelling, in one logic, of one construct, kind, or literal.

    • CONSTRUCT_ADMISSION

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRUCT_ADMISSION
      Why a keyword binding exists: to admit what it names to the logic's allowed set. Identity is enforced at admission by checking what the construct takes and yields.

    • LANGUAGE_MEMBERSHIP

      public static final IkeConcept LANGUAGE_MEMBERSHIP
      Why the Binding language field is recorded: the logic's allowed constructs are exactly the constructs its bindings name.

    • SURFACE_SPELLING

      public static final IkeConcept SURFACE_SPELLING
      Why the Keyword text field is recorded: the spelling in the logic, so that spelling variants are two bindings on one construct, and one spelling naming two constructs is visible.

    • GRAMMATICAL_PLACEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept GRAMMATICAL_PLACEMENT
      Why the Lexical role field is recorded: where in the logic's grammar the keyword stands, and so what kind of thing the binding names.

    • CONSTRUCT_DENOTATION

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRUCT_DENOTATION
      What a Construct Denotation Pattern semantic is: what one operator takes and what it yields, recorded as operand kind, result kind, and arity.

    • WELL_TYPED_RELATION

      public static final IkeConcept WELL_TYPED_RELATION
      Why a denotation exists: a relation between two constructs is a claim only when both sides say what they take and yield; the kinds decide which relations are even possible; and one keyword naming two constructs is legitimate only when their operand kinds differ.

    • OPERAND_TYPING

      public static final IkeConcept OPERAND_TYPING
      Why the Operand kind field is recorded: what the operator takes.

    • RESULT_TYPING

      public static final IkeConcept RESULT_TYPING
      Why the Result kind field is recorded: what the operator yields. The result kind also decides which check runs: every combination of the three presence values for presence measures, and corpus equality for concept sets.

    • OPERAND_COUNT

      public static final IkeConcept OPERAND_COUNT
      Why the Arity field is recorded: how many operands the operator takes.

    • LITERAL_DENOTATION

      public static final IkeConcept LITERAL_DENOTATION
      What a Literal Denotation Pattern semantic is: the kind and the bounds of one literal, a fixed value of the query language.

    • FIXED_VALUE

      public static final IkeConcept FIXED_VALUE
      Why a literal denotation exists: a literal is a value, not an operator, so what is recorded is its bounds rather than what it takes and yields. A logic's literal keyword then names bounds, which is how CQL's "true", "false", and "null" become Present, Absent, and Indeterminate as data the gate can check.

    • LITERAL_LOWER_BOUND

      public static final IkeConcept LITERAL_LOWER_BOUND
      Why the literal's lower bound is recorded: the low end of the value it stands for.

    • LITERAL_UPPER_BOUND

      public static final IkeConcept LITERAL_UPPER_BOUND
      Why the literal's upper bound is recorded: the high end of the value it stands for.

    • CONSTRUCT_RELATION_ASSERTION

      public static final IkeConcept CONSTRUCT_RELATION_ASSERTION
      What a Construct Relation Pattern semantic is: a checked claim that the referenced construct bears the named relation to the core construct.

    • CHECKED_RELATION

      public static final IkeConcept CHECKED_RELATION
      Why a relation assertion exists: to record a claim of the kind a proof can settle, whose check the build runs, in place of an editorial correspondence.

    • RELATION_TARGET

      public static final IkeConcept RELATION_TARGET
      Why the Core construct field is recorded: which core construct the claim is about.

    • RELATION_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept RELATION_KIND
      Why the Construct relation field is recorded: which of the three checked relations is claimed, and therefore which check runs.

    • GENERIC_AND

      public static final IkeConcept GENERIC_AND
      A connective operator that joins two or more operands of one kind into a result of that same kind. The operation combines all of the operands to produce the result, and their order and grouping make no difference. AND means every operand is required, not just some of them, so the result is only what is all of the operands at once. Adding another operand can only narrow the result, never widen it. Each descendant applies this to one kind of operand: EL++ AND builds the class of things that belong to every operand class at once, Set AND keeps the members found in every operand set, whatever kind of thing they are, and Presence AND is Present only when every operand is Present.

    • LOGICAL_EXPRESSION_VERTEX

      public static final IkeConcept LOGICAL_EXPRESSION_VERTEX
      The kinds of node in an EL++ expression tree that are not operators: the definition root that anchors an expression, and the concept reference that names a class. Their inherited home beside the connectives was a filing accident.

    • INDETERMINATE_RESULT

      public static final IkeConcept INDETERMINATE_RESULT
      An indeterminate result means a determination was performed but could not arrive at a value within its frame of reference. The frame of reference is what the measure semantic names: millimoles per liter for a serum sodium, present or absent for a finding on a film, the calendar for a date. The result covers the whole frame: it says the determination was done, and no more. It is a fact about this determination only; a later determination may succeed. It is never a stand-in for missing information. A result that was not sought, or was sought and not obtained, is recorded as the disposition of the act. The reason is an associated statement. A subject with no statement at all simply has no record here.

    • PRESENT_LITERAL

      public static final IkeConcept PRESENT_LITERAL
      One of the three presence values: the determination found the topic present. The value CQL's "true" names.

    • ABSENT_LITERAL

      public static final IkeConcept ABSENT_LITERAL
      One of the three presence values: the determination found the topic absent. Absent is a finding, not a gap: a subject with no statement on the topic has no record, not an Absent. The value CQL's "false" names.

    • INDETERMINATE_LITERAL

      public static final IkeConcept INDETERMINATE_LITERAL
      An indeterminate result on the presence frame of reference, and one of the three presence values: the determination could not tell whether the topic was present or absent. It arises in two ways. A determination may report it directly, as with a test read in its equivocal zone. Or it may come from comparing a recorded range with a threshold or a date inside that range: an HbA1c recorded between 8.5 and 9.5 against a threshold of 9, or a determination dated to sometime in March against the 15th. Any measure a statement carries can be recorded as a range, so any of them can produce it, and the answer carries the measure that produced it, so the reader can see why. It is the one presence value that NOT leaves unchanged, and it is what CQL's "null" becomes when "null" stands for a determination that was performed and did not resolve.

    • PRESENCE_AND

      public static final IkeConcept PRESENCE_AND
      A connective operator that joins two or more presence values into one, in any order; every one of them is required. The result is Present if every operand is Present, Absent if any operand is Absent, and Indeterminate otherwise. This is exactly how CQL's "and" behaves over "true", "false", and "null", which is why CQL's "and" names it. It combines criteria; Set AND combines the sets a filter has produced.

    • PRESENCE_OR

      public static final IkeConcept PRESENCE_OR
      A connective operator that joins two or more presence values into one, in any order; any one of them is enough. The result is Present if any operand is Present, Absent if every operand is Absent, and Indeterminate otherwise. This is exactly how CQL's "or" behaves over "true", "false", and "null", which is why CQL's "or" names it. It combines criteria; Set OR combines the sets a filter has produced.

    • PRESENCE_NOT

      public static final IkeConcept PRESENCE_NOT
      A connective operator on one presence value that turns Present into Absent and Absent into Present, and leaves Indeterminate as it is, because the opposite of could not tell is still could not tell. This is exactly how CQL's "not" behaves over "true", "false", and "null", which is why CQL's "not" names it. NOT belongs to the query, not to the record: a determination that found the topic absent is stored as Absent, never as NOT Present. It is not a subtraction of one set from another, which is Set difference, and it has no generic parent, because EL++ has no NOT.

    • PRESENCE_IMPLICATION

      public static final IkeConcept PRESENCE_IMPLICATION
      A connective operator on two presence values: Present when the first is Absent or the second is Present, Absent when the first is Present and the second is Absent, and Indeterminate otherwise. It is Presence NOT of the first joined by Presence OR with the second, so it is definable from Presence OR. CQL's "implies" is this, and its nine-row table follows from the bounds.

    • PRESENCE_EXCLUSIVE_OR

      public static final IkeConcept PRESENCE_EXCLUSIVE_OR
      A connective operator on two presence values: Present when one is Present and the other Absent, Absent when both are Present or both are Absent, and Indeterminate when either is Indeterminate. It is Presence OR of the two joined by Presence AND with Presence NOT of their Presence AND, so it is definable from Presence AND. CQL's "xor" is this, and its nine-row table follows from the bounds.

    • CONDITIONAL

      public static final IkeConcept CONDITIONAL
      An if-then-else: a value chosen by a condition, with any number of further conditions and a fallback, every branch of one kind. An if-then-else needs a yes or a no, and in this model a comparison can also come out Indeterminate, so each condition is a comparison on the presence semantic that names which outcomes take its branch, Present alone or Present and Indeterminate together, and is therefore always decided. A bare comparison that could come out Indeterminate is not accepted, for the reason a filter does not accept one. An author who wants the middle in a branch of its own adds a condition for Indeterminate alone and gives that branch what fits: for measures, the widest range the two branches allow; for concepts, both, as candidates. CQL's "if" and "case" are this with Present fixed as the outcome that takes the branch and never written down, so an Indeterminate condition goes to the else branch, and the binding records that as data.

    • MEASURE_WITHIN

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_WITHIN
      An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the first is inside the second. Present when every value the first allows is inside the second, Absent when none is, and Indeterminate when some are and some are not. A stay that ran past the end of a period is Absent. An onset recorded as March 2024, against a period that ends in the middle of March, is Indeterminate. A result is inside its own normal range when the whole range of the result is inside. It serves CQL's "included in", "during", "between", "in", and "within" alike, because a timing is a measure; "within 7 days of" an admission is this relation against the admission widened by 7 days each way, which Measure addition of minus 7 to plus 7 days produces. The result and the normal range are two cross-cutting measurements of one statement, and that relation can be decided only with the statement's own range.

    • MEASURE_CONTAINS

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_CONTAINS
      An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the first encloses the second. Measure within with the operands swapped.

    • MEASURE_OVERLAPS

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_OVERLAPS
      An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the two share any of the scale. Two stays that shared a day are Present, and two that did not are Absent; a stay whose discharge is known only to the day, against a period that begins in the middle of that day, is Indeterminate. For a moment against a period the question becomes whether the moment is inside the period, which is Measure within.

    • MEASURE_BEFORE

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_BEFORE
      An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the first is entirely earlier, or lower, than the second. For two periods, Present when the first ended before the second began, and Absent otherwise. For a value known to a range, Present when the upper bound of the first is below the lower bound of the second, Absent when the lower bound of the first is not below the upper bound of the second, and Indeterminate otherwise: an onset known only to a month is before a date when every day of that month is earlier. It decides the same way as Less than on every pair of measures, and the set asserts that equivalence. CQL's "before"; "on or before" and "before or on" are Less than or equal to.

    • MEASURE_AFTER

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_AFTER
      An operator on two measures on one scale that yields a presence value: whether the first is entirely later, or higher, than the second. Measure before with the operands swapped, and Greater than by the same equivalence. CQL's "after"; "on or after" and "after or on" are Greater than or equal to, and "30 days or more after" a discharge is Greater than or equal to against the discharge plus 30 days.

    • MEASURE_OPERATOR

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_OPERATOR
      An operator that produces a measure from one or more measures. A measure is a range with a lower and an upper bound on a measure semantic, so a measure operator works on the whole range, never on one number picked from inside it, and it never guesses how likely any value inside the range is. A single value is a measure whose two bounds are equal. The measure semantic of the result is the concept the knowledge layer defines for that operation on the operands' measure semantics: millimoles per liter less millimoles per liter is millimoles per liter, one date less another is a length of time, and milligrams per deciliter times deciliters is milligrams, each because a concept in the knowledge layer defines that combination, and where none does the operation is refused. The result's resolution is the coarsest among the operands. A comparison or a measure relation answers a question about measures with Present, Absent, or Indeterminate; a measure operator produces a value on a scale. Presence has no arithmetic, because its measure semantic defines none, so the connectives are the only operations on presence values. Its members are Measure addition, Measure subtraction, Measure multiplication, Measure division, Measure lower bound, Measure upper bound, Measure width, Measure whole unit, Measure outer span, Measure inner span, Measure conversion, and Measure aggregate, which works over a list of measures.

    • MEASURE_ADDITION

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_ADDITION
      A measure operator that adds two or more measures, in any order. The lower bound of the result is the lower bounds added together, and the upper bound is the upper bounds added together. An end of the result is included only when every end that produced it is included. An operand that is Indeterminate contributes its whole frame, so the sum still says at least how much: a total daily dose with one dose Indeterminate is at least the sum of the known doses. The sum is Indeterminate only when its own bounds cover its whole frame. CQL's "+" is this addition; CQL adds single values, and there the two agree.

    • MEASURE_SUBTRACTION

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_SUBTRACTION
      A measure operator that takes the second of two measures away from the first. The lower bound of the result is the first's lower bound less the second's upper bound, and the upper bound is the first's upper bound less the second's lower bound: the smallest and the largest difference the two ranges allow. An HbA1c recorded as 8.5 to 9.5, less a threshold of 9, is minus 0.5 to plus 0.5, so a query can say at most half a point above and possibly not above at all, which is all the record supports. A date is a measure on the calendar, so one date less another is a length of time in the unit the query names. CQL's "-" is this subtraction, and CQL's "duration in days between" two dates is this subtraction read in whole days, as it is for any unit of fixed length; a duration in months or years depends on the calendar and is not this subtraction. CQL's "difference in days between" two dates is this subtraction of the starts of their whole days, which is why it counts the day boundaries crossed.

    • MEASURE_MULTIPLICATION

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_MULTIPLICATION
      A measure operator that multiplies two or more measures, in any order. The bounds of the result are the smallest and the largest product that can be made from one bound of each operand. An operand that is Indeterminate contributes its whole frame, and the product is Indeterminate only when its own bounds cover its whole frame. CQL's "*" is this multiplication.

    • MEASURE_DIVISION

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_DIVISION
      A measure operator that divides the first of two measures by the second. The bounds of the result are the smallest and the largest quotient that can be made from one bound of each operand. Dividing by a measure whose range includes zero gives Indeterminate, since the quotient could then be any value at all. CQL's "/" is this division.

    • MEASURE_LOWER_BOUND

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_LOWER_BOUND
      A measure operator that gives the lowest value inside a measure as a single value on the same measure semantic: the lower bound when it is included, and otherwise the first value above it at the measure's resolution. CQL's "start of" an interval is this.

    • MEASURE_UPPER_BOUND

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_UPPER_BOUND
      A measure operator that gives the highest value inside a measure as a single value on the same measure semantic: the upper bound when it is included, and otherwise the first value below it at the measure's resolution. CQL's "end of" an interval is this.

    • MEASURE_WIDTH

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_WIDTH
      A measure operator that gives how wide a measure's range is, the upper bound less the lower bound, as a single value on the measure semantic the knowledge layer defines for a difference on that scale: for a range of dates, a length of time. It is how a query asks how uncertain a result is. CQL's "width of" an interval is this, and CQL's "duration in days of" an interval is this read in whole days.

    • MEASURE_WHOLE_UNIT

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_WHOLE_UNIT
      A measure operator that gives the whole unit of a named size that a measure occupies: the day of a timestamp is the whole day, from midnight to midnight, the month of a date is the whole month, and a range that touches two days becomes those two whole days. It is not division into equal buckets counted from zero: a day, a month, and a year are units of the calendar, defined in the knowledge layer, and a month varies in length. Every precision-based comparison uses it: CQL's "same day as" is Equal to on the whole days, "before day of" is Measure before on them, and "date from" a timestamp is the whole day, the one keyword bound to this operator. The whole day of a timestamp depends on the zone: it takes the timing's own zone when it has one and the query's zone otherwise.

    • MEASURE_OUTER_SPAN

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_OUTER_SPAN
      A measure operator that takes two measures on one scale and gives the period from the earliest value the first allows to the latest value the second allows. For a dispense date and that date plus its days supply, it is everything that might have been covered. When both are single values it is the period from the first to the second, which is what CQL's Interval constructor builds. ANF's period has two bounds and cannot hold an end that is itself a range, so the outer span and the inner span together are what an uncertain end becomes.

    • MEASURE_INNER_SPAN

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_INNER_SPAN
      A measure operator that takes two measures on one scale and gives the period from the latest value the first allows to the earliest value the second allows: what was certainly covered, and nothing at all when those two cross. When both are single values it is the same period as the outer span. Counting days over inner spans gives at least how many were covered, and over outer spans at most.

    • MEASURE_CONVERSION

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_CONVERSION
      A measure operator that converts a measure from one unit to another: a weight recorded in grams given in kilograms, a glucose in milligrams per decilitre given in millimoles per litre. The result is a new measure whose measure semantic is the target unit, a value inside the query as a sum or a difference is; nothing is written, and the statement's recorded measure is unchanged. It needs a rule between the two units that the knowledge layer defines, the way a unit with a measurement basis is defined. Where the rule is a fixed factor and offset, grams to kilograms, milliseconds to seconds, Fahrenheit to Celsius, milligrams per decilitre to millimoles per litre for a named substance by its molar mass, the bounds and the resolution are scaled exactly and nothing is lost. Where the rule carries a width of its own, the HbA1c master equation between the percentage and the millimoles-per-mole scale, the result widens by that width. Where the knowledge layer has no rule, the conversion is refused. It is Measure multiplication by the factor and Measure addition of the offset, so it is definable from Measure multiplication. CQL's "convert ... to" is this; "as" and "cast" change a value's type, and kinds here are fixed before a query runs, so they are not bound.

    • MEASURE_AGGREGATE

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_AGGREGATE
      A measure operator that produces one measure from a list of measures. Every member counts unless the aggregate is set to count only the members that arrived at a value, those that are not Indeterminate, the way a filter's criteria say which outcomes count. Each member of this family is exact on ranges for one reason: none of them can go down when a member goes up, so the aggregate of all the low ends and the aggregate of all the high ends are the ends of the true range, and count is exact outright. CQL's aggregate functions skip null, so each binds with the choice fixed to members with a value and never written down. Its members are Measure count, Measure sum, Measure least, Measure greatest, Measure mean, Measure median, Measure all present, Measure any present, Closed-world all present, and Closed-world any present.

    • MEASURE_COUNT

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_COUNT
      A measure aggregate that gives how many members count, as a single value whose measure semantic is a count of statements. Set to count only members with a value, it gives how many statements arrived at one. CQL's Count is this with that choice fixed.

    • MEASURE_SUM

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_SUM
      A measure aggregate that adds every member that counts, Measure addition across the list: the low ends added together to the high ends added together, on the members' measure semantic. A total daily dose with one dose Indeterminate is at least the sum of the known doses. CQL's Sum is this with members with a value fixed.

    • MEASURE_LEAST

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_LEAST
      A measure aggregate that gives the least value among the members that count: from the lowest of the low ends to the lowest of the high ends. HbA1c results of 7.0 to 8.0 and exactly 7.5 have a least result between 7.0 and 7.5. An Indeterminate member that counts puts the low end at the bottom of the frame. CQL's Min is this with members with a value fixed.

    • MEASURE_GREATEST

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_GREATEST
      A measure aggregate that gives the greatest value among the members that count: from the highest of the low ends to the highest of the high ends. The same results have a greatest result between 7.5 and 8.0. An Indeterminate member that counts puts the high end at the top of the frame. CQL's Max is this with members with a value fixed.

    • MEASURE_MEAN

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_MEAN
      A measure aggregate that gives the mean of the members that count: from the mean of the low ends to the mean of the high ends. An Indeterminate member widens the mean by its share of the frame, a third of it among three. CQL's Avg is this with members with a value fixed.

    • MEASURE_MEDIAN

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_MEDIAN
      A measure aggregate that gives the median of the members that count: from the median of the low ends to the median of the high ends. CQL's Median is this with members with a value fixed.

    • MEASURE_ALL_PRESENT

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_ALL_PRESENT
      A measure aggregate over presence values, Presence AND across a list: Present when every member that counts is Present, Absent when any member is Absent, and Indeterminate otherwise; with no member it comes out with nothing, as Existence does on an empty set. The list is the outcomes of one determination across many statements, every screening question in a set answered yes. It takes the aggregate's choice of which members count, every member or only those with a value.

    • MEASURE_ANY_PRESENT

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_ANY_PRESENT
      A measure aggregate over presence values, Presence OR across a list: Present when any member that counts is Present, Absent when every member is Absent, and Indeterminate otherwise; with no member it comes out with nothing. Existence is Presence OR of a criterion across a set of statements, and this is Presence OR across a list of measures, one idea at two kinds, the way one AND has three places. It takes the aggregate's choice of which members count.

    • CLOSED_WORLD_ALL_PRESENT

      public static final IkeConcept CLOSED_WORLD_ALL_PRESENT
      Measure all present read as if the store held the whole world: with no member it comes out Present instead of nothing, since nothing was found Absent. It agrees with Measure all present wherever that has an answer and differs only on the empty list, which makes it a conservative extension. CQL's AllTrue is this with the choice of members fixed to those with a value, which is how CQL skips null.

    • CLOSED_WORLD_ANY_PRESENT

      public static final IkeConcept CLOSED_WORLD_ANY_PRESENT
      Measure any present read as if the store held the whole world: with no member it comes out Absent instead of nothing, since nothing was found Present. It agrees with Measure any present wherever that has an answer and differs only on the empty list, which makes it a conservative extension. CQL's AnyTrue is this with the choice of members fixed to those with a value.

    • MEASURE_LIST_OPERATOR

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_LIST_OPERATOR
      An operator that produces a list of measures from a list of measures, the measures of a set of statements gathered by a Measure projection.
