The search is linear, and returns the index of the first element for which the equality comparison returns true. If the list is empty, or no element is found, the result is -1. If either argument is null, the result is null.

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_FLATTEN

    • ELM_SORT

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SORT

If the argument is null, the result is null.

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_FOREACH
      From the ELM specification: The ForEach expression iterates over the list of elements in the source element, and returns a list with the same number of elements, where each element in the new list is the result of evaluating the element expression for each element in the source list. If the element argument evaluates to null for some item in the source list, the resulting list will contain a null for that element.

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DISTINCT

The operator uses equality comparison semantics as defined in the Equal operator, with the exception that nulls are considered equal for the purposes of distinct determination. This means that multiple nulls in the input will result in a single null in the output. If the source argument is null, the result is null.

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CURRENT

Scopes are introduced by the named scoping operators (Filter, ForEach, and Repeat), the implicit scoping operators (Sort and Aggregate) as well as introduced within Queries by the AliasedQuerySource, LetClause, AggregateClause, and SortClause elements. It is an error to invoke the Current operator outside of a scoped operation.

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ITERATION

Scopes are introduced by the named scoping operators (Filter, ForEach, and Repeat), the implicit scoping operators (Sort and Aggregate) as well as introduced within Queries by the AliasedQuerySource, LetClause, AggregateClause, and SortClause elements.       public static final IkeConcept ELM_SINGLETONFROM

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_AGGREGATEEXPRESSION
      From the ELM specification: Aggregate expressions perform operations on lists of data, either directly on a list of scalars, or indirectly on a list of objects, with a reference to a property present on each object in the list. For example, in a Sum over Dose, any instance of Medication with no value for Dose would be ignored. An aggregate operation performed over an empty list is defined to return null, except as noted in the documentation for each operator (Count, AllTrue, and AnyTrue are the exceptions). The schema marks it abstract: a tree never holds it directly, only one of the types that extend it.

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_MAX

If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_GEOMETRICMEAN

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_GEOMETRICMEAN
      From the ELM specification: The GeometricMean operator returns the geometric mean of the non-null elements in source. If a path is specified, elements with no value for the property specified by the path are ignored. If the source contains no non-null elements, null is returned. If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_MEDIAN

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_MEDIAN
      From the ELM specification: The Median operator returns the median of the elements in source. If a path is specified, elements with no value for the property specified by the path are ignored. If the source contains no non-null elements, null is returned. If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_MODE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_MODE
      From the ELM specification: The Mode operator returns the statistical mode of the elements in source. If a path is specified, elements with no value for the property specified by the path are ignored. If the source contains no non-null elements, null is returned. If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_VARIANCE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_VARIANCE
      From the ELM specification: The Variance operator returns the statistical variance of the elements in source. If a path is specified, elements with no value for the property specified by the path are ignored. If the source contains no non-null elements, null is returned. If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_POPULATIONVARIANCE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_POPULATIONVARIANCE
      From the ELM specification: The PopulationVariance operator returns the statistical population variance of the elements in source. If a path is specified, elements with no value for the property specified by the path are ignored. If the source contains no non-null elements, null is returned. If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_STDDEV

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_STDDEV
      From the ELM specification: The StdDev operator returns the statistical standard deviation of the elements in source. If a path is specified, elements with no value for the property specified by the path are ignored. If the source contains no non-null elements, null is returned. If the list is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_POPULATIONSTDDEV

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_POPULATIONSTDDEV
      From the ELM specification: The PopulationStdDev operator returns the statistical standard deviation of the elements in source. If a path is specified, elements with no value for the property specified by the path are ignored. If the source contains no non-null elements, null is returned. If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_ALLTRUE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ALLTRUE
      From the ELM specification: The AllTrue operator returns true if all the non-null elements in source are true. If a path is specified, elements with no value for the property specified by the path are ignored. If the source contains no non-null elements, true is returned. If the source is null, the result is true.

    • ELM_ANYTRUE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ANYTRUE
      From the ELM specification: The AnyTrue operator returns true if any non-null element in source is true. If a path is specified, elements with no value for the property specified by the path are ignored. If the source contains no non-null elements, false is returned. If the source is null, the result is false.

    • ELM_PROPERTY

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_PROPERTY
      From the ELM specification: The Property operator returns the value of the property on the source (or named scope) specified by the path attribute. If the result of evaluating source (or the named scope) is null, the result is null. The path attribute may include qualifiers (.) and indexers ([x]). Indexers must be literal integer values. If the path attribute contains qualifiers or indexers, each qualifier or indexer is traversed to obtain the actual value. If the object of the property access at any point in traversing the path is null, the result is null. If a scope is specified, the name is used to resolve the scope in which the path will be resolved. Scopes can be named by the scoping operators (Filter, ForEach, Repeat, and Sort) as well as introduced within a Query through the AliasedQuerySource, LetClause, AggregateClause, and SortClause. Property expressions can also be used to access the individual points and closed indicators for interval types using the property names low, high, lowClosed, and highClosed.

    • ELM_ALIASEDQUERYSOURCE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ALIASEDQUERYSOURCE
      From the ELM specification: The AliasedQuerySource element defines a single source for inclusion in a query scope. The type of the source is determined by the expression element, and the source can be accessed within the query scope by the given alias.

    • ELM_LETCLAUSE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LETCLAUSE
      From the ELM specification: The LetClause element allows any number of expression definitions to be introduced within a query scope. Defined expressions can be referenced by name within the query scope.

    • ELM_RELATIONSHIPCLAUSE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_RELATIONSHIPCLAUSE
      From the ELM specification: The RelationshipClause element allows related sources to be used to restrict the elements included from another source in a query scope. Note that the elements referenced by the relationship clause can only be accessed within the suchThat condition, and that elements of the related source are not included in the query scope. The schema marks it abstract: a tree never holds it directly, only one of the types that extend it.

    • ELM_WITH

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_WITH
      From the ELM specification: The With clause restricts the elements of a given source to only those elements that have elements in the related source that satisfy the suchThat condition. This operation is known as a semi-join in database languages.

    • ELM_WITHOUT

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_WITHOUT
      From the ELM specification: The Without clause restricts the elements of a given source to only those elements that do not have elements in the related source that satisfy the suchThat condition. This operation is known as a semi-difference in database languages.

    • ELM_SORTBYITEM

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SORTBYITEM
      A type of the ELM specification; the schema gives no description. The schema marks it abstract: a tree never holds it directly, only one of the types that extend it.

    • ELM_BYDIRECTION

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_BYDIRECTION
      From the ELM specification: The ByDirection element specifies that the sort should be performed using the given direction. This approach is used when the result of the query is a list of non-tuple elements and only the sort direction needs to be specified.

    • ELM_BYCOLUMN

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_BYCOLUMN
      From the ELM specification: The ByColumn element specifies that the sort should be performed using the given column and direction. This approach is used to specify the sort order for a query when the result is a list of tuples.

    • ELM_BYEXPRESSION

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_BYEXPRESSION
      From the ELM specification: The ByExpression element specifies that the sort should be performed using the given expression and direction. This approach is used to specify the sort order as a calculated expression. Within the expression, the iteration accessor $this can be used to access the current iteration value, and $index can be used to access the 0-based index of the current iteration.

    • ELM_SORTCLAUSE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SORTCLAUSE
      From the ELM specification: The SortClause element defines the sort order for the query.

    • ELM_RETURNCLAUSE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_RETURNCLAUSE
      From the ELM specification: The ReturnClause element defines the shape of the result set of the query.

    • ELM_AGGREGATECLAUSE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_AGGREGATECLAUSE
      From the ELM specification: The AggregateClause element defines the result of the query in terms of an aggregation expression performed for each item in the query.

    • ELM_QUERY

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_QUERY
      From the ELM specification: The Query operator represents a clause-based query. The result of the query is determined by the type of sources included, as well as the clauses used in the query.

    • ELM_ALIASREF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ALIASREF
      From the ELM specification: The AliasRef expression allows for the reference of a specific source within the scope of a query.

    • ELM_QUERYLETREF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_QUERYLETREF
      From the ELM specification: The QueryLetRef expression allows for the reference of a specific let definition within the scope of a query.

    • ELM_CHILDREN

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CHILDREN
      From the ELM specification: For structured types, the Children operator returns a list of all the values of the elements of the type. List-valued elements are expanded and added to the result individually, rather than as a single list. For list types, the result is the same as invoking Children on each element in the list and flattening the resulting lists into a single result. If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_DESCENDANTS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DESCENDANTS
      From the ELM specification: For structured types, the Descendants operator returns a list of all the values of the elements of the type, recursively. List-valued elements are expanded and added to the result individually, rather than as a single list. For list types, the result is the same as invoking Descendants on each element in the list and flattening the resulting lists into a single result. If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_DESCENDENTS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DESCENDENTS
      From the ELM specification: DEPRECATED: Use Descendants. For structured types, the Descendents operator returns a list of all the values of the elements of the type, recursively. List-valued elements are expanded and added to the result individually, rather than as a single list. For list types, the result is the same as invoking Descendents on each element in the list and flattening the resulting lists into a single result. If the source is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_MESSAGE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_MESSAGE
      From the ELM specification: The Message operator is used to support errors, warnings, messages, and tracing in an ELM evaluation environment. The operator is defined to return the input source. If the severity is Error, the operator is expected to raise a run-time error and return the message to the calling environment. This is the only severity that stops processing. All other severities continue evaluation of the expression. If the severity is Trace, the operator is expected to make the message available to a tracing mechanism such as a debug log in the calling environment. If the severity is Warning, the operator is expected to provide the message as a warning to the calling environment. If the severity is Message, the operator is expected to provide the message as information to the calling environment.

    • ELM_CODEFILTERELEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CODEFILTERELEMENT
      From the ELM specification: The CodeFilterElement type specifies a terminology filter criteria for use within a retrieve, specified as either [property] [comparator] [value] or [search] [comparator] [value].

    • ELM_DATEFILTERELEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATEFILTERELEMENT
      From the ELM specification: The DateFilterElement type specifies a date-valued filter criteria for use within a retrieve, specified as either a date-valued [property], a date-value [lowProperty] and [highProperty] or a [search], and an expression that evaluates to a date or time type, an interval of a date or time type, or a time-valued Quantity.

    • ELM_OTHERFILTERELEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_OTHERFILTERELEMENT
      From the ELM specification: The OtherFilterElement type specifies an arbitrarily-typed filter criteria for use within a retrieve, specified as either [property] [comparator] [value] or [search] [comparator] [value].

    • ELM_INCLUDEELEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_INCLUDEELEMENT
      From the ELM specification: The IncludeElement type specifies include information for an include within a retrieve.

    • ELM_RETRIEVE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_RETRIEVE
      From the ELM specification: The retrieve expression defines clinical data that will be used by the artifact. This expression allows clinically relevant filtering criteria to be provided in a well-defined and computable way. This operation defines the integration boundary for artifacts. The result of a retrieve is defined to return the same data for subsequent invocations within the same evaluation request. This means in particular that patient data updates made during the evaluation request are not visible to the artifact. In effect, the patient data is a snapshot of the data as of the start of the evaluation. This ensures strict deterministic and functional behavior of the artifact, and allows the implementation engine freedom to cache intermediate results in order to improve performance.

    • ELM_SEARCH

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SEARCH
      From the ELM specification: The Search operation provides an operator that returns the result of an indexing expression on an instance. It is effectively the same as a property access, but uses the name of a defined search on the type, rather than the name of a property on the class.

    • ELM_CODESYSTEMDEF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CODESYSTEMDEF
      From the ELM specification: The CodeSystemDef type defines a code system identifier that can then be used to identify code systems involved in value set definitions.

    • ELM_VALUESETDEF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_VALUESETDEF
      From the ELM specification: The ValueSetDef type defines a value set identifier that can be referenced by name anywhere within an expression. The id specifies the globally unique identifier for the value set. This may be an HL7 OID, a FHIR URL, or a CTS2 value set URL. If version is specified, it will be used to resolve the version of the value set definition to be used. Otherwise, the most current published version of the value set is assumed. If codeSystems are specified, they will be used to resolve the code systems used within the value set definition to construct the expansion set. Note that the recommended approach to statically binding to an expansion set is to use a value set definition that specifies the version of each code system used. The codeSystemVersions attribute is provided only to ensure static binding can be achieved when the value set definition does not specify code system versions as part of the definition header.

    • ELM_CODEDEF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CODEDEF
      From the ELM specification: The CodeDef type defines a code identifier that can then be used to reference single codes anywhere within an expression.

    • ELM_CONCEPTDEF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CONCEPTDEF
      From the ELM specification: The ConceptDef type defines a concept identifier that can then be used to reference single concepts anywhere within an expression.

    • ELM_CODESYSTEMREF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CODESYSTEMREF
      From the ELM specification: The CodeSystemRef expression allows a previously defined named code system to be referenced within an expression. Conceptually, referencing a code system returns the set of codes in the code system. Note that this operation should almost never be performed in practice. Code system references are allowed in order to allow for testing of code membership in a particular code system.

    • ELM_VALUESETREF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_VALUESETREF
      From the ELM specification: The ValueSetRef expression allows a previously defined named value set to be referenced within an expression. Conceptually, referencing a value set returns the expansion set for the value set as a list of codes.

    • ELM_CODEREF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CODEREF
      From the ELM specification: The CodeRef expression allows a previously defined code to be referenced within an expression.

    • ELM_CONCEPTREF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CONCEPTREF
      From the ELM specification: The ConceptRef expression allows a previously defined concept to be referenced within an expression.

    • ELM_CODE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CODE
      From the ELM specification: The Code type represents a literal code selector.

    • ELM_CONCEPT

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CONCEPT
      From the ELM specification: The Concept type represents a literal concept selector.

    • ELM_INCODESYSTEM

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_INCODESYSTEM
      From the ELM specification: The InCodeSystem operator returns true if the given code is in the given code system. The first argument is expected to be a String, Code, or Concept. The second argument is expected to be of type CodeSystem. When this argument is statically a CodeSystemRef, this allows for both static analysis of the code system references within an artifact, as well as the implementation of code system membership by the target environment as a service call to a terminology server, if desired.

    • ELM_ANYINCODESYSTEM

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ANYINCODESYSTEM
      From the ELM specification: The AnyInCodeSystem operator returns true if any of the given codes are in the given code system. The first argument is expected to be a list of String, Code, or Concept. The second argument is expected to be of type CodeSystem. When this argument is statically a CodeSystemRef, this allows for both static analysis of the code system references within an artifact, as well as the implementation of code system membership by the target environment as a service call to a terminology server, if desired.

    • ELM_INVALUESET

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_INVALUESET
      From the ELM specification: The InValueSet operator returns true if the given code is in the given value set. The first argument is expected to be a String, Code, or Concept. The second argument is expected to be of type ValueSet. When this argument is statically a ValueSetRef, this allows for both static analysis of the value set references within an artifact, as well as the implementation of valueset membership by the target environment as a service call to a terminology server, if desired.

    • ELM_ANYINVALUESET

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ANYINVALUESET
      From the ELM specification: The AnyInValueSet operator returns true if any of the given codes are in the given value set. The first argument is expected to be a list of String, Code, or Concept. The second argument is expected to be of type ValueSet. When this argument is statically a ValueSetRef, this allows for both static analysis of the value set references within an artifact, as well as the implementation of valueset membership by the target environment as a service call to a terminology server, if desired.

    • ELM_EXPANDVALUESET

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_EXPANDVALUESET
      From the ELM specification: The ExpandValueSet operator returns the current expansion for the given value set. The operation exoects a single argument of type ValueSet. This may be a static reference to a value set (i.e. a ValueSetRef), or a ValueSet value to support dynamic value set usage. The operation is used as the implicit conversion from a ValueSet reference to a list of codes. If the argument is null, the result is null.

    • ELM_SUBSUMES

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SUBSUMES
      From the ELM specification: The Subsumes operator returns true if the given codes are equivalent, or if the first code subsumes the second (i.e. the first code is an ancestor of the second in a subsumption hierarchy), and false otherwise. For the Concept overload, this operator returns true if any code in the first concept subsumes any code in the second. If either or both arguments are null, the result is null.

    • ELM_SUBSUMEDBY

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SUBSUMEDBY
      From the ELM specification: The SubsumedBy operator returns true if the given codes are equivalent, or if the first code is subsumed by the second code (i.e. the first code is a descendent of the second code in a subsumption hierarchy), and false otherwise. For the Concept overload, this operator returns true if any code in the first concept is subsumed by any code in the second. If either or both arguments are null, the result is null.

    • ELM_QUANTITY

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_QUANTITY
      From the ELM specification: The Quantity type defines a clinical quantity. For example, the quantity 10 days or 30 mmHg. The value is a decimal, while the unit is expected to be a valid UCUM unit or calendar duration keyword, singular or plural.

    • ELM_RATIO

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_RATIO
      From the ELM specification: The Ratio type defines a ratio between two quantities. For example, the titre 1:128, or the concentration ratio 5 mg/10 mL. The numerator and denominator are both quantities.

    • ELM_CALCULATEAGE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CALCULATEAGE
      From the ELM specification: Calculates the age in the specified precision of a person born on the given date. The CalculateAge operator is defined for Date and DateTime. For the Date overload, the calculation is performed using Today(), the precision must be one of year, month, week, or day, and the result is the number of whole calendar periods that have elapsed between the given date and today. For the DateTime overload, the calculation is performed using Now(), and the result is the number of whole calendar periods that have elapsed between the given datetime and now.

    • ELM_CALCULATEAGEAT

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CALCULATEAGEAT
      From the ELM specification: Calculates the age in the specified precision of a person born on a given date, as of another given date. The CalculateAgeAt operator has two signatures: (Date, Date) (DateTime, DateTime) For the Date overload, precision must be one of year, month, week, or day, and the result is the number of whole calendar periods that have elapsed between the first date and the second date. For the DateTime overload, the result is the number of whole calendar periods that have elapsed between the first datetime and the second datetime.

    • ELM_VERSIONEDIDENTIFIER

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_VERSIONEDIDENTIFIER
      From the ELM specification: VersionedIdentifier is composed of three parts: (1) an optional system, or namespace, which provides a globally unique, stable scope for the identifier, (2) an identifier which identifies the set of all versions of a given resource, and (3) the actual version of the instance of interest in this set. The VersionedIdentifier therefore points to an individual 'versioned' instance of a resource such as the third version of a library.

    • ELM_USINGDEF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_USINGDEF
      From the ELM specification: Defines a data model that is available within the artifact.

    • ELM_INCLUDEDEF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_INCLUDEDEF
      From the ELM specification: Includes a library for use within the artifact.

    • ELM_CONTEXTDEF

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_CONTEXTDEF
      From the ELM specification: The ContextDef type defines a context definition statement. Note that this is a placeholder for the context statement within the library. The effect of the context definition is applied by the translator to the definitions that follow.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_USINGS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_USINGS
      From the ELM specification: Set of data models referenced in the Expression objects in this knowledge artifact.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_INCLUDES

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_INCLUDES
      From the ELM specification: Set of libraries referenced by this artifact. Components of referenced libraries may be used within this artifact.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_PARAMETERS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_PARAMETERS
      From the ELM specification: The parameters defined within this library.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_CODESYSTEMS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_CODESYSTEMS
      From the ELM specification: The code systems defined within this library.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_VALUESETS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_VALUESETS
      From the ELM specification: The value sets defined within this library.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_CODES

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_CODES
      From the ELM specification: The codes defined within this library.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_CONCEPTS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_CONCEPTS
      From the ELM specification: The concepts defined within this library.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_CONTEXTS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_CONTEXTS
      From the ELM specification: The contexts defined within this library.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_STATEMENTS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_STATEMENTS
      From the ELM specification: The statements section contains the expression and function definitions for the library.

    • ELM_LIBRARY

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY
      From the ELM specification: A Library is an instance of a CQL-ELM library.

    • ELM_ACCESSMODIFIER

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ACCESSMODIFIER
      From the ELM specification: The AccessModifier type is used to specify the access level for the various definitions within a library such as parameters, expressions, and functions. If no access modifier is specified, public is assumed. Private definitions can only be accessed within the library in which they are defined.

    • ELM_ACCESSMODIFIER_PUBLIC

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ACCESSMODIFIER_PUBLIC
      The AccessModifier value Public of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_ACCESSMODIFIER_PRIVATE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ACCESSMODIFIER_PRIVATE
      The AccessModifier value Private of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION
      From the ELM specification: The DateTimePrecision type specifies the units of precision available for temporal operations such as DurationBetween, SameAs, SameOrBefore, SameOrAfter, and DateTimeComponentFrom.

    • ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_YEAR

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_YEAR
      The DateTimePrecision value Year of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_MONTH

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_MONTH
      The DateTimePrecision value Month of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_WEEK

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_WEEK
      The DateTimePrecision value Week of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_DAY

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_DAY
      The DateTimePrecision value Day of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_HOUR

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_HOUR
      The DateTimePrecision value Hour of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_MINUTE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_MINUTE
      The DateTimePrecision value Minute of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_SECOND

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_SECOND
      The DateTimePrecision value Second of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_MILLISECOND

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DATETIMEPRECISION_MILLISECOND
      The DateTimePrecision value Millisecond of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_SORTDIRECTION

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SORTDIRECTION
      An enumeration of the ELM specification with 4 values; the schema gives no description.

    • ELM_SORTDIRECTION_ASC

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SORTDIRECTION_ASC
      The SortDirection value asc of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_SORTDIRECTION_ASCENDING

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SORTDIRECTION_ASCENDING
      The SortDirection value ascending of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_SORTDIRECTION_DESC

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SORTDIRECTION_DESC
      The SortDirection value desc of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_SORTDIRECTION_DESCENDING

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SORTDIRECTION_DESCENDING
      The SortDirection value descending of the ELM specification.

    • ELM_TREES

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_TREES
      How ELM logic is held in IKE: one tree per definition of a library, ordered lists where order carries meaning, and references as links. The ELM node catalog says what each node may hold; this family says how a library's definitions are recorded as semantics.

    • ELM_FIRST_OPERAND_POSITION

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_FIRST_OPERAND_POSITION
      The first of the two or three operands an ELM operator takes. Where a node kind takes exactly two or three operands, our tree names them first, second, and third in place of the catalog's operand, so that no order is needed to tell them apart.

    • ELM_SECOND_OPERAND_POSITION

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_SECOND_OPERAND_POSITION
      The second of the two or three operands an ELM operator takes, named in place of the catalog's operand where a node kind takes exactly two or three.

    • ELM_THIRD_OPERAND_POSITION

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_THIRD_OPERAND_POSITION
      The third of the three operands an ELM operator takes, named in place of the catalog's operand where a node kind takes exactly three.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_OF_DEFINITIONS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_OF_DEFINITIONS
      A library of definitions, as ELM gives it: the concept a tree semantic is about. One library concept per library id; its CQL versions are versions of its definition semantics, and the version string is data on its identity record.

    • ELM_TREE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_TREE
      A tree whose vertices are ELM nodes: the one field of the ELM tree pattern. A vertex is one ELM node kind; a position that holds a plain value is a property on the vertex; a position that holds a node is an edge, named by an argument vertex between the two whose meaning is the position filled. The tree carries no order.

    • ELM_DEFINITION

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_DEFINITION
      One definition of a library as ELM gives it: a using, an include, a parameter, a code system, a value set, a code, a concept, a context, an expression define, or a function define, or the library's own identity record. Why a tree is recorded.

    • ELM_LIST_ITEMS

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIST_ITEMS
      The items of one ELM list position, in order: the one field of the ELM ordered list pattern. Each item is an ELM tree semantic of its own, about the library, identified by what it contains.

    • ELM_ORDER

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_ORDER
      The order of items where ELM order carries meaning, such as the items of a sort, the items of a case, the elements of a list, or the operands of a function. Why a list is recorded apart from the tree.

    • ELM_REFERENCE

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_REFERENCE
      A thing a definition names: another define, a value set, a code, a code system, a concept, a parameter, a function, or an included library. Why a reference is recorded: so that every name is a link the store can follow and check.

    • ELM_REFERENCE_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_REFERENCE_KIND
      The kind of thing a definition names, as one of the catalog's reference node kinds, such as ELM ValueSetRef or ELM ExpressionRef.

    • ELM_REFERENCED_DEFINITION

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_REFERENCED_DEFINITION
      The definition a name means, as a direct link to that definition's semantic.

    • ELM_NAME_AS_WRITTEN

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_NAME_AS_WRITTEN
      The name exactly as the library writes it.

    • ELM_LIBRARY_NAME_AS_WRITTEN

      public static final IkeConcept ELM_LIBRARY_NAME_AS_WRITTEN
      The library name exactly as written, empty when the thing named is in the same library.

    • UNIFIED_CODE_FOR_UNITS_OF_MEASURE

      public static final IkeConcept UNIFIED_CODE_FOR_UNITS_OF_MEASURE
      The Unified Code for Units of Measure as knowledge: its properties, its units, its prefixes, and the units composed from them, read from the unmodified UCUM file when a knowledge base is assembled, every code, name, symbol, and definition UCUM's own. What hangs here that IKE adds is marked as IKE's: the identities, the patterns, and the dimensions and magnitudes computed from UCUM's definitions.

    • UCUM_PROPERTY

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_PROPERTY
      What a unit measures, in UCUM's word for it: length, mass, time, pressure. Each imported property is a concept under this one, and each unit hangs under its property, so a unit's place says what it measures.

    • UCUM_PREFIX

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_PREFIX
      A multiplier a metric unit may carry, kilo through yocto: a concept for each of UCUM's prefixes, with its code, name, symbol, and factor.

    • UCUM_COMPOSED_UNIT

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_COMPOSED_UNIT
      A unit built by UCUM's grammar from prefixes, units, powers, products, and quotients, such as mg/dL or kg.m/s2, made when it is first met and never listed in advance. It is identified by its canonical content, so one unit spelled two ways is one concept, and the spelling a library used stays on its tree.

    • UCUM_DIALECT

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_DIALECT
      The dialect in which a unit's UCUM name and print symbol are read, so that a unit is found by either, the way a definition is found by its name.

    • UCUM_CODE

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_CODE
      The code UCUM gives a unit or a prefix, case-sensitive, as written: mg, min, mm[Hg].

    • UCUM_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CODE

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_CASE_INSENSITIVE_CODE
      The code UCUM gives for systems that cannot keep case, as written.

    • UCUM_PRINT_SYMBOL

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_PRINT_SYMBOL
      The symbol UCUM prints for a unit or a prefix, as written.

    • UCUM_CLASS

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_CLASS
      The class UCUM files a unit under, as written: si, iso1000, clinical, and the rest.

    • UCUM_METRIC

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_METRIC
      Whether UCUM marks the unit metric, so that it may carry a prefix.

    • UCUM_SPECIAL

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_SPECIAL
      Whether UCUM marks the unit special: defined by a function rather than a factor, like degrees Celsius, so that it does not convert by a ratio.

    • UCUM_ARBITRARY

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_ARBITRARY
      Whether UCUM marks the unit arbitrary: a procedure-defined unit like an international unit, which never converts.

    • UCUM_DEFINITION_VALUE

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_DEFINITION_VALUE
      The number in UCUM's definition of the unit, as written.

    • UCUM_DEFINITION_UNIT

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_DEFINITION_UNIT
      The unit UCUM defines the unit in terms of, as written.

    • UCUM_PREFIX_FACTOR

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_PREFIX_FACTOR
      The multiplier a prefix stands for, as UCUM writes it.

    • UNIT_CANONICAL_CODE

      public static final IkeConcept UNIT_CANONICAL_CODE
      IKE's canonical spelling of a composed unit: its factors in one fixed order, the seed of its identity.

    • UNIT_DIMENSION

      public static final IkeConcept UNIT_DIMENSION
      IKE's reduction of a unit to the base dimensions, so much length, mass, time, charge, temperature, luminous intensity, and angle, computed from UCUM's definitions; two units convert only when their dimensions agree.

    • UNIT_MAGNITUDE

      public static final IkeConcept UNIT_MAGNITUDE
      IKE's reduction of a unit to a magnitude in the base units, computed from UCUM's definitions; two commensurable units convert by the ratio of their magnitudes.

    • UCUM_RECORD

      public static final IkeConcept UCUM_RECORD
      Why a field is recorded: it is what UCUM says, kept verbatim.

    • UNIT_REDUCTION

      public static final IkeConcept UNIT_REDUCTION
      Why a field is recorded: it is what IKE computes from UCUM's definitions, and is IKE's, not UCUM's.

    • DATA_MODEL

      public static final IkeConcept DATA_MODEL
      A data model as the CQL translator describes it in model information: the classes a library can retrieve and walk, each with its elements and their types, the contexts a library can run in, and the conversions to other models. Each model at a version is a concept under this one and its classes hang under it, read from the translator project's unmodified model information files when a knowledge base is assembled; what IKE adds, the resolution of a name to a concept and the marks that write a pattern of IKE's own into model information, is marked as IKE's.

    • MODEL_INFORMATION_RECORD

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_INFORMATION_RECORD
      Why a field is recorded: it is what the model information file says, kept verbatim.

    • MODEL_RESOLUTION

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_RESOLUTION
      Why a field is recorded: it is what IKE resolved the file's text to, a concept, a semantic, or a tree of the catalog's type specifiers, and is IKE's, not the file's.

    • MODEL_GENERATION

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_GENERATION
      Why a field is recorded: it says how a pattern of IKE's own is written into model information, so that a library can be written against IKE's own knowledge.

    • FHIR_DIALECT

      public static final IkeConcept FHIR_DIALECT
      The dialect in which a class's name and label are read as the FHIR model information writes them, so that a class is found by either, the way a unit is found by its name and its symbol.

    • QDM_DIALECT

      public static final IkeConcept QDM_DIALECT
      The dialect in which a class's name and label are read as the QDM model information writes them, so that a class is found by either, the way a unit is found by its name and its symbol.

    • QUICK_DIALECT

      public static final IkeConcept QUICK_DIALECT
      The dialect in which a class's name and label are read as the QUICK model information writes them, so that a class is found by either, the way a unit is found by its name and its symbol.

    • QI_CORE_DIALECT

      public static final IkeConcept QI_CORE_DIALECT
      The dialect in which a class's name and label are read as the QI-Core model information writes them, so that a class is found by either, the way a unit is found by its name and its symbol.

    • US_CORE_DIALECT

      public static final IkeConcept US_CORE_DIALECT
      The dialect in which a class's name and label are read as the US Core model information writes them, so that a class is found by either, the way a unit is found by its name and its symbol.

    • MODEL_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_NAME
      The name the model information gives the model, as written: FHIR, QDM, QUICK.

    • MODEL_VERSION

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_VERSION
      The model's version as written, empty when the file gives none.

    • MODEL_URL

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_URL
      The url the model's types are qualified by in a library, as written.

    • MODEL_TARGET_URL

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_TARGET_URL
      The url of the model a profile model stands on, as written, empty when none.

    • MODEL_TARGET_VERSION

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_TARGET_VERSION
      The version of the model a profile model stands on, as written.

    • MODEL_TARGET_QUALIFIER

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_TARGET_QUALIFIER
      The qualifier the file gives the model's types, as written.

    • MODEL_PATIENT_CLASS

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_PATIENT_CLASS
      The class the file names as the patient, as written.

    • MODEL_PATIENT_CLASS_IDENTIFIER

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_PATIENT_CLASS_IDENTIFIER
      The identifier the file gives the patient class, as written.

    • MODEL_PATIENT_BIRTH_DATE_PROPERTY

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_PATIENT_BIRTH_DATE_PROPERTY
      The element the file names as the patient's birth date, as written.

    • MODEL_DEFAULT_CONTEXT

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_DEFAULT_CONTEXT
      The context a library runs in when it names none, as written.

    • MODEL_CASE_SENSITIVE

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_CASE_SENSITIVE
      Whether the file marks the model's names case sensitive.

    • MODEL_STRICT_RETRIEVE_TYPING

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_STRICT_RETRIEVE_TYPING
      Whether the file marks retrieves as strictly typed.

    • MODEL_SCHEMA_LOCATION

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_SCHEMA_LOCATION
      Where the file says the model's schema is, as written.

    • REQUIRED_MODEL_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept REQUIRED_MODEL_NAME
      The name of a model this model requires, as written.

    • REQUIRED_MODEL_VERSION

      public static final IkeConcept REQUIRED_MODEL_VERSION
      The version of a model this model requires, as written.

    • REQUIRED_MODEL

      public static final IkeConcept REQUIRED_MODEL
      The required model's concept in the store, resolved by IKE.

    • MODEL_CLASS_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_CLASS_KIND
      What kind of type the file declares, as written: a class, a profile, or a simple type.

    • CLASS_NAMESPACE

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_NAMESPACE
      The namespace the file gives the class, as written.

    • CLASS_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_NAME
      The class's name as written, qualified by its model.

    • CLASS_IDENTIFIER

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_IDENTIFIER
      The profile identifier the file gives the class, as written.

    • CLASS_LABEL

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_LABEL
      The label the file gives the class, as written, the name a QDM author writes.

    • CLASS_BASE_TYPE

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_BASE_TYPE
      The class the file says this one extends, as written.

    • CLASS_BASE

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_BASE
      The base class as a concept, resolved by IKE and stated as the parent; the model's own concept when the class has no base or extends a System type, since nothing hangs under the catalog's types.

    • CLASS_RETRIEVABLE

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_RETRIEVABLE
      Whether the file says a library may retrieve the class.

    • CLASS_PRIMARY_CODE_PATH

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_PRIMARY_CODE_PATH
      The element the file names as carrying the class's code, as written.

    • CLASS_PRIMARY_CODE_ELEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_PRIMARY_CODE_ELEMENT
      The element record that path names, resolved by IKE.

    • CLASS_PRIMARY_VALUE_SET_PATH

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_PRIMARY_VALUE_SET_PATH
      The element the file names as carrying the class's value set, as written.

    • CLASS_TARGET

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_TARGET
      The class of another model this class stands on, as written, empty when none.

    • CLASS_TARGET_TYPE

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_TARGET_TYPE
      That class as a concept, resolved by IKE when its model is in the store.

    • CLASS_DESCRIPTION

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_DESCRIPTION
      The short description the file gives the class, as written.

    • CLASS_COMMENT

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_COMMENT
      The comment the file gives the class, as written.

    • CLASS_MODEL

      public static final IkeConcept CLASS_MODEL
      The model the class belongs to, as a concept, resolved by IKE from the file the class came in.

    • UNRESOLVED

      public static final IkeConcept UNRESOLVED
      What a resolution field holds when the file's text resolves to nothing in the store: a class of a model that is not there, a path no element answers, a context the model does not declare.

    • ELEMENT_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_NAME
      The element's name as written.

    • ELEMENT_TYPE

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_TYPE
      The element's type as written, one class, a list, an interval, or a choice.

    • ELEMENT_CLASS

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_CLASS
      The class the type names, as a concept, resolved by IKE when the type names exactly one.

    • ELEMENT_TYPE_SPECIFIER

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_TYPE_SPECIFIER
      The element's type as a tree of the catalog's type specifiers, named, list, interval, and choice, each named type resolved to its class, built by IKE.

    • ELEMENT_MINIMUM

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_MINIMUM
      The least number of values the file allows, as written.

    • ELEMENT_MAXIMUM

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_MAXIMUM
      The most values the file allows, as written.

    • ELEMENT_PROHIBITED

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_PROHIBITED
      Whether the file prohibits the element.

    • ELEMENT_MUST_SUPPORT

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_MUST_SUPPORT
      Whether the file marks the element as one an implementation must support.

    • ELEMENT_ONE_BASED

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_ONE_BASED
      Whether the file marks a list element as counted from one.

    • ELEMENT_TARGET

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_TARGET
      The element of another model this element stands on, as written.

    • ELEMENT_LABEL

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_LABEL
      The label the file gives the element, as written.

    • ELEMENT_DESCRIPTION

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_DESCRIPTION
      The short description the file gives the element, as written.

    • ELEMENT_DEFINITION

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_DEFINITION
      The definition the file gives the element, as written.

    • ELEMENT_COMMENT

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_COMMENT
      The comment the file gives the element, as written.

    • ELEMENT_BINDING_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_BINDING_NAME
      The name of the value set binding the file gives the element, as written.

    • ELEMENT_BINDING_STRENGTH

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_BINDING_STRENGTH
      The binding's strength, as written: required, extensible, preferred, example.

    • ELEMENT_BINDING_VALUE_SET

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_BINDING_VALUE_SET
      The value set the binding names, as written.

    • CONTEXT_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept CONTEXT_NAME
      The context's name as written: Patient, Encounter, Practitioner.

    • CONTEXT_TYPE

      public static final IkeConcept CONTEXT_TYPE
      The class that is the context, as written.

    • CONTEXT_CLASS

      public static final IkeConcept CONTEXT_CLASS
      That class as a concept, resolved by IKE.

    • CONTEXT_KEY_ELEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept CONTEXT_KEY_ELEMENT
      The element that keys the context, as written.

    • CONTEXT_BIRTH_DATE_ELEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept CONTEXT_BIRTH_DATE_ELEMENT
      The element that carries the context's birth date, as written.

    • RELATIONSHIP_CONTEXT_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept RELATIONSHIP_CONTEXT_NAME
      The context a class reaches, as written.

    • RELATIONSHIP_CONTEXT

      public static final IkeConcept RELATIONSHIP_CONTEXT
      That context's record on the model, resolved by IKE.

    • RELATIONSHIP_KEY_ELEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept RELATIONSHIP_KEY_ELEMENT
      The element by which the class reaches the context, as written.

    • RELATIONSHIP_TO_TARGET

      public static final IkeConcept RELATIONSHIP_TO_TARGET
      Whether the file declares the relationship on the target model rather than this one.

    • CONVERSION_FROM_TYPE

      public static final IkeConcept CONVERSION_FROM_TYPE
      The type a conversion converts from, as written.

    • CONVERSION_TO_TYPE

      public static final IkeConcept CONVERSION_TO_TYPE
      The type a conversion converts to, as written.

    • CONVERSION_TARGET_CLASS

      public static final IkeConcept CONVERSION_TARGET_CLASS
      The type converted to, as a concept, resolved by IKE.

    • CONVERSION_FUNCTION

      public static final IkeConcept CONVERSION_FUNCTION
      The function the file names for the conversion, as written.

    • MARK_MODEL_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept MARK_MODEL_NAME
      The name of the model of IKE's own that a pattern is written into.

    • MARK_RETRIEVABLE

      public static final IkeConcept MARK_RETRIEVABLE
      Whether a library may retrieve the pattern's semantics as a class.

    • MARK_CODE_FIELD

      public static final IkeConcept MARK_CODE_FIELD
      The field of the pattern that carries the class's code.

    • NULLARY

      public static final IkeConcept NULLARY
      An operator that takes no operand: a literal, a reference, a retrieve.

    • LIST_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept LIST_KIND
      An operand kind: an ordered collection of values of one kind, kept in the order given and allowing a value to repeat; what a query yields before it is reduced. It is not a set, which has no order and no repeats.

    • TUPLE_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept TUPLE_KIND
      An operand kind: a value of named parts, each a value of a kind of its own, read part by part by name.

    • TEXT_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept TEXT_KIND
      An operand kind: a sequence of characters read as written, compared character by character; what CQL's String is a value of (IKE-Network/ike-issues#1122).

    • WRITTEN_VALUE

      public static final IkeConcept WRITTEN_VALUE
      A value written in the text of a library, a number, a text, a date, a truth value, held under its type and read as its type's relation says: a number as a measure on the dimensionless number, a truth value as a presence, a date as a measure on the calendar.

    • MISSING_VALUE

      public static final IkeConcept MISSING_VALUE
      A value of a kind with no content: an Indeterminate presence, a measure with its measure semantic and no bounds, a reference to no concept, a list that is missing rather than empty. CQL's null, of whatever type it is written with.

    • DEFINITION_REFERENCE

      public static final IkeConcept DEFINITION_REFERENCE
      The use of a definition's value by its name; evaluating it is evaluating the definition, once, for the subject at hand.

    • PARAMETER_REFERENCE

      public static final IkeConcept PARAMETER_REFERENCE
      The use of a value supplied to a library when it is evaluated, or the parameter's default when none is supplied.

    • ALIAS_REFERENCE

      public static final IkeConcept ALIAS_REFERENCE
      The value a query source's alias stands for at the moment it is read: one value of the source per pass.

    • PROPERTY_ACCESS

      public static final IkeConcept PROPERTY_ACCESS
      Reading one part of a value by name: on a statement, the reading the named element stands for; on a tuple, the part of that name.

    • QUERY

      public static final IkeConcept QUERY
      A pass over the values of one or more sources, alias by alias, keeping those a condition admits, correlating them with other sources where asked, and yielding what a return clause names, in order where sorted.

    • QUERY_SOURCE

      public static final IkeConcept QUERY_SOURCE
      One source of a query, a list or a single value, named by the alias the query reads it through.

    • SINGLETON_FROM_LIST

      public static final IkeConcept SINGLETON_FROM_LIST
      The one value of a list that holds one; a missing value for an empty list; a refusal for a list of more than one.

    • FIRST_PRESENT

      public static final IkeConcept FIRST_PRESENT
      The first of its operands that is not a missing value, or a missing value when every operand is.

    • KIND_ASSERTION

      public static final IkeConcept KIND_ASSERTION
      A value taken as being of a kind: the value itself when it is of that kind, the missing value of that kind when it is missing, and otherwise the missing value of that kind, or a refusal where the assertion is strict.

    • KIND_TEST

      public static final IkeConcept KIND_TEST
      Whether a value is of a kind or of one under it: Present or Absent, and Absent for a missing value, which is of no kind. A whole number and a decimal are told apart by the places they were written with.

    • KIND_CONVERSION

      public static final IkeConcept KIND_CONVERSION
      A value re-expressed in another kind where its content carries over: a whole number as a decimal at one place, a date as an instant, a code as a one-code concept, a value as a one-element list, text read into the value it writes, a value written out as text. Text that does not read yields a missing value.

    • CONVERSION_POSSIBLE

      public static final IkeConcept CONVERSION_POSSIBLE
      Whether a conversion has a value: of a value to a kind, or of a measure to a unit. Indeterminate for a missing value.

    • PART_LISTING

      public static final IkeConcept PART_LISTING
      The parts of a value as a list: a tuple's parts, a list's elements.

    • DEEP_PART_LISTING

      public static final IkeConcept DEEP_PART_LISTING
      The parts of a value and the parts of its parts, all the way down, as one list.

    • EVALUATION_MOMENT

      public static final IkeConcept EVALUATION_MOMENT
      The moment an evaluation runs at, fixed once per run: read as a date, as an instant, or as a time of day.

    • WRITTEN_COMPONENT_READING

      public static final IkeConcept WRITTEN_COMPONENT_READING
      One component of a value as written: the year, the month of the year, the day of the month, the hour, the minute, the second, or the millisecond of an instant or a time of day, read in the offset the value was written with, or the offset itself. A component finer than the value was written to is missing.

    • MEASURE_MAGNITUDE

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_MAGNITUDE
      A measure with its sign dropped: the distance from zero on its semantic.

    • MEASURE_ROUNDING

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_ROUNDING
      A number taken to a whole number or to a number of places: up, down, toward zero, or to the nearest with a half taken away from zero.

    • REMAINDER

      public static final IkeConcept REMAINDER
      What remains of a dividend after the whole quotient is taken, with the dividend's sign; missing at a zero divisor.

    • WHOLE_QUOTIENT

      public static final IkeConcept WHOLE_QUOTIENT
      The quotient of two numbers taken toward zero; missing at a zero divisor.

    • MEASURE_EXPONENTIATION

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_EXPONENTIATION
      A base raised to an exponent: exact for a whole exponent, a decimal at eight places otherwise; e is a base like any other.

    • MEASURE_LOGARITHM

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_LOGARITHM
      The exponent that raises a base to a value, at eight places; missing of a non-positive value or at base one.

    • KIND_LIMIT

      public static final IkeConcept KIND_LIMIT
      The greatest or least value a language writes for a kind: a limit of the language's machine words and calendars, not of the measure, which has no width.

    • WRITTEN_PRECISION

      public static final IkeConcept WRITTEN_PRECISION
      How finely a value was written: the places of a decimal, the digits of a date's, an instant's, or a time's resolution.

    • NEIGHBOURING_VALUE

      public static final IkeConcept NEIGHBOURING_VALUE
      The next or the previous value at a kind's step: one for a whole number, the eighth place for a decimal, one unit of the written resolution for a date or a time.

    • WRITTEN_BOUNDARY

      public static final IkeConcept WRITTEN_BOUNDARY
      An end of the span a value leaves unwritten, out to a precision asked: the first or the last value the written value could be.

    • MEASURE_ADJACENCY

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_ADJACENCY
      Whether one extent's end is the neighbour of the other's start at the kind's step, on either side or on a named one; an unknown end leaves it open.

    • MEASURE_ALIGNMENT

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_ALIGNMENT
      Whether two extents share a start, the first ending no later, or share an end, the first starting no earlier.

    • MEASURE_SINGLE_POINT

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_SINGLE_POINT
      The one value of an extent whose ends coincide; missing when the ends are unknown, refused when the extent is wider.

    • STRICT_INCLUSION

      public static final IkeConcept STRICT_INCLUSION
      Inclusion with sameness ruled out: a value within an extent and at neither end, a list holding an element among more than one, a collection within another and not the same.

    • EXTENT_MERGING

      public static final IkeConcept EXTENT_MERGING
      The fewest extents that cover the same points as a list of extents, those that overlap or meet merged, ordered by their starts.

    • EXTENT_PARTITION

      public static final IkeConcept EXTENT_PARTITION
      The unit extents of a step that cover an extent, or their starts as points; nothing for an extent written coarser than the step.

    • COLLECTION_SELECTION

      public static final IkeConcept COLLECTION_SELECTION
      Elements of a list or characters of a text picked by position: the first, the last, the one at a position, or those from one position up to another; missing off either end.

    • REPEAT_REMOVAL

      public static final IkeConcept REPEAT_REMOVAL
      A list with each value once, a missing element the same as a missing element, in the order first seen.

    • LIST_FLATTENING

      public static final IkeConcept LIST_FLATTENING
      A list of lists lifted one level into one list.

    • ELEMENT_POSITION

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_POSITION
      The first position of an element in a list, or minus one when absent.

    • COLLECTION_SIZE

      public static final IkeConcept COLLECTION_SIZE
      The count of a list's elements, missing ones included, or of a text's characters.

    • QUERY_PROJECTION

      public static final IkeConcept QUERY_PROJECTION
      What each kept row of a query yields, distinct unless the clause says all.

    • ORDERING

      public static final IkeConcept ORDERING
      The rows of a query in the order its keys give, missing values first.

    • ORDERING_KEY

      public static final IkeConcept ORDERING_KEY
      One key of an ordering: the rows themselves, a column by its path, or an expression of each row, ascending or descending.

    • QUERY_BINDING

      public static final IkeConcept QUERY_BINDING
      A name bound to a value per row of a query, for the clauses that follow.

    • QUERY_FOLDING

      public static final IkeConcept QUERY_FOLDING
      The rows of a query folded into one value through a named accumulator, from a starting value or missing, over distinct rows when asked.

    • MEASURE_MODE

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_MODE
      The most frequent present value of a list, the least of them when several tie; missing of none.

    • MEASURE_PRODUCT

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_PRODUCT
      The product of a list's present values; missing of none.

    • MEASURE_SPREAD

      public static final IkeConcept MEASURE_SPREAD
      How far a list's present values lie from their mean: the variance or its root, of the sample or of the population, at eight places; missing of none.

    • TEXT_JOINING

      public static final IkeConcept TEXT_JOINING
      Texts joined end to end, or a list's texts joined with a separator; missing when a text is, or the list is empty or missing.

    • TEXT_AFFIX_TEST

      public static final IkeConcept TEXT_AFFIX_TEST
      Whether a text begins or ends with another.

    • TEXT_POSITION

      public static final IkeConcept TEXT_POSITION
      The first or last position of a pattern in a text, or minus one.

    • TEXT_CASE

      public static final IkeConcept TEXT_CASE
      A text in lower or upper case.

    • TEXT_PATTERN_MATCH

      public static final IkeConcept TEXT_PATTERN_MATCH
      Whether the whole of a text matches a regular expression.

    • TEXT_PATTERN_REPLACEMENT

      public static final IkeConcept TEXT_PATTERN_REPLACEMENT
      A text with every match of a regular expression replaced.

    • TEXT_SPLITTING

      public static final IkeConcept TEXT_SPLITTING
      A text divided at a separator into a list of texts, the text whole when none is given or found.

    • TEXT_SLICE

      public static final IkeConcept TEXT_SLICE
      The characters of a text from a position for a length; missing off either end.

    • EVALUATION_MESSAGE

      public static final IkeConcept EVALUATION_MESSAGE
      A note attached to a value's evaluation, the value passed through; a message of error severity whose condition holds refuses the evaluation with its text.

    • CIRCUMSTANCE_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept CIRCUMSTANCE_KIND
      What kind of circumstance a statement holds beside its topic, one of three, as the ANF structural definition gives them: a performance, a request, or a narrative.

    • PERFORMANCE_CIRCUMSTANCE

      public static final IkeConcept PERFORMANCE_CIRCUMSTANCE
      A circumstance kind: what was determined about the topic, a result as a measure, with what became of the act, when, and by what method.

    • REQUEST_CIRCUMSTANCE

      public static final IkeConcept REQUEST_CIRCUMSTANCE
      A circumstance kind: what is sought about the topic, a requested result, with what became of the order, when it is wanted, and how often.

    • NARRATIVE_CIRCUMSTANCE

      public static final IkeConcept NARRATIVE_CIRCUMSTANCE
      A circumstance kind: text about the topic that resists being structured, kept as written.

    • STATEMENT_READING

      public static final IkeConcept STATEMENT_READING
      What a model's element answers when a library reads it off a statement: one of a closed set, the statement's topic, its circumstance kind, its disposition, its timing whole or by an end, its result, its statement time, or a fact of the subject.

    • TOPIC_READING

      public static final IkeConcept TOPIC_READING
      A statement reading: the statement's topic, a concept.

    • CIRCUMSTANCE_KIND_READING

      public static final IkeConcept CIRCUMSTANCE_KIND_READING
      A statement reading: which kind of circumstance the statement holds.

    • DISPOSITION_READING

      public static final IkeConcept DISPOSITION_READING
      A statement reading: what became of the act or the order, a concept.

    • TIMING_READING

      public static final IkeConcept TIMING_READING
      A statement reading: when the circumstance held, a measure on the calendar.

    • TIMING_START_READING

      public static final IkeConcept TIMING_START_READING
      A statement reading: the lower bound of the timing, an instant.

    • TIMING_END_READING

      public static final IkeConcept TIMING_END_READING
      A statement reading: the upper bound of the timing, an instant.

    • RESULT_READING

      public static final IkeConcept RESULT_READING
      A statement reading: the result of a performance, a measure.

    • STATEMENT_TIME_READING

      public static final IkeConcept STATEMENT_TIME_READING
      A statement reading: when the statement was made, an instant.

    • SUBJECT_BIRTH_DATE_READING

      public static final IkeConcept SUBJECT_BIRTH_DATE_READING
      A statement reading of the subject rather than the statement: the subject's birth date, a measure on the calendar.

    • MODEL_BRIDGE

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_BRIDGE
      Why a field is recorded: it says what a model's class or element stands for in IKE's own terms, authored by IKE and checked at admission, so that a library written against the model evaluates over statements.

    • BRIDGE_CIRCUMSTANCE_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept BRIDGE_CIRCUMSTANCE_KIND
      The kind of circumstance a statement must hold to answer a retrieve of the class.

    • BRIDGE_DISPOSITION

      public static final IkeConcept BRIDGE_DISPOSITION
      The disposition a statement must carry to answer a retrieve of the class, or the unresolved marker when the class fixes none.

    • BRIDGE_RELATION_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept BRIDGE_RELATION_KIND
      What the bridge claims: a definitional extension where the class is definable from what a statement says, a conservative extension where the class carries more.

    • ELEMENT_READING

      public static final IkeConcept ELEMENT_READING
      The statement reading a model's element answers.

    • SUBJECT_OF_COMMENTARY

      public static final IkeConcept SUBJECT_OF_COMMENTARY
      The referenced-component role a Comment Pattern semantic's attachment target plays: the subject free-text commentary is about — distinct from Comment, which names the commentary's own content type, not the component being commented on.

    • EDITORIAL_CLARIFICATION

      public static final IkeConcept EDITORIAL_CLARIFICATION
      Why a free-text comment is captured: to explain an authoring decision or provide context a formal field cannot, for a future reviewer or maintainer.

    • TAXONOMY_NAVIGATION_CACHE

      public static final IkeConcept TAXONOMY_NAVIGATION_CACHE
      Why a navigation pattern's referenced component carries an IsA semantic: a pre-computed parent/child structure so traversal doesn't require re-deriving from axioms every time.

    • CHRONICLE_IDENTITY_AND_HISTORY

      public static final IkeConcept CHRONICLE_IDENTITY_AND_HISTORY
      Why a chronicle-shape pattern's referenced component carries this semantic: to record that component's own identity (public id) alongside its complete version history.

    • PATTERN_MEMBERSHIP

      public static final IkeConcept PATTERN_MEMBERSHIP
      Why a Semantic Chronology Pattern's Semantic pattern field is recorded: to identify which pattern this semantic is an instance of.

    • ATTACHMENT_TARGET

      public static final IkeConcept ATTACHMENT_TARGET
      Why a Semantic Chronology Pattern's Semantic referenced component field is recorded: to identify what component this semantic is attached to.

    • VERSION_HISTORY

      public static final IkeConcept VERSION_HISTORY
      Why a Semantic Chronology Pattern's Semantic versions set is recorded: to hold every version of this semantic, in order — the semantic-level counterpart to the versions-field/set pair every other chronicle-shape pattern already names distinctly.

    • VERSION_SNAPSHOT

      public static final IkeConcept VERSION_SNAPSHOT
      Why a version-shape pattern's referenced component carries this semantic: to record one point-in-time state of a chronicle — the STAMP it was committed with, plus whatever field values were true then.

    • VERSION_PROVENANCE

      public static final IkeConcept VERSION_PROVENANCE
      Why a version-shape pattern's own STAMP field is recorded: to say who committed this version, in what state, module, path, and when.

    • MEANING_DECLARATION

      public static final IkeConcept MEANING_DECLARATION
      Why a Pattern Version Pattern's Pattern meaning field is recorded: to hold this pattern-version's own declared meaning concept.

    • PURPOSE_DECLARATION

      public static final IkeConcept PURPOSE_DECLARATION
      Why a Pattern Version Pattern's Pattern purpose field is recorded: to hold this pattern-version's own declared purpose concept.

    • MODULE_LINEAGE

      public static final IkeConcept MODULE_LINEAGE
      Why a module's own origin record is captured: to track which modules a given module originated from.

    • ORIGINATED_MODULE

      public static final IkeConcept ORIGINATED_MODULE
      What a Module origins pattern semantic's referenced component is: the module whose origins are declared — the module that originated from the modules the semantic names, distinct from Module origins, which names the origin-set value itself.

    • ORIGIN_MODULE_SET

      public static final IkeConcept ORIGIN_MODULE_SET
      Why a module's origin set value is recorded: to name the modules this module originated from.

    • PATH_LINEAGE

      public static final IkeConcept PATH_LINEAGE
      Why a path's own origin record is captured: to track which path it branched from, and when.

    • ORIGINATED_PATH

      public static final IkeConcept ORIGINATED_PATH
      What a Path origins pattern semantic's referenced component is: the path whose branch point is declared — the path that originated from the path the semantic names, distinct from Path origins, which names the origin-record value itself.

    • BRANCH_SOURCE

      public static final IkeConcept BRANCH_SOURCE
      Why the origin path value is recorded: to say which path this path branched from. The record's subject is the referenced component — the originated path — never this field.

    • BRANCH_POINT

      public static final IkeConcept BRANCH_POINT
      Why the origin instant is recorded: to fix the moment this path branched from its origin — the point up to which the origin path's versions are visible from this path.

    • TIME

      public static final IkeConcept TIME
      A point in time, as a general concept — the meaning counterpart to Status value/Author/Module/Path: what kind of value a STAMP's time field holds, distinct from TimeForVersion, which names why it is recorded. The time dimension of the STAMP — part of the STAMP model, stated logically as a Part of restriction.

    • DESCRIPTION_ATTACHMENT

      public static final IkeConcept DESCRIPTION_ATTACHMENT
      Why a Description Pattern semantic exists: to attach a human-readable name or definition to a concept.

    • CASE_SENSITIVITY_RULE

      public static final IkeConcept CASE_SENSITIVITY_RULE
      Why a description's case significance value is recorded: to say whether the description's text is case-sensitive.

    • DESCRIPTION_ROLE

      public static final IkeConcept DESCRIPTION_ROLE
      Why a description's type value is recorded: to say which of the three description roles — fully qualified name, regular name, or definition — this description plays.

    • EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_MAPPING

      public static final IkeConcept EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_MAPPING
      Why an Identifier Pattern semantic exists: to record an alternate identifier a component carries in an external terminology's own identifier scheme.

    • IDENTIFIER_AUTHORITY

      public static final IkeConcept IDENTIFIER_AUTHORITY
      Why an identifier source value is recorded: to say which identifier-issuing authority the identifier came from.

    • IDENTIFIER_TEXT

      public static final IkeConcept IDENTIFIER_TEXT
      Why an identifier value is recorded: to hold the identifier's own literal text, once a source has been chosen.

    • IDENTIFIED_COMPONENT

      public static final IkeConcept IDENTIFIED_COMPONENT
      What an Identifier Pattern semantic's referenced component is: the component an external identifier names — the carrier of an alternate identity in another identifier scheme, distinct from Identifier source, which names the field value saying where that identifier came from (IKE-Network/ike-issues#891).

    • AXIOMATIZED_COMPONENT

      public static final IkeConcept AXIOMATIZED_COMPONENT
      What an OWL Axiom Syntax Pattern semantic's referenced component is: the component whose definitional axioms the semantic expresses — distinct from Axiom syntax, which names the syntax text the field holds.

    • AXIOM_EXPRESSION

      public static final IkeConcept AXIOM_EXPRESSION
      Why an OWL Axiom Syntax Pattern semantic exists: to express a component's definitional axioms as OWL functional-syntax text.

    • NUMERIC_VALUE_RESTRICTION

      public static final IkeConcept NUMERIC_VALUE_RESTRICTION
      Why a Value Constraint Pattern semantic exists: to restrict which literal values are legal for a component — the numeric-domain counterpart to Field Value Restriction.

    • REFERENCE_RANGE_AUTHORITY

      public static final IkeConcept REFERENCE_RANGE_AUTHORITY
      Why a value constraint's source value is recorded: to name the organization that specifies the constraint.

    • UNIT_EXAMPLE

      public static final IkeConcept UNIT_EXAMPLE
      Why example UCUM units are recorded on a value constraint: to show a representative unit of measure for the constrained value, for a reader's reference.

    • SET_MEMBERSHIP

      public static final IkeConcept SET_MEMBERSHIP
      A component's role as an element of a pattern's own set of semantics — the modern replacement for the deprecated SOLOR term Membership semantic.

    • LEGACY

      public static final IkeConcept LEGACY
      A visible deprecation signal, not a functional restriction: content reparented here is dormant or superseded and a candidate for removal in a near-future revision. Being under Legacy says nothing about whether the content is still resolvable or referenced elsewhere -- it may well be -- only that it is no longer this project's preferred terminology going forward.

    • GRAPH

      public static final IkeConcept GRAPH
      A structure of vertices connected by edges — the root of the structure family this model stores knowledge in. Its kinds specialize by edge discipline: Tree (connected, acyclic), Directed graph (every edge has a direction), and Directed tree (both at once). A concept whose values merely have this shape — a data type, a default — is about a graph, not a kind of graph, and lives with its own family.

    • TREE

      public static final IkeConcept TREE
      A connected, acyclic graph: between any two vertices there is exactly one path. A kind of Graph. When its edges also carry direction from a single root, it is a Directed tree — which is therefore a kind of Tree and a kind of Directed graph at once.

    • DIRECTED_TREE

      public static final IkeConcept DIRECTED_TREE
      A rooted tree whose every edge is directed away from (or toward) the root: a kind of Directed graph and a kind of Tree at once — the multi-parent placement that makes a classified taxonomy a DAG rather than a tree. This is the shape of each stored logical expression (see EL++ ditree) and of the value a DiTree data type field carries.

    • EL_DITREE

      public static final IkeConcept EL_DITREE
      The directed tree carrying one concept's EL++ axiom expression — the stored form of a single stated or inferred definition, with sets and atoms as vertices under one definition root. The axiom form, per concept; distinct from EL++ digraph, the classification result over a full set of EL++ axioms, which is a DAG because concepts may classify under more than one parent.

    • VIEW_COORDINATE_MODEL

      public static final IkeConcept VIEW_COORDINATE_MODEL
      The model family for the coordinates composing a view of the knowledge graph: a view coordinate is composed of a stamp coordinate (which versions are visible), language coordinates (which descriptions to prefer), a logic coordinate (how to reason), a navigation coordinate (how to traverse), and an edit coordinate (where changes are written).
