Each per-coordinate properties family placed here is part of this model — stated logically as a transitive Part of restriction, in the part-to-whole direction EL++ supports.

    • STAMP_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES

      public static final IkeConcept STAMP_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES
      The dimensions of the stamp coordinate — the version filter of a view: allowed states, the module preference list, order, and exclusion set, the author set, and the position on path that together select which versions are visible. A model concept grouping those dimensions, and part of the view coordinate model — stated logically as a Part of restriction.

    • EDIT_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES

      public static final IkeConcept EDIT_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES
      The dimensions of the edit coordinate — where a view writes: the author, the default and destination modules, the module and path options offered, and the promotion path that together govern how new versions are stamped. A model concept grouping those dimensions, and part of the view coordinate model — stated logically as a Part of restriction.

    • NAVIGATION_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES

      public static final IkeConcept NAVIGATION_COORDINATE_PROPERTIES
      The dimensions of the navigation coordinate — how a view traverses parent/child structure: the navigation concept set naming which navigation patterns to read, the vertex state set filtering which states a vertex may be in, and the vertex sort ordering siblings. A model concept grouping those dimensions, and part of the view coordinate model — stated logically as a Part of restriction. The navigation coordinate is a coordinate-model notion; the directed graph it walks is a structure kind under Graph — the two concepts the baseline fused into one entry (IKE-Network/ike-issues#950).

    • STAMP

      public static final IkeConcept STAMP
      The versioning tuple every component version carries: Status, Time, Author, Module, and Path — the five dimensions that place a version in the knowledge space and that every coordinate filters by. Each dimension family is part of this model concept — stated logically as a transitive Part of restriction — mirroring the stamp record's composition in code.

    • ANNOTATION_MODEL

      public static final IkeConcept ANNOTATION_MODEL
      The apparatus that records what a person says about content without touching it: the annotation, its kinds, the pattern that carries it, and the module annotations are written to.

    • ANNOTATION

      public static final IkeConcept ANNOTATION
      A statement about one version of a component — an affirmation, a refutation, or a comment — recorded beside it, so the content keeps its own authorship and the annotator's stance carries theirs.

    • ANNOTATION_KIND

      public static final IkeConcept ANNOTATION_KIND
      What an annotation says about the content it references. The kinds form a controlled hierarchy; a new kind is a new concept, never a new keyword.

    • UNCATEGORIZED_COMMENT

      public static final IkeConcept UNCATEGORIZED_COMMENT
      Free commentary with no stance on the content: the default kind, and how a Comment pattern semantic reads.

    • JUDGMENT

      public static final IkeConcept JUDGMENT
      A stance on the referenced version. A later judgment by the same annotator on the same content supersedes an earlier one.

    • AFFIRMATION

      public static final IkeConcept AFFIRMATION
      The annotator has reviewed the version and stands behind it. An affirmation is the person's own act; nothing records one on their behalf. In git it is an Annotation: trailer on an empty commit, preferably signed.

    • REFUTATION

      public static final IkeConcept REFUTATION
      The annotator has reviewed the version and disputes it, with the reason as the annotation text. A refutation is an opinion, not a retirement: inactivating the content is a separate edit by whoever is accountable for it.

    • REVIEWED_PROVENANCE

      public static final IkeConcept REVIEWED_PROVENANCE
      Recording who reviewed which version of what, and their stance: the purpose of the Annotation pattern and its fields.

    • REVIEWED_VERSION

      public static final IkeConcept REVIEWED_VERSION
      The STAMP of the version the annotator saw; with the referenced component it names one exact, immutable version. When the referenced component is itself a STAMP, that STAMP. An annotation whose reviewed version is no longer the latest is about a superseded version.

    • ANNOTATED_ELEMENTS

      public static final IkeConcept ANNOTATED_ELEMENTS
      The elements within the referenced component an annotation covers, in order — a document's lines — or none, for the whole component.

    • REVIEW_MODULE

      public static final IkeConcept REVIEW_MODULE
      The module annotations made in a knowledge base are written to, so a module coordinate decides whether review metadata travels with a release. Annotations materialized from git stamp under the repository's own module.

    • ACTION_MODEL

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_MODEL
      The apparatus that describes what a person or the assistant can do in Komet: the kinds of action, the patterns their inputs and results take, and the definition that ties an action to them.

    • ACTION_DEFINITION

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_DEFINITION
      The definition of one kind of action: the patterns its input and result take and how a model should perform it.

    • ACTION_PERFORMANCE

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_PERFORMANCE
      Performing a kind of action the same way wherever it is offered — a menu, the assistant, the headless runner: the purpose of the Action definition pattern and its fields.

    • INPUT_PATTERN

      public static final IkeConcept INPUT_PATTERN
      The pattern each run's input takes. Its fields are what the action needs besides its subject; a menu gathers them from the person, the assistant fills them as a tool's arguments, and both face the same allowed values.

    • RESULT_PATTERN

      public static final IkeConcept RESULT_PATTERN
      The pattern each run's result takes: what the action produced, and whether it completed.

    • MODEL_INSTRUCTIONS

      public static final IkeConcept MODEL_INSTRUCTIONS
      What a model must know when it performs the action, beyond the action's definition: what to check first, what never to do, how to report.

    • ACTION_RECORD

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_RECORD
      Recording what was done, to what, by whom and with what outcome, so a run can be audited, replayed or forked: the purpose of the input and result patterns and their fields.

    • ACTION_INPUT

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_INPUT
      One run of an action, as asked for: a semantic of the action's input pattern whose referenced component is the action's subject — a component, a document or journal block, or a node in a logical definition. Its STAMP records who ran it and when; replaying the run performs the action again on this input.

    • PERFORMED_ACTION

      public static final IkeConcept PERFORMED_ACTION
      The kind of action a run performed: a concept beneath Komet action.

    • REPLACEMENT_TEXT

      public static final IkeConcept REPLACEMENT_TEXT
      The text a run puts in place of its subject's: for a document block, the block's new lines, one per line.

    • ACTION_RESULT

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_RESULT
      What one run of an action produced: a semantic of the action's result pattern whose referenced component is the run's input.

    • ACTION_OUTCOME

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_OUTCOME
      Whether a run of an action did what it was asked. A failure is an outcome, reported in the result, never an error raised past it.

    • ACTION_COMPLETED

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_COMPLETED
      The run did what it was asked, and its result says what it wrote or found.

    • ACTION_REFUSED

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_REFUSED
      The run did not start, because its subject or inputs did not allow it — a component already inactive, a value outside the allowed ones. Nothing was written.

    • ACTION_FAILED

      public static final IkeConcept ACTION_FAILED
      The run started and could not finish. Nothing it began was committed.

    • WRITTEN_VERSION

      public static final IkeConcept WRITTEN_VERSION
      The STAMP of the version a run wrote; with the run's subject it names that version.

    • OUTCOME_MESSAGE

      public static final IkeConcept OUTCOME_MESSAGE
      Text for the person or the model about the outcome: why the run was refused or failed, or what to look at next. Empty when there is nothing to add.

    • KOMET_ACTION

      public static final IkeConcept KOMET_ACTION
      Something a person or the assistant does to the knowledge base through Komet, with a defined input and result: offered in a menu by the rules that decide when it makes sense, and offered to the assistant as a tool under the same rules.

    • READ_ACTION

      public static final IkeConcept READ_ACTION
      An action that reports on the knowledge base and changes nothing in it.

    • CHANGE_ACTION

      public static final IkeConcept CHANGE_ACTION
      An action that writes: a new component, or a new version of one. What it writes lands under the edit coordinate, and is uncommitted until the person commits it.

    • CHECK_ACTION

      public static final IkeConcept CHECK_ACTION
      An action that judges content against a rule or a method and reports findings, writing nothing but its result.

    • NAVIGATE_ACTION

      public static final IkeConcept NAVIGATE_ACTION
      An action that changes what a person sees — focus, window, layout — and nothing in the knowledge base.

    • ACTIVATE_COMPONENT

      public static final IkeConcept ACTIVATE_COMPONENT
      Makes an inactive component active again: writes a new version of the subject with state active and every field as the latest version has it. Earlier versions, including the inactive one, remain.

    • INACTIVATE_COMPONENT

      public static final IkeConcept INACTIVATE_COMPONENT
      Retires a component: writes a new version of the subject with state inactive and every field as the latest version has it. Nothing is deleted; earlier versions remain, and the component can be activated again.

    • EDIT_DOCUMENT_BLOCK

      public static final IkeConcept EDIT_DOCUMENT_BLOCK
      Replaces the text of one block of a document materialized from git, a block whose members are lines: an unchanged line keeps its element, a changed line gets a new version of it, a new line gets a provisional element until a commit gives it an identity, and a removed line leaves the block. The edit lands as uncommitted versions in the document's one pending edit, and the person's git commit of the file settles it.

    • KNOWLEDGE_BASE_PROVENANCE_MODEL

      public static final IkeConcept KNOWLEDGE_BASE_PROVENANCE_MODEL
      The apparatus a knowledge base uses to record what it is made of: the source releases imported into it and the assembly that composed them.

    • KNOWLEDGE_BASE_PROVENANCE

      public static final IkeConcept KNOWLEDGE_BASE_PROVENANCE
      Recording what a knowledge base is made of, inside the knowledge base, so a store can say which releases it holds and how it was assembled: the purpose of the source release and composition patterns and their fields.

    • SOURCE_RELEASE

      public static final IkeConcept SOURCE_RELEASE
      One release of a knowledge source as imported into a knowledge base: its name and date, the artifact it came from, the importer, and what the import wrote. Recorded once per importer under a stamp of the source's own, so the record travels with the source's content; a later release is a new version of the same record.

    • RELEASE_NAME

      public static final IkeConcept RELEASE_NAME
      The source's own name for the release, as its importer reports it: an edition, a version, a release date.

    • RELEASE_DATE

      public static final IkeConcept RELEASE_DATE
      When the release took effect in the knowledge base: the latest time among the stamps its import wrote.

    • RELEASE_ARTIFACT

      public static final IkeConcept RELEASE_ARTIFACT
      The artifact the release was imported from: its Maven coordinate when it was resolved from a repository, otherwise its file name.

    • ORIGIN_CHECKSUM

      public static final IkeConcept ORIGIN_CHECKSUM
      The SHA-256 of the artifact as imported, written sha256:; for a directory, of its files in path order, each relative path followed by its content.

    • IMPORTER

      public static final IkeConcept IMPORTER
      The importer that read the release, with its version: the implementation version of its jar, otherwise the jar's file name.

    • MODULES_WRITTEN

      public static final IkeConcept MODULES_WRITTEN

    • LICENSE

      public static final IkeConcept LICENSE
      The model family for content licenses — the terms a knowledge artifact is published and consumed under. This set is dual-licensed: Creative Commons Attribution for the knowledge content, Apache 2.0 alongside it, declared in every POM of the reactor and carried here as concepts (IKE-Network/ike-issues#952).

    • APACHE_2_0_LICENSE

      public static final IkeConcept APACHE_2_0_LICENSE
      The Apache License, Version 2.0: a permissive license permitting use, modification, and distribution with attribution and license notice. One of the two licenses this knowledge set is published under — Apache 2.0 together with Creative Commons BY (dual licensing, IKE-Network/ike-issues#952).

    • DEFAULTS_AND_TEMPLATES_MODEL

      public static final IkeConcept DEFAULTS_AND_TEMPLATES_MODEL
      The model family for the defaults, templates, and constraints capabilities: the attachment points a pattern's default and template semantics reference, the per-data-type default field concepts, and the field-constraint apparatus (taxonomy and value-set constraints, value restrictions, match rules). Terminology about these capabilities lives here, in the foundation module; the instance content it describes is packaged separately in the Defaults and templates module.

    • DEFAULT_VALUE_CONCEPT

      public static final IkeConcept DEFAULT_VALUE_CONCEPT
      The attachment point for default values: a default value semantic of a pattern is a complete semantic of that pattern whose referenced component is this concept and whose fields carry the default values an editor offers for that pattern's fields. Attachment here is a support declaration only — never a domain assertion about this concept or any other component — and this concept never joins a domain member set.

    • TEMPLATE_CONCEPT

      public static final IkeConcept TEMPLATE_CONCEPT
      Parent of the per-purpose template attachment concepts: each child is minted for one template purpose, and a template semantic of a pattern for that purpose is a complete semantic of that pattern whose referenced component is that child — starting content offered when authoring new components. As with a default value semantic, attachment there is a support declaration, never a domain assertion, and no child joins a domain member set.

    • DEFAULTS_AND_TEMPLATES_MODULE

      public static final IkeConcept DEFAULTS_AND_TEMPLATES_MODULE
      The module scoping every default value and template semantic. The boundary is bidirectional and live-and-die: every version of a defaults or template chronology lives in this module, and this module holds only defaults and template content — a violation in either direction is an error to be withdrawn, never adopted as precedent. As the export dimension, module crossed with path selects a user's preferences for exchange: include this module to carry defaults and templates alongside domain content, exclude it to leave them behind.

    • STRING_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept STRING_DEFAULT
      The String field's loud default: the literal "UNINITIALIZED" — a value that works as an initial value but reads as obviously needing revision, never Java's silent empty string.

    • COMPONENT_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept COMPONENT_DEFAULT
      The Component field's loud default: Uninitialized Component (SOLOR), the base set's own loud placeholder for a component not yet chosen. Not Blank Concept — Blank means a deliberate not-applicable, while Uninitialized means a value still owed.

    • COMPONENTIDSET_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept COMPONENTIDSET_DEFAULT
      The ComponentIdSet field's loud default: the singleton set holding Uninitialized Component — present and non-empty (an empty set would be a silent zero-value), its one member itself the loud placeholder.

    • COMPONENTIDLIST_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept COMPONENTIDLIST_DEFAULT
      The ComponentIdList field's loud default: the singleton list holding Uninitialized Component — present and non-empty (an empty list would be a silent zero-value), its one entry itself the loud placeholder.

    • DITREE_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept DITREE_DEFAULT
      The DiTree field's loud default: a single-vertex tree whose vertex meaning is Uninitialized Component — the smallest well-formed tree, carrying the loud placeholder at its root.

    • DIGRAPH_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept DIGRAPH_DEFAULT
      The DiGraph field's loud default: a simple cycle — two vertices, both Uninitialized Component, with edges in both directions. The cycle is deliberate: a cycle can never be a tree, so the value proves the field truly holds a graph and not a tree.

    • CONCEPT_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept CONCEPT_DEFAULT
      The Concept field's loud default: Uninitialized Component (SOLOR) — the loud placeholder for a concept not yet chosen, obviously needing revision wherever it appears.

    • SEMANTIC_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept SEMANTIC_DEFAULT
      The Semantic field's loud default: the fully qualified name description semantic of Uninitialized Component — a real, resolvable semantic whose subject is itself the loud placeholder, so the reference is valid yet plainly unrevised.

    • INTEGER_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept INTEGER_DEFAULT
      The Integer field's loud default: the stretched-sevens sentinel 777777777 (nine sevens) — a repdigit signature that reads as deliberately planted and cannot plausibly occur as natural data, where Integer.MIN_VALUE would read as an overflow bug. Never Java's silent zero.

    • FLOAT_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept FLOAT_DEFAULT
      The Float field's loud default: NaN, the type's native non-value — chosen over a stretched-sevens sentinel because a true non-value is louder still: it cannot be mistaken for data at all, and it propagates through arithmetic, so any computation over an unrevised default stays loudly not-a-number.

    • BOOLEAN_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept BOOLEAN_DEFAULT
      The Boolean field's default: false — a flagged compromise. A two-valued type has no loud member, so no Boolean default can announce itself as unrevised; false is offered as the initial value with that limitation stated rather than hidden.

    • BYTEARRAY_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept BYTEARRAY_DEFAULT
      The ByteArray field's loud default: the UTF-8 bytes of "UNINITIALIZED" — the loud String default carried in byte form, never a silent empty array.

    • ARRAY_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept ARRAY_DEFAULT
      The Array field's loud default: an array of exactly one element, the String "UNINITIALIZED" — present and non-empty (an empty array would be a silent zero-value), its single element the loud String default.

    • INSTANT_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept INSTANT_DEFAULT
      The Instant field's loud default: the premundane instant, the time type's native non-value — the platform's own before-all-recorded-time marker, chosen over a sentinel date because a true non-value cannot be mistaken for a real timestamp.

    • LONG_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept LONG_DEFAULT
      The Long field's loud default: the stretched-sevens sentinel 777777777777777777 (eighteen sevens) — a repdigit signature that reads as deliberately planted and cannot plausibly occur as natural data, where Long.MIN_VALUE would read as an overflow bug (and sits one away from the platform's premundane time sentinel). Never Java's silent zero.

    • DECIMAL_DEFAULT

      public static final IkeConcept DECIMAL_DEFAULT
      The Decimal field's loud default: the stretched-sevens sentinel 777777777.777 — nine sevens, a decimal point, three more sevens. The decimal point placement deliberately demonstrates the type's distinguishing property (a scaled decimal, not an integer) — the same move as the DiGraph cycle proving graph-ness. Never Java's silent zero.

    • DATA_TYPE_DEFAULT_EXEMPLAR

      public static final IkeConcept DATA_TYPE_DEFAULT_EXEMPLAR
      Why every Data Type Defaults Pattern field value is recorded: to carry its data type's loud default — a value that works as an initial value but reads as obviously needing revision, never Java's silent zero-value. One purpose serves all sixteen fields because every field exists for this identical reason; distinct purposes would be manufactured variety.

    • DEFAULTED_DATA_TYPES

      public static final IkeConcept DEFAULTED_DATA_TYPES
      What a Data Type Defaults Pattern semantic means: the sixteen data types ConceptToDataType recognizes for pattern fields, each exemplified by one field carrying that type's loud default.

    • DATA_TYPE_DEFAULT_PROVISION

      public static final IkeConcept DATA_TYPE_DEFAULT_PROVISION
      Why a Data Type Defaults Pattern semantic exists: to provide, in one semantic, a loud default value for every data type a pattern field can declare — and, replayed, to exercise every field serialization path the store supports end to end.
